2026-11-01-01.headline: Nasdaq ends October down 5.3% after an AI-stock sell-off, with Intel down 29% and chip stocks down more than 8% on Friday
numbers: Nasdaq Composite: -2.9% on Friday, -5.3% in October
Alphabet: -12% on Thursday, worst day on record
Semiconductor ETF: more than -8% on Friday
2026-11-01-01.soWhat: Investors have paid high prices for companies expected to profit from artificial intelligence, so a weak outlook or a spending warning from one large company now moves the whole group. The cost of building data centers is rising faster than the revenue it brings in for some firms, and that is what the market is now questioning. Chip designers, equipment makers and cloud providers lose the most when that doubt spreads, while defensive sectors such as health care and consumer staples gain as investors rotate. The open question is whether the coming Apple and AMD reports show spending turning into sales.

sources.title: Yahoo Finance: Markets News, Oct. 30, 2026
CNBC: Stock market outlook for Nov. 2-6, 2026

2026-11-01-01.summary: US stocks fell sharply on Friday, October 30. The S&P 500 closed at 7,580.07, down 1.82%, the Nasdaq Composite fell about 2.9% to 25,437, and the Dow lost about 1.1%. The Nasdaq dropped 5.3% for October, its worst month since March 2025, while the Dow gained 1.7%. Intel fell about 29% after a weak fourth-quarter forecast, Alphabet had already fallen 12% on Thursday, its worst one-day drop on record, and Amazon's revenue and free cash flow disappointed. A semiconductor ETF lost more than 8% on the day, and money moved toward health care and consumer staples.

2026-11-01-02.headline: Thrive Holdings agrees to take home-security company ADT private in a deal valued at $15.3 billion including debt
numbers: Price: $10.00 per share in cash (45.6% premium)
2026-11-01-02.soWhat: ADT earns recurring fees for monitoring homes and small businesses, which gives it steady cash that can support a lot of debt. The gap between the $7.6 billion equity value and the $15.3 billion total value shows how much of the price is borrowing the buyer takes on, roughly $7.7 billion. Thrive says it buys established companies and upgrades them with technology, so the logic is to cut costs and add services to a customer base that already pays every month. Rivals such as cable companies, Amazon's Ring and Google Nest compete for the same homes. The open question is whether a higher bid appears during the go-shop period.

sources.title: ADT press release (SEC 8-K)

2026-11-01-02.summary: Thrive Holdings, a permanent-capital holding company, agreed to buy ADT for $10.00 per share in cash, a 45.6% premium to the $6.87 closing price on October 27. The price values ADT's equity at about $7.6 billion and the whole company, including debt, at $15.3 billion. Funds managed by Apollo Global Management are the only source of financing, and there is no financing condition. ADT may seek rival offers until November 28 under a go-shop clause, and closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027 after a shareholder vote and US antitrust clearance. ADT will become the base of Thrive's smart-home security business.

2026-11-01-03.headline: AstraZeneca's cancer sales grow 18% and lift nine-month revenue to $46.9 billion, while older heart and diabetes drugs shrink
2026-11-01-03.soWhat: A drugmaker's growth depends on new patented products replacing older ones whose protection ends, and AstraZeneca shows both sides at once: cancer drugs growing at double digits while older medicines fall. The Summit stake and the cost program show how large drug companies buy outside science and trim overhead to protect profit as that handoff happens. China's volume-based buying is a reminder that government purchasing can cut prices on mature drugs. The pipeline had four trial setbacks this year, so the open question is how many of the 12 positive late-stage results turn into approved products.

sources.title: AstraZeneca 9M and Q3 2026 results (SEC 6-K)

2026-11-01-03.summary: AstraZeneca reported nine-month revenue of $46.9 billion, up 8%, and third-quarter revenue of $16.2 billion, up 7%. Oncology sales rose 18% to $21.9 billion and now make up 47% of revenue, while the BioPharmaceuticals unit fell 2% because Farxiga and Brilinta lost patent exclusivity and China began volume-based buying. Rare disease grew 12%. The company kept its 2026 outlook for revenue to grow by a mid-to-high single-digit percentage and core earnings per share by a low double-digit percentage. It also announced a $2 billion investment in Summit Therapeutics for about 12% of its shares and a cost program targeting $1.5 billion of yearly savings.

2026-11-01-04.headline: Wall Street enters a week of midterm elections, Apple earnings and a jobs report with profits up about 30% but unusually thin beats
2026-11-01-04.soWhat: Strong growth with small beats means expectations were already high, so stocks need a stronger outlook, not just good results, to rise. A weak jobs number could ease pressure for a rate hike, but strong inflation keeps that debate open after the Fed's 10-2 vote this week. The election matters for specific industries: analysts say a Democratic sweep could mean slower defense spending, more pressure on drug prices and new rules for data centers. Most investors expect little market impact, so the open question is whether the AI spending doubts of the past week matter more than politics.

sources.title: CNBC: Stock market outlook for Nov. 2-6, 2026

2026-11-01-04.summary: Corporate profits are strong going into the week of November 2. FactSet projects S&P 500 earnings growth of about 30% for the third quarter, but companies are beating estimates by only 1.4% on average, against 7.5% over five years, with Meta and Alphabet pulling the figure down. 138 S&P 500 companies report this week, including Apple and Palantir on Monday. The October jobs report is due Friday: analysts expect 55,000 new jobs and unemployment at 4.2%, after September added just 29,000. Midterm elections are on Tuesday, and polls show Democrats have a chance at both the House and Senate.

2026-11-01-05.headline: Burger King's US sales jump 8.4% while Popeyes slips 1.8%, leaving Restaurant Brands' growth uneven
2026-11-01-05.soWhat: Restaurant Brands mostly franchises its restaurants and collects royalties on franchisee sales, so a rise in comparable sales flows into its revenue with little added cost. That is why Burger King's turnaround matters more than any single quarter's net income, which was boosted by a one-time tax item. Popeyes' decline shows how one brand can offset gains elsewhere in a multi-brand portfolio. The company still carries debt at 4.0 times earnings, so continued sales growth is what lets it keep paying dividends and reducing leverage.

sources.title: Restaurant Brands International Q3 2026 results (SEC 8-K)

2026-11-01-05.summary: Restaurant Brands International reported third-quarter global comparable sales up 3.8% and system-wide sales of $13.0 billion. Burger King US comparable sales rose 8.4%, Tim Hortons rose 1.5% (Canada 1.8%), international rose 3.9% and Popeyes fell 1.8% (US 2.2%). Adjusted operating income rose to $737 million, up 6.7% on an organic basis, and net leverage fell to 4.0 times from 4.4 times. Reported net income jumped to $704 million, helped mainly by a $133 million tax benefit, and the company kept its 2026 targets, including 8% organic operating income growth.

2026-11-02-01.headline: Marvell Technology agrees to buy optical-components maker Lumentum in an all-stock deal valued at $115 billion
2026-11-02-01.soWhat: AI data centers are running into a bandwidth wall, so moving data with light (optical links) is becoming as important as the chips that process it. Marvell is betting that owning the lasers and optical parts, not just the custom AI chips and interconnect silicon, lets it sell a bigger bundle to cloud customers and compete with Broadcom and Nvidia. The risk is price and timing: paying a premium in stock while AI-linked shares are falling, for a deal that will not close for more than a year. The open question is whether optical demand keeps outrunning supply long enough to justify $115 billion.

sources.title: Marvell to buy Lumentum in $115 billion deal in AI data-center bet (MarketScreener/Reuters)
CNBC: Stock market today, Nov. 2, 2026

2026-11-02-01.summary: Marvell will pay 4.5 of its own shares for each Lumentum share, or $1,132 per share, a 23.9% premium to Lumentum's price on October 28 before talks were reported. The equity value is about $102.5 billion, or $115 billion including debt, and Lumentum holders would own roughly 33% of the combined company. Marvell expects the deal to close in the first half of 2028 and to deliver more than $1 billion of annual cost savings. It is Marvell's largest purchase since the $10 billion Inphi deal in 2021. Lumentum shares fell more than 10% and Marvell more than 5% in early trading.

2026-11-02-02.headline: Oil drops about 6% as US-Iran diplomacy advances, even though OPEC+ keeps December output targets unchanged
2026-11-02-02.soWhat: Oil is trading on the odds of reopening the Strait of Hormuz, not on OPEC+ quotas, which barely matter while Gulf exports are physically disrupted. A deal would cut crude prices, but it would also shrink the refining margins that lifted oil majors' profits this quarter, so producers, refiners and shipowners do not all win or lose together. Importing countries and airlines gain from lower fuel costs, while US shale producers lose some of the windfall. The open question is whether talks hold, since prices have swung on every headline.

sources.title: CNBC: Stock market today, Nov. 2, 2026
Voice of Emirates: Oil prices decline on Monday

2026-11-02-02.summary: Brent crude fell more than 6% to about $106 a barrel and US WTI fell to about $97 on reports that the United States and Iran were pursuing talks to end an eight-month conflict. Iran's supreme leader reportedly gave the government some authority to negotiate, and Iranian and Qatari officials held three days of talks. OPEC+ left its December production targets unchanged. The drop follows an October in which crude rose more than 10%, so prices are still far above where they were before the conflict.

2026-11-02-03.headline: US stocks rebound as oil falls, with elections and a jobs report ahead; European factories keep expanding
2026-11-02-03.soWhat: Markets are being pulled by three forces at once: oil and inflation, AI-spending doubts, and political and data events. A fall in oil helps because lower inflation reduces pressure on central banks to keep raising rates, which supports valuations. The October rotation shows investors paying for stable earners over AI growth stories after a sharp tech sell-off. Strong European and UK factory data also cuts the other way, since faster activity can keep rate-hike talk alive at the Bank of England.

sources.title: CNBC: Stock market today, Nov. 2, 2026

2026-11-02-03.summary: The S&P 500 rose 0.6%, the Nasdaq 0.8% and the Dow 537 points, or 1%, in Monday trading as lower oil prices eased inflation worries. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq had both lost ground in October on AI spending worries, the Nasdaq's worst month since March 2025, while the Dow gained almost 2% as investors rotated toward defensive sectors such as healthcare. US midterm elections are on Tuesday and the monthly jobs report is due this week. In Europe, the eurozone manufacturing PMI came in at 52.7, above the 52.4 forecast and just under September's four-year high of 52.9, and UK factory output grew at its fastest pace in more than two years.

2026-11-02-04.headline: Kioxia shares fall about 14% after it says flash-memory price gains are stalling
numbers: NAND price growth: mid-20% range vs ~70% prior quarter
Guided operating profit: 2 trillion yen vs 2.35 trillion expected
2026-11-02-04.soWhat: Memory is a commodity business where profits depend on price much more than on volume. Prices were being driven up by AI data centers buying storage, and a slowdown in price growth, even from very high levels, is read as a sign the shortage is peaking. That matters for makers, which have earned very high margins, and for buyers such as phone, PC and server makers, which would gain from easier pricing. It also adds to October's worry that AI-linked chip stocks had priced in too much.

sources.title: CNBC: Stock market today, Nov. 2, 2026
ZeroHedge (relaying Bloomberg): Flash crash, Kioxia warns NAND price surge ending

2026-11-02-04.summary: Kioxia, the Japanese flash-memory maker, said average selling prices for NAND rose in the mid-20% range in the three months to September, versus about 70% the quarter before. It guided operating profit of 2 trillion yen for the current quarter, below the 2.35 trillion yen analysts expected, and its shares fell about 14%. A Bloomberg report relayed by ZeroHedge said its fab partner Sandisk fell as much as 8%.

2026-11-02-05.headline: BP's third-quarter underlying profit jumps to $8.5 billion as record refining margins help, and net debt falls to $13.9 billion
2026-11-02-05.soWhat: Refining margins hit records because war-related outages and strikes on Russian refineries left fuel short, and the Gulf Coast 3-2-1 crack spread reached an all-time high of $72.64 in September. BP, like Exxon and Chevron, used the windfall to repair its balance sheet rather than increase payouts, which shows how cautious oil majors are about a margin spike that could reverse. Impairments on low-carbon assets show the other side of the strategy shift away from renewables. The open question is how quickly margins normalize if Hormuz reopens.

sources.title: Political.org: Exxon, Chevron and BP beat third-quarter forecasts
Egypt Oil & Gas: bp posts $8.5 Bn underlying profit in Q3 2026

2026-11-02-05.summary: BP reported underlying replacement-cost profit of $8.5 billion, against $2.2 billion a year earlier, $5.7 billion in the second quarter and a consensus of $6.2 billion. The gain came mainly from much higher refining margins and a stronger gas and marketing trading result. It also booked about $4 billion of impairments, mostly on transition businesses such as offshore wind and solar developer Lightsource bp. Net debt fell to $13.9 billion from $22.3 billion at the end of June. CEO Meg O'Neill said the dividend remains the first call on cash, with buybacks only when appropriate, and that refining margins are starting to soften.

2026-11-02-06.headline: Oracle offers $10 billion of common stock as investors question the cost of AI infrastructure
2026-11-02-06.soWhat: Building data centers for AI customers costs far more than the cash these businesses generate today, so even large companies are turning to debt and new shares. Selling stock dilutes existing holders but avoids adding to Oracle's debt load, which markets have been watching closely. It shows that the AI build-out is now limited by financing as much as by chips and power. Lenders and shareholders will push for proof that contracted demand turns into cash.

sources.title: CNBC: Stock market today, Nov. 2, 2026
Bisnow: Oracle aims to calm investor fears with $50B AI funding plan

2026-11-02-06.summary: Oracle launched an offering of $10 billion of common stock, with Wells Fargo, Citigroup and BNP Paribas among the bookrunners, and its shares fell more than 2.5% in premarket trading. The raise fits a financing plan Oracle laid out earlier this year to fund about $45 billion to $50 billion of new cloud capacity, roughly half through equity. The sale comes in the same week Alphabet reported negative free cash flow and Amazon guided to roughly $220 billion of capex.

2026-11-02-07.headline: Jio Platforms posts its first results as a listed company: profit up 14% and EBITDA margin at 54.1%
2026-11-02-07.soWhat: Telecom is a scale business: once the network is built, extra subscribers and data use drop through to profit, which is why margins can expand while revenue grows around 11%. Jio's high 5G share shows how a single operator can shift a whole market to a new technology and then monetize it through data use and gradual price increases. Its listing gives investors a direct way to own India's fastest-growing digital consumer base. The risk is that price competition or regulators cap how fast ARPU can rise.

sources.title: Mint via TradingView: Jio Platforms shares jump 3% post strong Q2 results

2026-11-02-07.summary: Jio Platforms, India's largest mobile operator, reported September-quarter revenue of Rs 40,475 crore, up 11% from a year earlier, and net profit of Rs 8,389 crore, up 14%. EBITDA rose 17% and the margin widened by 2.5 percentage points to 54.1%. Average revenue per user was Rs 218.8, a modest rise, with promotions on fixed broadband holding it back. It added 9.1 million net subscribers, has 300 million 5G users, and 5G now carries 56% of wireless data traffic. Shares rose as much as 3% after the report, following a debut on October 28 at a 21% premium to the IPO price.

2026-11-03-01.headline: Apple's September-quarter revenue rises 12% to a record $114.5 billion on iPhone and Mac strength
2026-11-03-01.soWhat: iPhone is still about half of Apple's revenue, so the upgrade cycle largely sets the company's results, while the steadily growing Services line adds a recurring layer on top of the installed base of devices. The margin is the thing to watch: about a point of the 47.9% came from one-off tariff refunds, and memory chip costs have been the main source of margin pressure. That ties a consumer-device maker to the same memory cycle that drives chipmakers such as Kioxia and SK hynix. The open question is whether strong China demand holds up as the cost of components keeps rising.

sources.title: Apple 8-K: fiscal Q4 2026 results
Stock Titan: stock market today, November 2, 2026

2026-11-03-01.summary: Apple reported fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $114.5 billion, up 12% and a record for a September quarter, in its first report under CEO John Ternus. iPhone revenue was $57.6 billion, up about 17%, and Services reached an all-time high of $31.6 billion, up about 10%. Mac sales jumped about 24% to $10.8 billion while iPad fell about 10% to $6.2 billion. Greater China was the fastest-growing region at $17.5 billion, up about 21%. Gross margin was 47.9%, including roughly one point from tariff refunds, and diluted earnings per share rose 14% to $2.10.

2026-11-03-02.headline: Palantir's revenue nearly doubles to $2.31 billion as US commercial sales pass government sales for the first time
2026-11-03-02.soWhat: The mix shift matters: Palantir began as a government supplier, and companies buying its AI software now bring in more US revenue than agencies do. A 62% adjusted operating margin shows how software costs little to deliver once the product is built and sold. The gap between 96% revenue growth and 6% growth in total contract value suggests revenue is catching up with earlier signings. The open question is whether new bookings accelerate enough to keep growth near this pace.

sources.title: Palantir 8-K: Q3 2026 press release
Closing Look, Monday November 2, 2026

2026-11-03-02.summary: Palantir reported third-quarter revenue of $2.313 billion, up 96% from a year earlier and 20% from the prior quarter. US commercial revenue rose 148% to $984 million, overtaking US government revenue, which grew 96% to $953 million. Adjusted operating margin was 62% and net income was $1.128 billion. The company raised its 2026 revenue forecast to about $8.53 billion and its US commercial forecast to more than $3.559 billion. Total contract value grew only 6% to $2.918 billion.

2026-11-03-03.headline: Marathon Petroleum earns $7.4 billion in a quarter as its refining margin hits $45.70 a barrel, and sells two northern refineries for $4.2 billion
2026-11-03-03.soWhat: A refiner earns the gap between what it pays for crude and what it sells fuel for, multiplied by the barrels it processes, so a margin that is more than two and a half times last year's, on a plant running flat out, produces a profit several times larger. Product supply has been tight while Gulf flows are disrupted, which widens that gap. Selling smaller inland refineries to reinvest on the Gulf Coast concentrates the company where plants are larger and can reach export markets. The open question is how long margins last: crude fell 7.6% on Monday on hopes of a US-Iran deal, and a reopening of Gulf shipping would ease product tightness.

sources.title: Marathon Petroleum 8-K: Q3 2026 earnings release
Stock Titan: stock market today, November 2, 2026

2026-11-03-03.summary: Marathon Petroleum reported third-quarter net income of $7.4 billion, or $26.59 a share, against $1.4 billion a year earlier. Adjusted EBITDA was $11.7 billion, up from $3.2 billion. Its refining and marketing margin was $45.70 a barrel, up from $17.60, and its refineries ran at 100% of crude capacity. It agreed to sell the St. Paul Park and Mandan refineries and related midstream assets for $4.2 billion, with $3.45 billion going to Marathon and $750 million to its pipeline affiliate MPLX. It returned $3.3 billion to shareholders, raised its dividend 10% and added $5 billion to its buyback authorization.

2026-11-03-04.headline: Pfizer raises its 2026 revenue outlook to $62 to $64 billion as new products offset the fading COVID franchise
2026-11-03-04.soWhat: Big pharma has to keep replacing revenue as older products fade, and Pfizer shows the pattern: the pandemic drugs shrink quickly while cancer, heart and other medicines, many bought or licensed from smaller developers, carry growth. Flat reported revenue hides a business growing 7% without COVID products. Paying for outside assets, such as the Innovent deal, hits earnings up front through charges but is how large drugmakers refill pipelines. The open question is whether launches grow fast enough to offset patent expiries later in the decade.

sources.title: Pfizer 8-K: Q3 2026 results

2026-11-03-04.summary: Pfizer's third-quarter revenue was $16.6 billion, roughly flat, and adjusted earnings per share were $0.87, unchanged. Excluding the COVID products Comirnaty and Paxlovid, revenue grew 7%, and launched and acquired products grew 32%. Paxlovid fell 63% and Comirnaty 29%, while Eliquis rose 25% and the cancer drug Padcev rose 55%. The company raised 2026 revenue guidance to $62.0 to $64.0 billion from $60.5 to $62.5 billion, and adjusted EPS guidance to $2.95 to $3.05, which absorbs about $0.10 from a $650 million charge tied to its Innovent Biologics deal.

2026-11-03-05.headline: US factory activity expands for a tenth month with the ISM index at 55.5, while construction spending falls 1.9%
2026-11-03-05.soWhat: A reading above 50 means more factories are growing than shrinking, so manufacturers are still gaining, and a prices-paid reading of 75 means input costs are still rising quickly. That keeps pressure on inflation and explains why markets are pricing a possible rate rise rather than a cut. High borrowing costs show up first in building, where spending fell sharply. The open question is whether the drop in oil prices begins to pull the prices-paid gauge down in the months ahead.

sources.title: Stock Titan: stock market today, November 2, 2026
Closing Look, Monday November 2, 2026

2026-11-03-05.summary: The ISM manufacturing index rose to 55.5 in October from 54.5, beating the 54.5 forecast, and has now signaled expansion for ten straight months. Its production gauge rose to 59.0, the highest since November 2021, while the prices-paid gauge eased to 75.2 from 77.9. A separate S&P Global US manufacturing index eased to 54.9 from 55.9. September construction spending fell 1.9% against an expected 0.4% gain, the steepest drop since April 2020. Futures priced about a 72% chance of a Fed rate rise in December.

2026-11-03-06.headline: A $6.3 billion theft from Binance, linked by analysts to North Korean hackers, is the largest crypto heist on record
2026-11-03-06.soWhat: Exchanges hold customer assets in a small number of large wallets, so one security failure can threaten the whole business, and confidence that customers can withdraw in full is what prevents a run. Covering the loss from its own balance sheet shows Binance's scale, and the modest 2% outflow suggests most customers stayed. State-backed hacking is a growing funding source for sanctioned governments, which raises pressure on regulators to set tougher custody and security standards. The open question is how much of the stolen money can be recovered.

sources.title: Blockchain intelligence firms link North Korea to $6.3B hack on Binance (ITV/AP)
UK Business News Today: 2 November 2026
Closing Look, Monday November 2, 2026

2026-11-03-06.summary: Hackers moved about $6.3 billion out of Binance in roughly 20 minutes across ten blockchains. The blockchain-analysis firm TRM Labs says with high confidence that North Korea's TraderTraitor group was responsible, while Chainalysis calls it likely. Binance has not confirmed who was behind it. Reports say about $3 billion was frozen, and Binance says it will cover all customer losses and had covered about 95% of the stolen assets by Monday. One report puts net withdrawals after service resumed at $3.6 billion, about 2% of customer holdings. Early findings point to a compromised employee laptop.

2026-11-03-07.headline: AI hardware stocks slide as spending worries return, with AMD down 7.5% and Micron down 5.8%
2026-11-03-07.soWhat: Chip, memory and storage makers sell into a small number of customers who are spending borrowed or newly raised money, so doubts about how that spending is financed hit suppliers first. Oracle selling stock and a reported smaller raise at OpenAI both suggest the cost of funding AI capacity is rising. Memory and storage are especially cyclical because prices swing with the pace of orders. The open question is whether AMD's results and outlook on Tuesday show demand still outrunning the funding worries.

sources.title: Closing Look, Monday November 2, 2026
Stock Titan: stock market today, November 2, 2026
UK Business News Today: 2 November 2026

2026-11-03-07.summary: AI hardware shares fell on Monday: AMD dropped 7.52%, Dell 7.43%, Micron 5.78%, Seagate 7.88% and Western Digital 7.52%, while Nvidia fell 1.26%. The Nasdaq Composite lost 1.07% and the technology sector was the worst in the S&P 500 at down 2.95%. Oracle fell 8.76% after it moved to sell $10 billion of stock and $10 billion of notes to fund its AI buildout. UK press also reported that OpenAI has cut its pre-IPO fundraising target to $20 billion from $30 billion, a report this site has not independently confirmed. AMD reports results on Tuesday after the close.

2026-11-03-08.headline: Affle agrees to buy ad-tech firm Perion for about $420 million in cash
2026-11-03-08.soWhat: Independent ad-tech companies sell tools to advertisers, but the largest platforms, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta, take most of the growth in ad spending, which leaves mid-sized independents struggling to reach scale on their own. For the buyer, the appeal is added reach in fast-growing channels such as connected TV and retail media. A premium of about a third is typical when a small public company with a depressed share price is sold. The open question is whether another bidder emerges before shareholders vote.

sources.title: Perion Form 6-K: merger agreement with Affle
Stock Titan: stock market today, November 2, 2026

2026-11-03-08.summary: Affle 3i Limited signed a definitive merger agreement on November 1 to acquire Perion Network for $11.70 a share in cash, a 34.5% premium to the October 30 close. That values Perion's equity at about $420 million. The deal needs Perion shareholder approval and is expected to close in early 2027. Perion sells AI-driven tools that help advertisers buy media across connected TV, digital out-of-home, retail media and social channels. It withdrew its 2026 outlook and suspended its share buyback, under which it had repurchased 21.3 million shares for $196.8 million. Its stock rose about 31% to $11.41.

2026-11-03-09.headline: EVgo's controlling shareholder LS Power proposes to buy out public shareholders at $2.00 a share
2026-11-03-09.soWhat: When a controlling owner buys out the minority, the owner sits on both sides of the deal, which is why an independent committee negotiates the price. EV charging is capital-intensive because networks of fast chargers must be built before they earn, so a private owner can fund growth without the pressure of quarterly results. A closing price below the offer shows investors doubt the deal will be completed at this price. The open question is whether the committee pushes for a higher bid.

sources.title: EVgo Form 8-K: LS Power proposal
Stock Titan: stock market today, November 2, 2026

2026-11-03-09.summary: LS Power, which holds about 56% of EVgo's voting power, made a non-binding proposal on November 2 to buy all the Class A shares it does not already own for $2.00 each in cash. The price is a 59% premium to the October 30 close and 62% above the 30-day average price. LS Power prefers a long-form merger, which gives minority shareholders full disclosure and appraisal rights, and says it will proceed only if a special committee of independent directors recommends it. EVgo has formed that committee and says no decision has been made. Its shares closed up about 47% at $1.85, below the offered price.

2026-11-03-10.headline: US airline shares jump about 4% as crude's sharpest drop in three months eases fuel-cost fears
2026-11-03-10.soWhat: Fuel is one of an airline's largest costs, so a sharp fall in crude lifts expected profit almost immediately, while oil producers and refiners lose the same amount. Most US airlines do not hedge much of their fuel, which makes their shares move quickly with the oil price. The reaction also shows that investors treat the Gulf disruption as the main driver of the energy price spike. The open question is whether the diplomatic progress is real, since a breakdown in talks would reverse the move.

sources.title: Stock Titan: stock market today, November 2, 2026
Closing Look, Monday November 2, 2026

2026-11-03-10.summary: United Airlines rose 4.80%, Delta 4.08% and American 3.81% on Monday as oil had its sharpest one-day drop in three months on hopes for US-Iran diplomacy. Brent fell 7.63% to $104.77 a barrel and US crude fell 7.36% to $96.46. Energy was the worst sector in the S&P 500, down 3.96%, while consumer discretionary was the best, up 2.41%. Iran has offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz under strict conditions, and talks with Qatari mediators continued.

2026-11-03-11.headline: IDEXX lifts its 2026 profit outlook after veterinary diagnostics revenue rises 10% to $1.21 billion
2026-11-03-11.soWhat: IDEXX follows a razor-and-blade model: it places analyzers in veterinary clinics and then earns recurring revenue from the test consumables and lab services that run on them. Each new instrument adds years of repeat sales, so installations are an early signal of future revenue. Investors had worried that fewer vet visits would slow growth, and the 10% organic gain shows testing and pricing are offsetting that. The open question is whether visit volumes recover or stay soft.

sources.title: IDEXX 8-K: Q3 2026 results
Stock Titan: stock market today, November 2, 2026

2026-11-03-11.summary: IDEXX Laboratories reported third-quarter revenue of $1.214 billion, up 10% both as reported and organically. Diluted earnings per share were $4.01, up 18% as reported and 22% on a comparable basis. The company raised its 2026 EPS outlook to $14.96 to $15.16, about $0.25 higher at the midpoint, driven by a higher revenue forecast. Its Companion Animal Group grew 11%, helped by a strong quarter of diagnostic imaging system installations. The shares closed up about 22% on Monday.

2026-11-03-12.soWhat: Discount chains run on thin margins and large fixed costs, mainly leases and wages, so rising sales, which grew 8.4% in the three weeks to October 18, cannot fix a balance sheet with too much debt or too many expensive stores. Administration lets a buyer pick the better stores and leases and leave the rest, which is why several rivals are circling. Higher business rates and wages hit low-priced, labor-heavy retailers hardest. The open question is how many stores and jobs survive a sale.

2026-11-04-01.headline: The 10-year Treasury yield climbs to 4.96% as two Fed presidents say rates may need to rise
2026-11-04-01.soWhat: The 10-year yield sets the baseline for mortgages, auto loans and corporate bonds, so a yield near 5% means borrowing stays expensive for households and companies alike. Sectors that rely on cheap debt, such as housing, utilities and leveraged buyouts, feel it most, while banks and savers earning more on cash gain. The open question is whether Friday's jobs data pushes the Fed toward a hike or lets inflation pressure ease.

2026-11-04-02.headline: Brent settles near $103.60 after a 7% one-day drop on reports Iran has cleared the way for peace talks
2026-11-04-02.soWhat: Oil still carries a large war premium, so headlines about talks move prices by several dollars in a day. Producers and shippers gain from high prices, while airlines, refiners buying crude and consumers pay more, so a deal that reopens Hormuz would shift profits quickly. The open question is whether talks produce a real reopening, since no deal has been reached and the US has threatened to resume strikes after the midterm elections.

2026-11-04-03.headline: AMD posts record $13.4 billion revenue as data center sales nearly double and guides next quarter to about $17 billion
2026-11-04-03.soWhat: Data center products now make up about 63% of AMD's revenue, so the company's results track AI infrastructure spending more than the PC cycle. Selling whole rack systems rather than single chips lets AMD capture more of each customer's budget, but it also raises the bar on execution against Nvidia. 2026-11-04-06.soWhat: Cannabis producers are consolidating because many sell at low prices into crowded markets and need scale in purchasing, production and distribution. 2026-11-04-07.soWhat: Shopify earns far more from payments and shipping services on its merchants' sales than from monthly subscriptions, so its revenue tracks how much its merchants sell. Kelley Blue Book counted 20,237 Cybertrucks sold in the US last year, down 48% from 38,965 in 2024, against Musk's early prediction of 250,000 a year. NHTSA has logged 11 recalls since the truck launched in 2023. Cybercab entered production this year with installed capacity listed above 125,000 units, and NHTSA opened an audit in September on how Tesla certified its safety compliance.

2026-11-08-06.headline: IEA data show global energy investment of about $3.4 trillion in 2026, with China the largest spender at $940 billion
2026-11-08-06.soWhat: Who spends determines who builds the plants, grids and supply chains for the next decade, and China outspending the US by about $325 billion a year (calculated) gives its equipment makers and utilities a large home market. Suppliers of turbines, transformers and cables gain from high spending, while countries with less capital face higher borrowing costs for the same projects. Utilities that earn a return on what they build benefit most when spending is high. The open question is how much of the total goes to power networks rather than fuel supply.

sources.title: Global Times: Global energy investment (IEA data, Nov 5, 2026)

2026-11-08-06.summary: Global energy investment is expected to reach about $3.4 trillion in 2026, according to International Energy Agency data presented in a November 5 report by Global Times. China leads at $940 billion, followed by the United States at $615 billion and the European Union at $440 billion. Advanced economies and China together account for more than 70% of the total. The figure covers all energy spending, not only clean energy.

2026-11-09-01.headline: Crédit Agricole proposes merging its Italian unit into Banco BPM to build Italy's third-largest bank
2026-11-09-01.soWhat: A merger of this type lets Crédit Agricole lift its stake through new shares in a combined bank instead of a cash bid, which avoids a mandatory takeover offer for the whole company. Bank deals in Europe are driven by scale: a larger Italian franchise spreads technology, compliance and funding costs over more customers and gives it more weight against UniCredit and Intesa Sanpaolo. Banco BPM shareholders gain a premium and a cash payout but give up some control to a dominant holder. The open question is whether the board and Italian authorities accept a structure that leaves the French group close to majority ownership.

sources.title: Investing.com: Crédit Agricole proposes Banco BPM merger, 20% premium and €1 bln dividend
Crédit Agricole SA release via Manila Times (Nov 9, 2026)

2026-11-09-01.summary: Crédit Agricole made a friendly proposal on November 9 to combine Banco BPM with its own Italian arm, Crédit Agricole Italia, including the Italian insurance businesses. The French group's stake would rise from 29.6% to about 45% of the combined bank. Banco BPM shareholders would receive an exchange ratio that reflects a 20% premium plus an extraordinary dividend of €1 billion. The combined group would stay listed in Milan, and completion is targeted for the second half of 2027. Banco BPM's board has not yet agreed to open talks.

2026-11-09-02.headline: Nvidia's board opens an investigation after CEO Jensen Huang admits an affair with a businesswoman US intelligence links to China
2026-11-09-02.soWhat: Nvidia sells the chips that most AI data centers run on, and the US government controls which of them can go to China, so questions about a leader's contacts touch both investor confidence and export-control politics. A drop of this size is a governance discount rather than a change in demand: the chip order book is unchanged, and rivals such as AMD and Broadcom rose the same day. Customers and lawmakers will watch how the board handles the review and whether Huang's role in shaping chip export policy is questioned. The open question is whether the inquiry stays a personal matter or widens into scrutiny of Nvidia's China-related sales.

sources.title: CNBC: Nvidia board investigation into CEO Jensen Huang (Nov 8, 2026)
CNBC: Stock market today, Nov 9, 2026

2026-11-09-02.summary: Nvidia's board has opened an independent inquiry into reports that a foreign intelligence effort targeted Jensen Huang through his relationship with a businesswoman tied to Megaspeed, a cloud company and Nvidia customer accused of helping restricted Chinese firms obtain AI chips. Huang emailed staff on November 8 admitting he had been unfaithful and apologizing. The board said it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised, and a spokesperson said he will stay as CEO. Nvidia shares fell about 5% to 6% in Monday trading, and the company reports third-quarter earnings on November 17.

2026-11-09-03.headline: US stocks surge as oil falls about 4%, with the Dow up about 650 points and the Nasdaq up 2%
2026-11-09-03.soWhat: Oil is an input cost for almost every business and a driver of inflation, so a fall in crude eases pressure on both company margins and the central bank. That matters now because markets have been pricing a December Fed rate hike after the strong jobs data, and high yields have hurt growth stocks. Winners from cheaper oil include airlines, chemical makers and consumers; oil producers lose revenue. The open question is whether the move lasts, since talks over Iran and the Strait of Hormuz have stalled before.

sources.title: CNBC: Stock market today, Nov 9, 2026
Stock Market Watch: Nightly Market Digest, Nov 6, 2026

2026-11-09-03.summary: The Dow rose about 650 points (1.3%), the S&P 500 gained 1.5% and the Nasdaq added 2% on Monday as falling oil prices lifted the broader market. Brent dropped about 4% to roughly $94 a barrel and WTI fell 3% to about $87. The rally partly reversed Thursday's AI-driven selloff, which left the Nasdaq about 11% below its record. Traders still face a hot jobs report, with 165,000 jobs added in October, and US consumer price data due Tuesday. Broadcom and AMD rose about 5% each, Amazon gained 5%, and Nvidia fell 5% to 6%.

2026-11-09-04.headline: Oil slips as Iran talks stall: Brent near $94 after eight months of war, with Hormuz still disrupted
2026-11-09-04.soWhat: A large share of the world's oil and LNG moves through the Strait of Hormuz, so every sign of a deal or a breakdown moves crude within hours, and prices near $90 or above mean producers earn windfall margins while importers face inflation. Upstream companies outside the Gulf, such as US shale and Norwegian operators, gain most from the higher price. Refiners and airlines lose when crude spikes and gain when it falls. The open question is whether a signed deal can reopen the strait for good after earlier attempts failed.

sources.title: CNBC: Trump says Iran strikes unlikely if talks produce a deal (Nov 8, 2026)
CNBC: Stock market today, Nov 9, 2026

2026-11-09-04.summary: Brent fell about 4% to roughly $94 and WTI about 3% to $87 on Monday, even though talks to end the US-Iran war looked stalled. President Trump said renewed strikes are highly unlikely if Iran signs a deal on its nuclear program and the Strait of Hormuz, but kept strikes on bridges and power plants as an option. Secretary of State Marco Rubio called Iran's demands outrageous. The war is now more than eight months old, the US has kept a naval blockade of Iranian ports for months, and three US aircraft carriers are in the region.

2026-11-09-05.headline: China's factory-gate prices rise 5.7%, the fastest since 2022, while consumer inflation slows to 0.7%
2026-11-09-05.soWhat: The wide gap between factory prices and shop prices squeezes manufacturers, who pay more for raw materials but cannot pass the cost on to cautious households. It also shows two different Chinas: strong external demand and commodity costs on the supply side, and a property slump weighing on consumer confidence at home. For global buyers, higher Chinese producer prices can feed into the price of exported goods. The open question is whether firms will eventually raise consumer prices or absorb the cost through thinner margins.

sources.title: CNBC: China inflation at four-year high (Nov 9, 2026)

2026-11-09-05.summary: China's producer price index rose 5.7% year on year in October, above the 5.3% economists expected and the fastest since June 2022. It was the third straight month of acceleration, driven by sharp price rises in mining and raw materials. Consumer prices rose only 0.7%, down from 0.9% in September, and core inflation slowed to 0.8% from 1%. Gasoline was the largest upward push on consumer prices, but a bigger-than-expected fall in food prices offset much of it. Weak property-market demand is holding back consumer inflation, and the CSI 300 index rose 0.56% after the data.

2026-11-09-06.headline: UniCredit posts record third-quarter profit of €3.3 billion and lifts its 2026 target
2026-11-09-06.soWhat: Profit is rising faster than revenue because the bank keeps costs and credit losses low relative to income, and fee and insurance income reduces dependence on interest rates. A bank earning a 25% return on tangible equity can fund large dividends and an acquisition at once, which is why it can afford to take control of a rival such as Commerzbank. Rivals and smaller banks face a stronger consolidator, as the Crédit Agricole proposal for Banco BPM shows. The open question is how much of the profit growth depends on interest rates staying high.

sources.title: RTTNews: UniCredit lifts FY26 profit view after higher Q3 (Nov 9, 2026)
Investing.com: UniCredit tops Q3 2026 forecasts, lifts guidance

2026-11-09-06.summary: UniCredit reported third-quarter net profit of about €3.26 billion, up 24% from a year earlier, on revenues of €6.9 billion, up 11.8%. Net interest income rose 8.2% to €3.83 billion and fees and insurance income rose 10.7% to €2.39 billion. Loan loss provisions rose 85% to €210 million. The bank now expects 2026 net profit well above €11.5 billion, up from well above €11 billion, and expects the remaining approvals for taking control of Commerzbank by late November. UniCredit shares rose about 5% in Milan.

2026-11-09-07.headline: Fox completes its $22 billion purchase of Roku, putting a TV operating system under a broadcaster

2026-11-09-07.soWhat: The deal joins a company that owns programs and sports with the company that controls the TV home screen, where viewers choose what to watch and where ads are sold. Owning the platform gives Fox direct data on viewers and a larger ad business, but it also invites suspicion from Netflix, Disney and others whose apps sit on Roku devices. Roku shareholders gain a premium and a stake in the combined company; rival streamers lose a neutral distributor. The open question is whether Fox's promise to keep Roku open holds as it pushes its own services.

sources.title: The Desk: Fox completes acquisition of Roku (Nov 9, 2026)

2026-11-09-07.summary: Fox closed its roughly $22 billion acquisition of streaming platform Roku, ahead of the first-half-2027 timetable. Each Roku share converted into $95.30 in cash plus 0.9799 Fox Class A shares, and former Roku holders will own about 26% of the combined company. Roku joins Tubi, Fox One and Red Seat Ventures in a new unit called Fox Digital Platforms, and founder Anthony Wood joins the Fox board. Fox expects about $400 million of annual cost savings within two years. Roku's platform reaches more than 100 million households, and Fox says it will keep Roku open to all content partners.

2026-11-09-08.headline: Voters back limits on data centers: restrictions passed in 44 of 45 local votes as power bills become a campaign issue
numbers: Governor winners backing tighter rules: 32 of 34
Voters opposing a local data center: ~75%
2026-11-09-08.soWhat: Data centers are now one of the largest new sources of electricity demand in the US, so rules on where they go and who pays for new power lines decide how much grid capacity utilities will build. Tighter rules could slow demand growth for utilities and gas-turbine makers and raise costs for cloud companies, while helping developers who already hold permits. Texas, expected to overtake northern Virginia as the largest data-center market by 2030, is the key test. The open question is whether new rules will mainly shift costs onto the data centers or reduce how many get built.

sources.title: AP via OPB: AI data centers took a beating in the midterm elections (Nov 6, 2026)

2026-11-09-08.summary: In the November midterms, restrictions on data centers passed in 44 of the 45 local referendums where counting was complete, across 47 votes in 44 municipalities in 12 states. Data Center Watch found that 32 of 34 governors elected, in races AP called, support stronger regulation or restrictions, and 12 support bans or moratoriums. Campaigns spent more than $380 million on TV ads mentioning data centers, and about three-quarters of voters oppose a new data center in their own community. The Nasdaq fell 11% below its record on Thursday amid worries that costlier borrowing and tighter rules could slow construction.

2026-11-09-09.headline: AST SpaceMobile signs a $1.3 billion deal for Firefly rocket engines and the right to build them itself
2026-11-09-09.soWhat: Launch is a bottleneck for satellite operators, so AST is buying its way toward its own rocket instead of waiting for others. The license shows a different model from a normal parts supply deal: the engine maker earns a large upfront payment but gives up part of the future production volume. Firefly gains funding and a major customer; rocket providers such as SpaceX lose a potential launch customer. The open question is whether AST can build and fly a new reusable rocket on a late-2028 schedule.

sources.title: New Space Economy: AST SpaceMobile is buying Firefly engines and the right to build them (Nov 6, 2026)
Devdiscourse (Reuters): Firefly inks $1.3 billion deal to supply engines for AST SpaceMobile

2026-11-09-09.summary: AST SpaceMobile agreed a three-year, $1.3 billion-plus contract with Firefly Aerospace for engines for AST's planned heavy-lift rocket. Firefly will deliver 36 engines (27 Miranda and 9 Vira) for the first three rockets, and AST gets a license to make the same engines itself afterward. Firefly keeps the designs and can sell to other customers. AST will pay in cash and Class A shares, and Firefly plans to expand test bays in Briggs, Texas. Firefly shares rose about 18% on the news, according to Reuters, and defense and space stocks led gains on Friday.

2026-11-10-01.headline: FDA orders new vision-loss warnings on Mounjaro, Zepbound, Ozempic and Wegovy, yet Lilly and Novo shares rise
2026-11-10-01.soWhat: A label change is a lighter regulatory step than a restriction, and the absolute risk is small, so investors treated it as manageable. The stakes are highest for Lilly, where Mounjaro and Zepbound make up about two-thirds of $24.4 billion in quarterly revenue, so any slowdown in new prescriptions would be visible quickly. Rivals developing obesity drugs also rose, which suggests the market sees the warning as applying to the whole drug class rather than to one maker. The open question is whether doctors and patients start fewer treatments once the new labels reach them.

sources.title: IBTimes: FDA orders GLP-1 vision-loss warnings, Lilly and Novo shares rebound

2026-11-10-01.summary: On November 9 the FDA required updated labels for GLP-1 drugs to cover non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION), a rare eye condition that can cause sudden, permanent vision loss in one eye. In a review of 126 clinical trials, the agency found 6.4 probable cases per 100,000 person-years among GLP-1 patients, against 3.8 for patients on a placebo or another diabetes drug. Lilly shares rose 4.3% to $1,412.05 and Novo Nordisk's US-listed shares rose 2.7% to $41.40, helped by a market-wide rally. Lilly said it is reviewing the decision and Novo said it remains confident in its drugs' benefit-risk profile.

2026-11-10-02.headline: Strathcona agrees to buy Greenfire in an Alberta oil sands deal worth up to C$2.9 billion
numbers: Cash option: C$11.00 per share, ~39% premium
2026-11-10-02.soWhat: Oil sands projects have large fixed costs for steam, processing and transport, so combining two Alberta producers lets one operator spread those costs over more barrels. Waterous Energy Fund owns about 72% of Greenfire and 57% of Strathcona, so the largest owner is on both sides and has backed the deal, which makes approval more likely. Greenfire holders gain a sizeable premium, while the choice of cash or shares lets smaller holders either exit or stay exposed to the larger company. The open question is whether the remaining shareholder and regulatory approvals arrive on the early-2027 timetable.

sources.title: BOE Report (Reuters): Canada's Strathcona to buy Greenfire in up to C$2.9 billion deal
BNN Bloomberg: Strathcona Resources signs deal to buy Greenfire Resources

2026-11-10-02.summary: Strathcona Resources agreed to acquire Greenfire Resources in a deal valued at about C$2.7 billion to C$2.9 billion (roughly US$1.9 billion) including debt. Greenfire holders can choose C$11.00 in cash or 0.25 Strathcona shares per share; the cash option is a premium of nearly 39% to the November 6 close and the share option about 15%. Strathcona expects to issue 43 million to 60 million shares and pay up to C$740 million in cash, depending on elections. Greenfire had net debt of about C$550 million at September 30, and closing is expected in early 2027.

2026-11-10-03.headline: Constellation Energy jumps 10.5% as quarterly profit and revenue beat estimates
numbers: Driver: results above analyst estimates plus data-center power deals
2026-11-10-03.soWhat: A generator without long-term contracts earns whatever the wholesale power market pays, so contracts with data-center customers turn volatile revenue into steadier, pre-agreed income. That is why the stock reacts so strongly to evidence that these deals are producing profit. The risk runs the other way too: if local limits or higher financing costs slow data-center building, demand growth for power would be lower than investors have priced in. The open question is how widely restrictions spread beyond the local votes held so far.

sources.title: BNN Bloomberg: US stocks rally and recover most of last week's losses as oil prices swing lower

2026-11-10-03.summary: Constellation Energy shares rose 10.5% on November 9 after the nuclear-heavy power producer reported summer-quarter profit and revenue above analyst expectations. The company has benefited from deals to supply power to data centers run by large technology firms. The jump came as AI-infrastructure stocks rebounded: CoreWeave rose 5.6% after a 15.4% fall the week before. That sell-off was driven by worries that Democratic gains in state elections could bring limits on data centers, which are drawing voter anger over power bills, and by rising borrowing costs.

2026-11-10-04.headline: Trade Desk surges after hours as third-quarter revenue of $736 million beats estimates by a wide margin
2026-11-10-04.soWhat: The Trade Desk is an independent platform that advertisers use to buy ads across the open internet, and it earns a share of the spend that runs through it. Its stock had fallen on fears that large rivals such as Amazon were taking budget, so a quarter 13% above the revenue it had guided shows spend through independent platforms held up. Growth is still flat on a year earlier, so the market is rewarding stabilization, not a return to fast growth. The open question is whether the fourth-quarter guide of at least $755 million proves the bottom or only a short bounce.

sources.title: CNBC: Stocks making the biggest moves after hours, Trade Desk, Sanmina, Securitize and more
PPC Land: Trade Desk stock drops 24% as Q3 guidance points to 12% revenue decline

2026-11-10-04.summary: The Trade Desk reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of 33 cents a share on revenue of $736 million, against analyst estimates of 25 cents and $650 million. It guided fourth-quarter revenue to at least $755 million, also above expectations, and the shares rose as much as 19% after hours. The result follows an August outlook that sent the stock down about 24%, when the company guided to at least $650 million for the quarter. Revenue was roughly flat on the $739 million reported a year earlier.

2026-11-10-05.headline: Embraer posts record third-quarter revenue of $2.35 billion and raises its 2026 sales and cash targets
2026-11-10-05.soWhat: Aircraft makers book revenue when jets are delivered, so a backlog is a forward view of demand: $35.7 billion equals about four years of sales at this year's guided pace. Embraer sells commercial regional jets, business jets and defense aircraft, which spreads its exposure beyond airline cycles. Higher margins on higher volume show the benefit of fixed factory costs being spread over more aircraft. The open question is whether suppliers and the factory can keep delivery rates rising to convert the backlog on schedule.

sources.title: Investing.com: Embraer Q3 2026 results lift stock on record revenue

2026-11-10-05.summary: Embraer reported third-quarter revenue of $2.35 billion, up 17% on a year earlier, with adjusted EBIT of $255 million and a margin of 10.9% versus 8.6% a year ago. Its backlog reached a record $35.7 billion, up 14%, and it delivered 22 commercial and 41 executive jets in the quarter. The company raised 2026 revenue guidance to $8.4 billion to $8.6 billion and lifted its adjusted free cash flow target to at least $700 million, while keeping delivery and margin guidance. Shares rose about 5.7% in premarket trading to above their 52-week high.

2026-11-10-06.headline: Ferguson lifts its 2026 sales outlook after quarterly sales rise 9.5% to $9.03 billion
2026-11-10-06.soWhat: A building-products distributor earns a margin on the goods it moves, so growth comes from more volume, more customers and acquisitions rather than from higher margins, which is what a flat 10.7% margin shows. Faster non-residential growth shows commercial and industrial projects are carrying demand while housing grows more slowly. Ferguson completed eleven acquisitions this year adding about $1.5 billion of annualized revenue, a sign that fragmented regional distributors are being consolidated into larger networks. The open question is how long non-residential demand stays strong.

sources.title: Investing.com: Ferguson soars on earnings beat, raised guidance

2026-11-10-06.summary: Ferguson reported fiscal third-quarter sales of $9.03 billion, up 9.5%, with organic growth of 7.0% and acquisitions adding 2.7%. Adjusted earnings were $3.43 a share against an estimate of $2.46, and adjusted operating profit rose 8.9% to $962 million at a flat 10.7% margin. The distributor now expects calendar 2026 sales growth of about 7%, up from mid-single digits, and raised the low end of its margin range to 9.6% to 9.8%. Non-residential sales grew 15% and residential 6%, and shares rose about 12% on Monday.

2026-11-10-07.headline: Maersk raises its 2026 profit outlook a third time, but shares fall about 11%
numbers: Q3 EBITDA: $4.7B vs $2.7B a year earlier
2026-11-10-07.soWhat: A container line's profit depends mostly on the price per box compared with a fixed cost of ships and terminals, so a rate spike lifts earnings sharply without any extra cargo. Shares fell because the guidance raise was largely expected and the quarter came in under forecasts. Congestion that ties up ships works like a cut in supply, which helps carriers and hurts shippers who pay more. The open question is whether rates hold once congestion clears.

2026-11-10-07.summary: Maersk reported third-quarter EBITDA of $4.7 billion, up from $2.7 billion a year earlier but below the $5.04 billion analysts expected, and raised its 2026 underlying EBITDA guidance to $14.0 billion to $14.5 billion from $10.5 billion to $12.5 billion. The upgrade came from higher freight rates, with the Shanghai container freight index averaging 46% above the previous quarter amid port congestion, while Maersk's own volumes fell about 1%. It now expects free cash flow above $3 billion. The report came on November 5 and was still being digested in shipping briefs on November 9.

2026-11-10-08.headline: Treasury yields hold near 4.9% as stocks rebound, with falling oil the main relief
2026-11-10-08.soWhat: The 10-year yield is the benchmark behind mortgage rates, corporate borrowing and the discount rate investors apply to stocks, so a yield near 4.9% weighs on everything from housing to data-center financing. Oil is the swing factor: lower crude cuts fuel costs and eases the inflation pressure that keeps yields high. The open question is whether oil stays lower long enough to pull yields down, or whether strong jobs data keeps rate expectations rising.

CNBC: Post Market Wrap, November 9, 2026

2026-11-10-08.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield edged up to 4.87% on November 9 from 4.86% on Friday, still well below last month's peak above 5.30%, the highest in two decades. Stocks rallied as the S&P 500 rose 2.3% to 7,549.94, its best day since April, while Brent crude fell 5.8% to $92.57 from above $112 at the start of the month. The New York Fed's survey showed inflation expectations unchanged at still-elevated levels, and strong jobs data on Friday had reinforced expectations of higher rates.

2026-11-10-09.headline: Airlines and cruise lines rise as oil slides on hopes the Iran war will not resume
2026-11-10-09.soWhat: Fuel is one of the largest costs for airlines and cruise operators, so a fall in crude flows straight into profit forecasts, while oil producers lose the same amount. That is why the two groups move in opposite directions on a day like this. Travel demand also depends on confidence that conflict will not spread, so progress in talks helps both costs and bookings. The open question is whether the talks hold, since a return to strikes would send oil back up.

sources.title: BNN Bloomberg: US stocks rally and recover most of last week's losses as oil prices swing lower
CNBC: Stocks making the biggest moves after hours, November 9, 2026

2026-11-10-09.summary: Brent crude fell 5.8% to $92.57 a barrel on November 9, from above $112 at the start of the month, after President Trump said resuming strikes on Iran was highly unlikely if negotiations progress. WTI traded near $87. Energy stocks fell while cruise lines and airlines rose. Secretary of State Marco Rubio described some Iranian demands for ending the war as outrageous, so talks remain unsettled.

2026-11-10-10.headline: GLP-1 users cut snack spending and buy more supplements, and Novonesis sees an opening
numbers: GLP-1 users spending less on snacks: ~70%
Novonesis Human Health Q3 organic sales: -8%
2026-11-10-10.soWhat: Weight-loss drugs change what households buy: snack volumes fall and spending shifts toward products that address nutrient gaps. Ingredient suppliers such as Novonesis hope to follow that demand, but its own probiotic sales fell, which shows the opportunity is not yet in the results. Packaged-food makers face lower volumes, while suppliers with scientific proof for a health claim could win. The open question is whether clinical evidence appears to support supplements for GLP-1 users.

2026-11-10-10.summary: A PwC survey of UK adults found about 70% of GLP-1 users spend less on snacks while 40% spend more on vitamins and supplements, and over 80% of those who stopped the drugs kept some diet changes. Its Human Health unit, about 11% of sales, saw organic sales fall 8% in the third quarter on weaker North American probiotic demand. The global dietary supplements market was about $209.5 billion in 2025.

2026-11-10-11.headline: Drone delivery firm Zipline raises $1.5 billion at a $21.5 billion valuation as Walmart adds 300 sites
2026-11-10-11.soWhat: Delivery from the last warehouse or store to the customer is one of retail's most expensive steps, and drones aim to make fast delivery cheaper by using store parking lots as launch points. For Walmart, the stores it already operates become hubs, which is an advantage over rivals without a dense store network. The valuation depends on drones scaling from dozens of sites to hundreds. The open question is whether regulators and communities accept the noise and safety trade-offs.

The round was led by Paradigm, WCM Investment Management and Layer Global, with Fidelity, Uber and others taking part. A new multi-year Walmart agreement adds 300 US drone delivery sites, up from 21 active sites today. Zipline plans to spend the money on manufacturing and hiring.

2026-11-10-12.headline: Lucid's third-quarter revenue of $350 million misses estimates as it resets production
2026-11-10-12.soWhat: A low-volume carmaker carries large fixed costs for its factory and engineering, so building fewer cars than it delivers cuts cash burn and clears inventory but also pushes the loss per car higher. Withdrawing the volume target shows how hard it is to reach scale in premium electric cars when demand is uneven. The open question is whether its Gravity SUV can lift volumes enough to cover those fixed costs.

It withdrew its 2026 target of 25,000 to 27,000 vehicles and is aiming for $1.4 billion of cash-flow improvements this year.

2026-11-10-13.headline: Qualys beats third-quarter estimates but its shares fall about 8% on a cautious outlook
2026-11-10-13.soWhat: Subscription software is valued on how fast recurring revenue grows, so a guide that only matches consensus can disappoint even when profit beats. Qualys sells cloud-based security scanning on annual contracts, which makes revenue steady but slow to accelerate. The market is signaling that profit beats count for less than evidence of faster sales growth. The open question is whether new products can lift revenue growth above the current pace.

sources.title: Investing.com: Qualys beats Q3 2026 estimates but shares fall after hours

2026-11-10-13.summary: Qualys reported third-quarter earnings of $2.12 per diluted share on revenue of $188 million, ahead of estimates.
