Shares fell 7.9% after hours to $186.54 as investors weighed a solid quarter against a modest sales outlook.

2026-11-11-01.headline: Hotter October inflation pushes the 10-year Treasury yield back above 5% as the Fed signals a December hike
2026-11-11-01.soWhat: A 10-year yield at 5% raises the cost of mortgages, corporate bonds and project finance across the economy, and it lowers what investors will pay today for profits expected far in the future. That hits growth and tech stocks hardest, while banks and insurers can earn more on new loans and bonds. Falling gasoline prices should cool headline inflation in November, so the open question is whether core prices keep running hot enough to force more than one hike.

sources.title: CNBC: Stock market live updates, November 10, 2026
Eurasia Business News: Dow, Nasdaq, S&P 500 fall on November 10, 2026; oil and gold retreat

2026-11-11-01.summary: US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October against a 0.3% forecast, and core prices, which strip out food and energy, rose 0.3% against 0.2%. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said he leans toward raising rates in December and that a half-point move should be considered, while Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan said two more quarter-point hikes are likely needed. The 10-year Treasury yield jumped more than 14 basis points to about 5.00%. The S&P 500 fell 0.38% to 7,520.93 and the Nasdaq 0.74%, a day after the S&P's best session since April.

2026-11-11-02.headline: Anthropic sets its IPO range at $70 to $78 a share, aiming to raise up to $64 billion at a value of up to $1.4 trillion
2026-11-11-02.soWhat: This would be one of the largest share sales ever, and it gives public investors their first direct stake in a leading AI model developer rather than in the chip and cloud companies that supply it. The strategic placement shows how tightly the AI supply chain is linked: chipmakers and cloud providers are investing in a customer that buys their products. The range sits below the roughly $2 trillion some early holders hoped for, a sign that the recent selloff in AI stocks has made investors more careful about price. The open question is whether demand holds up at the top of the range after a week of falling tech shares.

sources.title: CNBC: Anthropic sets IPO price range of $70 to $78, looks to start trading Nov. 19

2026-11-11-02.summary: Anthropic launched the roadshow for its Nasdaq listing under the ticker ANT, offering 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each. At the top of the range the deal would raise about $64.4 billion and value the company at up to $1.405 trillion on a fully diluted basis, against $965 billion in a May funding round. Seven strategic partners, AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC, agreed to buy $26 billion of non-voting stock at the IPO price. The filing shows nine-month revenue of $33.24 billion and a $104 billion net loss, mostly from fair-value changes on convertible notes and derivatives; pricing is planned for November 18.

2026-11-11-03.headline: Nvidia's board hires Wachtell Lipton for an independent review of CEO Jensen Huang, and the shares fall another 6%
2026-11-11-03.soWhat: Nvidia supplies most of the chips used to train and run AI models, so investors treat its leadership as part of the AI industry's own risk. A long review raises key-person risk for a company closely identified with its founder, and it lands while Washington is already debating chip export rules for China. Customers are unlikely to switch suppliers quickly, so the near-term effect is on the stock's valuation more than on orders. The open question is how long the review takes and whether it leads to any change in leadership or export controls.

sources.title: CNBC: Nvidia hires law firm Wachtell Lipton to lead Jensen Huang affair probe
CNBC: Stock market live updates, November 10, 2026

2026-11-11-03.summary: Nvidia's independent directors retained law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, with former acting US Attorney Joon H. Kim leading the work, to examine whether company secrets or national security were compromised. The review follows reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort and his acknowledgment of a personal relationship with a woman reported to be linked to Chinese intelligence. The board said on Sunday it had no reason to believe secrets or security were compromised, and Nvidia said Huang is committed to continuing as CEO. The stock fell more than 4% on Monday and about 6% on Tuesday, and its market value briefly dipped below $4 trillion.

2026-11-11-04.headline: Brent briefly drops below $90 for the first time since August as hopes grow that the Iran conflict is ending
2026-11-11-04.soWhat: Falling crude moves money from producers to consumers: airlines, truckers, chemical makers and drivers pay less, while oil companies' cash flow and budgets shrink. The high freight cost for Gulf barrels shows that buyers in Asia still pay a war premium to move oil, which favors exporters in the Americas whose cargoes avoid Hormuz. US drilling has kept rising, with the rig count at 604, the most since May 2024, so a lasting drop in prices could slow that growth next year. The open question is whether a deal with Iran restores Gulf flows fully or the tanker attacks keep a floor under prices.

sources.title: OilPrice.com: Oil falls to lowest level since August
Eurasia Business News: Dow, Nasdaq, S&P 500 fall on November 10, 2026; oil and gold retreat
CNBC: Stock market live updates, November 10, 2026

2026-11-11-04.summary: Brent crude for January settled at $91.49 a barrel on Tuesday, down 1.2%, after briefly trading below $90, and WTI settled at $86.04; both were the lowest closes since August 31. Crude has fallen almost $30 a barrel since the US midterm elections, as the administration signaled it is reluctant to strike Iran again and markets priced in an end to the conflict. Shipping risk has not gone away: drones and missiles have hit at least 16 tankers in the Strait of Hormuz this month, and a supertanker voyage from the Gulf to China costs about $36 to $37 a barrel against about $22.50 from the US. The US average gasoline price fell below $4 a gallon for the first time since July.

2026-11-11-05.headline: A windless cold spell sends European power prices above €600 per megawatt-hour in peak hours
numbers: German Oct average: ~€171/MWh vs €82 a year earlier
2026-11-11-05.soWhat: When wind and solar drop, the most expensive plants still running, usually gas-fired, set the price for every megawatt-hour sold, so a calm cold week lifts power bills across the whole system. That rewards owners of flexible gas plants, batteries and pumped storage, which earn the most in scarce hours, and hurts energy-intensive industry and retailers that have not hedged. Episodes like this are why grid operators pay for backup capacity and why storage investment keeps rising. The open question is how many more of these windless spells Europe faces this winter while gas prices stay high.

sources.title: Irish Examiner (Bloomberg): European power prices shoot above €600 as wind generation slumps
Energy Connects (Bloomberg): Soaring gas costs squeeze out Europe's negative power prices

2026-11-11-05.summary: A slow-moving weather front left northwest and central Europe still and cloudy this week, cutting wind and solar output, with the lull expected to last through Wednesday. Peak evening prices rose above €600 per megawatt-hour on Monday; Germany's day-ahead price for the day was €345.64 and France's €334.12, the highest for France since December 2022. December power futures in both countries traded near €200, more than double a year earlier, and Britain's grid operator forecast a supply shortfall of about 1.4 GW. Higher gas prices had already pushed Germany's average October power price to about €171, more than double a year earlier.

2026-11-11-06.headline: CoreWeave's revenue jumps 168% to $3.66 billion and it raises its outlook, but its loss widens on interest costs
2026-11-11-06.soWhat: CoreWeave rents out Nvidia-powered computing capacity under multi-year contracts, so its backlog is a direct read on how much AI developers have committed to spend. The catch is financing: it borrows heavily to buy chips and build data centers before customers pay, so interest costs can wipe out operating profit even as sales soar. Rising Treasury yields make that model more expensive, which is why the stock had fallen so far. The open question is whether contracted revenue arrives fast enough to cover debt costs and $37 billion to $39 billion of planned capital spending this year.

sources.title: Yahoo Finance: CRWV stock climbs 8% after hours as $132B revenue backlog reinforces AI compute demand

2026-11-11-06.summary: AI cloud provider CoreWeave reported third-quarter revenue of $3.66 billion, up 168% from a year earlier and above the roughly $3.54 billion analysts expected. Its revenue backlog rose to about $132.5 billion from $104.2 billion at the end of June, and it raised its 2026 revenue forecast to $13.0 billion to $13.3 billion. Adjusted operating income was $379 million, a 10% margin, but the net loss widened to $709 million from $110 million as interest expense reached $846 million. The shares rose as much as 8% after hours, having fallen about 42% before the report.

2026-11-11-07.headline: TSMC's board approves up to $500 million each for stakes in Anthropic and OpenAI, plus about $41 billion of new capacity
2026-11-11-07.soWhat: The world's dominant contract chipmaker is taking small stakes in two of its largest indirect customers, the AI labs whose models run on chips TSMC makes for Nvidia, AMD, Google and others. The sums are tiny next to its capital budget, so the stakes are more about relationships and visibility into future demand than about financial return. The $41 billion approval shows TSMC still plans to add capacity despite the recent selloff in AI stocks. The open question is whether investors see these cross-investments as healthy partnerships or as a sign of circular financing in the AI supply chain.

sources.title: SEC: TSMC Form 6-K, board meeting resolutions, November 10, 2026
Everhint: Stock market news, November 10, 2026 evening update

2026-11-11-07.summary: TSMC's board approved buying up to $500 million of Anthropic common shares at its IPO price and up to $500 million of OpenAI preferred stock, along with up to $500 million to set up a separate vehicle for semiconductor and ecosystem investments. The same meeting approved about $40.9 billion of capital appropriations for advanced chipmaking, advanced packaging, specialty processes and new fabs. TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1,494 billion and net income of NT$763 billion, and approved a NT$9 cash dividend per share. Its Taipei shares rose 4.2% on the day.

2026-11-11-08.headline: SoftBank swings to a ¥1.1 trillion quarterly loss as AI stocks fall and a US data-center power plan is reworked
2026-11-11-08.soWhat: SoftBank is an investment holding company, so its profits swing with the market value of what it owns, and this quarter the AI selloff worked against it. It has also moved from investing in startups to financing physical AI infrastructure, which means borrowing, prepaying for equipment and taking losses when plans change. Higher interest rates make that strategy costlier: the yield on its bonds rose to about 8.2%. The open question is whether a successful round of AI listings, such as Anthropic's, lifts the value of private AI stakes like its holding in OpenAI.

sources.title: The Star (Reuters): SoftBank swings to US$7bil net loss in second quarter
Seoul Economic Daily: SoftBank posts $7.2 billion quarterly loss, first in two years

2026-11-11-08.summary: SoftBank Group posted a net loss of ¥1.1153 trillion, about $7 billion, for July to September, against a ¥2.5 trillion profit a year earlier and analyst expectations of a small profit. Falling share prices at holdings including Arm, Intel and Coupang hurt results, and SoftBank booked ¥597.2 billion of losses in the first half on advance payments after changing plans to supply power equipment to an Ohio data-center project. Financing costs reached ¥461.9 billion in the quarter, about 2.6 times a year earlier, after heavy borrowing. SoftBank has spent $64.6 billion on a 13% stake in OpenAI, and its shares have nearly halved since June.

2026-11-11-09.headline: Occidental beats forecasts and cuts debt to $10 billion, using high oil prices to repair its balance sheet
2026-11-11-09.soWhat: Occidental took on heavy debt to buy Anadarko in 2019 and CrownRock in 2024, and it is using this year's high prices to pay that down instead of expanding drilling. Lower debt cuts interest costs and makes the company safer if oil keeps falling from wartime highs, and management says it opens the way for larger shareholder returns. Its midstream unit earned far less than in the second quarter as the gap between West Texas and Gulf Coast gas prices narrowed. The open question is how quickly cash flow falls if Brent stays near $90 or lower.

sources.title: SEC: Occidental third quarter 2026 earnings release

2026-11-11-09.summary: Occidental reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of $1.91 a share, against a consensus of about $1.47, on production of 1,427 thousand barrels of oil equivalent a day, above the middle of its guidance. Its realized oil price was $85.91 a barrel, down 11% from the second quarter. It generated $2.8 billion of free cash flow before working capital and cut principal debt by $1.8 billion to $10.0 billion, bringing repayments this year to $10.4 billion. A third-party pipeline constraint cut Gulf of America volumes by about 24% from the prior quarter.

2026-11-11-10.headline: FDA approves Bayer's Sunharbo, the first factor XIa blood thinner, for secondary stroke prevention
2026-11-11-10.soWhat: Factor XIa drugs aim to prevent clots with less bleeding than existing blood thinners, a long-standing trade-off that has limited how widely they are used, so the class could become a multibillion-dollar market. Being first gives Bayer a lead over Bristol Myers Squibb and Johnson & Johnson's milvexian, which has had setbacks, and a partial replacement for Xarelto revenue lost to generics. Sunharbo failed in a key atrial fibrillation study, so for now it addresses a smaller group of patients. The open question is how fast insurers cover it and doctors beyond stroke specialists adopt it.

sources.title: BioPharma Dive: Bayer wins FDA approval for stroke prevention drug Sunharbo

2026-11-11-10.summary: The FDA approved Bayer's asundexian, sold as Sunharbo, for adults who have had a non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke or a high-risk warning stroke, taken alongside antiplatelet drugs. In the OCEANIC-STROKE trial of more than 12,000 adults it cut the risk of ischemic stroke by 26% versus placebo, with similar rates of major bleeding. The list price is $748.50 for a 30-day supply. Bayer's older blood thinner Xarelto faces generic competition, and its sales fell almost 43% to €738 million in the first half of 2026.

2026-11-11-11.headline: Vodafone raises its profit and cash outlook as Africa grows 13%, while Germany stays weak
2026-11-11-11.soWhat: Telecom is a high fixed-cost business, so small changes in revenue growth swing profits, and Vodafone's growth now comes mostly from African mobile money and data rather than Europe. Germany, its largest market, is still losing customers to rivals and faces a court ruling on 26 November about past price increases, so cost cuts are carrying the profit there. The UK merger with Three is starting to deliver savings. The open question is whether Germany can return to growth or whether Vodafone's European business keeps relying on cutting jobs.

sources.title: Investing.com: Vodafone H1 FY27 slides: guidance raised on 6.4% growth, Germany lags

2026-11-11-11.summary: Vodafone's group service revenue grew 5.8% organically in the six months to September, accelerating to 6.4% in the second quarter, and adjusted EBITDAaL rose 6.4% to €6.5 billion. It raised its full-year EBITDAaL forecast to €13.2 billion to €13.4 billion and adjusted free cash flow to €2.8 billion to €3.0 billion. Africa's service revenue rose 13.4% and now provides about 32% of group EBITDAaL, while Germany, about 33%, grew service revenue just 0.4% and lost 85,000 mobile contract customers in the quarter. Vodafone announced about 2,300 more job cuts in Germany on top of about 3,000 across Europe in the half.

2026-11-11-12.headline: Honda raises its annual profit forecast 20% on hybrids and a weaker yen, despite another ¥485 billion in EV costs
2026-11-11-12.soWhat: Japanese carmakers are being squeezed in China by local EV makers such as BYD, and Honda is responding by cutting EV spending and leaning on hybrids, which sell well in the US and earn better margins today. A weaker yen raises the value of overseas profits when converted back to yen, which helps cover the restructuring costs. The new Ohio plant moves more production into the US, reducing exposure to tariffs. The open question is whether pulling back on EVs leaves Honda behind if EV demand recovers later in the decade.

sources.title: CBT News (Reuters): Honda raises annual profit outlook 20% despite EV restructuring costs

2026-11-11-12.summary: Honda raised its forecast for operating profit in the year to March 2027 to ¥780 billion from ¥650 billion, though analysts had expected more. Operating profit for July to September fell 39% to ¥118 billion, well below the ¥250 billion analysts expected, after ¥484.8 billion of costs to restructure its electric-vehicle business. It cut its global vehicle sales forecast 7% to 3.16 million, mainly because of falling sales in China. Honda also plans a $3 billion assembly plant in Ohio that could build 240,000 vehicles a year from 2029.

2026-11-11-13.headline: Sea's revenue jumps 43% to $8.6 billion as Shopee and its Monee lending arm keep growing fast
2026-11-11-13.soWhat: Shopee earns more per order than a year ago because it charges sellers more for advertising, logistics and payment services, which is how e-commerce platforms turn scale into profit. Lending to the same shoppers and sellers through Monee is now growing even faster, and it carries credit risk that rises if Southeast Asian consumers come under strain. Rivals such as TikTok Shop and Lazada compete on price, which limits how far fees can rise. The open question is whether bad loans stay near 1.3% as the loan book grows 60% a year.

sources.title: SEC: Sea Limited third quarter 2026 results (Form 6-K)

2026-11-11-13.summary: Sea Limited, the Singapore owner of Shopee, reported third-quarter revenue of $8.6 billion, up 43.4%, and net income of $502.5 million, up 34%. Shopee's gross merchandise value rose 23.3% to $39.7 billion on 4.5 billion orders, and its adjusted EBITDA rose 44.7% to $269.2 million. Digital finance arm Monee grew revenue 63.9% to $1.6 billion, with $12.6 billion of loans outstanding, up 60%, and a 90-day non-performing loan ratio of 1.3%. The board approved another $1.0 billion share buyback.

2026-11-11-14.headline: TransDigm guides to about 14% sales growth in fiscal 2027 after a year of $4.4 billion in acquisitions
2026-11-11-14.soWhat: TransDigm buys makers of specialized aircraft parts that are often the only certified source, then raises prices, especially on spare parts sold to airlines for decades after a plane is delivered. That is why its margins are above 50%, far higher than aircraft makers, and why it keeps buying more such businesses with borrowed money. Airlines are flying older planes longer because new jets are late, which keeps aftermarket demand strong. The open question is whether defense right-to-repair rules or pricing scrutiny limit its pricing power.

sources.title: SEC: TransDigm fiscal 2026 fourth quarter results

2026-11-11-14.summary: Aircraft parts maker TransDigm reported fiscal fourth-quarter net sales of $2.99 billion, up 23%, and full-year sales of $10.56 billion, up 20%. Its EBITDA As Defined margin was 52.7% for the year. For fiscal 2027 it expects net sales of $11.95 billion to $12.15 billion, about 14% growth at the midpoint, with high single-digit growth in commercial aftermarket and defense. It spent about $4.4 billion on acquisitions in fiscal 2026, including Simmonds Precision Products and Prince & Izant.

2026-11-11-15.headline: JBS's quarterly EBITDA falls 36% as costly cattle squeeze beef margins in the US and Brazil
2026-11-11-15.soWhat: Beef packers buy live cattle and sell meat, so their margin is the spread between the two, and when herds are small, as in the US now, cattle prices rise faster than beef prices. Chicken grows in weeks rather than years, so poultry margins recover faster, which is why chicken is carrying JBS's profits. Shoppers pay more for beef while processors earn less, and ranchers capture most of the gain. The open question is how long the US cattle shortage lasts before herds are rebuilt.

sources.title: SEC: JBS third quarter 2026 earnings release

2026-11-11-15.summary: Meat processor JBS reported third-quarter net sales of $22.7 billion, up 1%, but adjusted EBITDA fell 36% to $1.18 billion, a 5.2% margin. Its North American beef business roughly broke even, while chicken units Seara and Pilgrim's Pride earned margins of 13.2% and 9.9%. Net income attributable to JBS fell to $164 million from $581 million, free cash flow was negative $167 million, and leverage rose to 3.54 times EBITDA from 2.39. Brazil was hurt by higher cattle prices and lower exports to China after a quota was filled.

2026-11-11-16.headline: Barrick files to list its North American gold mines as American Barrick Gold on the NYSE
2026-11-11-16.soWhat: Barrick is separating its lower-risk North American mines from operations in Africa and elsewhere because investors often pay higher valuations for gold mines in stable jurisdictions. With gold near $4,000, those mines earn wide margins, and a separate listing lets the market price them directly. Part of the proceeds will repay a note to Barrick, returning cash to the parent. The open question is whether the remaining Barrick, with more of its value in riskier countries, ends up trading at a deeper discount.

sources.title: SEC: American Barrick Gold Corp Form S-1
Eurasia Business News: Dow, Nasdaq, S&P 500 fall on November 10, 2026; oil and gold retreat

2026-11-11-16.summary: American Barrick Gold filed for a New York Stock Exchange IPO under the ticker ABGC, holding Barrick's 61.5% of Nevada Gold Mines and 60% of Pueblo Viejo in the Dominican Republic, with Newmont owning the rest of both. The business produced about 2.0 million attributable ounces of gold in 2025 and holds about 40 million ounces of reserves, roughly 20 years of output. It reported revenue of $7.26 billion for the six months to June. Barrick will keep a majority stake, and the filing does not yet give a size or price; gold fell about 2.6% to around $4,030 an ounce on Tuesday.

2026-11-12-01.headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia's CEO after a personal scandal, and CFO Colette Kress becomes interim chief
numbers: Close on Nov 11: $173.73, about 27% below the Oct 6 record
2026-11-12-01.soWhat: Huang co-founded Nvidia and led it for 33 years, so investors have treated his product and customer relationships as part of the company's value. The business itself does not change overnight: the board says customer commitments and the product roadmap continue, and quarterly results come as scheduled on November 17. The open question is whether a new leader can keep Nvidia's pace of yearly chip launches and its ties with hyperscale buyers, while rivals such as AMD and in-house chips at cloud companies try to take share during the transition.

2026-11-12-01.summary: Nvidia's board accepted Jensen Huang's resignation as president, CEO and director late on November 11, effective immediately, after reports of two personal relationships, one with an executive at Megaspeed, a large Singapore-based customer, whom US intelligence reportedly suspects of passing information to Beijing. Chief financial officer Colette Kress becomes interim CEO while keeping the CFO role, and former Synopsys CEO Harvey Jones becomes the company's first-ever board chair. The board will consider internal and external candidates for a permanent CEO. Nvidia shares had closed up about 2.9% at $173.73 on Wednesday, roughly 27% below their October record, then fell about 10% before Thursday's open.

2026-11-12-02.headline: Brent climbs back to about $93 after Trump says no Iran deal is needed, as OPEC keeps its weak 2026 demand forecast
numbers: OPEC 2027 demand growth: 2.55M b/d to 108.28M b/d
2026-11-12-02.soWhat: Oil now trades on two forces pulling in opposite directions: a war premium that rises and falls with every Iran headline, and a physical market where the war itself has cut demand. Stocks have been drawn down hard, which leaves little cushion if Hormuz flows are hit again, but returning Saudi and Iraqi barrels add supply quickly once tankers move. For producers, prices in the $85 to $95 range still support strong cash flow; for refiners and airlines, the swings make fuel costs hard to hedge. The open question is whether OPEC's 2027 rebound assumes a reopening of Gulf trade that has not yet happened.

sources.title: Oil prices jump after Trump says no Iran deal needed (CNBC)
OPEC forecasts 2027 global oil demand to hit 108.28 mb/d (allAfrica)

2026-11-12-02.summary: Brent crude rose about 0.5% to roughly $93 a barrel on Thursday morning after President Trump wrote that the US does not need a deal with Iran, cooling hopes of a quick end to the war that has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Brent had briefly slipped below $90 earlier in the week, and WTI is still down about 16% in November. OPEC's monthly report kept its forecasts unchanged: world demand grows just 180,000 barrels a day in 2026 to 105.72 million, far below the 1.4 million it expected before the war, then jumps 2.55 million in 2027. OPEC also estimates that global stocks fell 537 million barrels from February to end-September, while OPEC+ crude output rose 2.04 million barrels a day in October as Saudi Arabia and Iraq restored supply.

2026-11-12-03.headline: Poland's Orlen becomes the first buyer to cancel a long-term LNG contract with QatarEnergy, citing endless force majeure
2026-11-12-03.soWhat: Long-term LNG contracts work because buyers trust them more than the spot market; a prolonged force majeure breaks that trust and gives buyers a legal exit. Qatar supplied about a fifth of world LNG before the war, so if other European and Asian buyers follow Orlen, QatarEnergy could lose committed demand just as its large expansion is due. US exporters gain most, because they can offer new long-term volumes away from Hormuz. The open question is whether Asian buyers, who rely far more on Qatar, follow Orlen or wait for repairs.

sources.title: Poland's Orlen becomes first buyer to cancel QatarEnergy LNG contract (The National)

2026-11-12-03.summary: Orlen has terminated a 1 million tonne-a-year LNG supply contract with QatarEnergy, signed in 2009 and due to run to 2034, saying the seller's force majeure has gone on too long. Missile strikes in March damaged two of the 14 production trains at Qatar's main export plant, and QatarEnergy has extended force majeure month by month, most recently through the end of 2026. The oil-linked contract was worth an estimated €570 million ($637 million) this year. Orlen keeps a second Qatari contract of up to 1 million tonnes a year and has signed deals for US LNG from Port Arthur and Plaquemines.

2026-11-12-04.headline: OpenAI's quarterly revenue jumps about 50% to $10 billion, but its operating loss widens to $10.9 billion
2026-11-12-04.soWhat: The figures show that AI labs can grow revenue very fast, but the cost of computing power grows almost as fast, so scale alone has not produced profits. The shift toward enterprise customers matters because businesses sign larger, steadier contracts than consumers. The comparison with Anthropic, reported at about $17 billion of quarterly revenue and a small operating loss, sharpens the contrast as Anthropic prepares its IPO. The open question is how long investors keep funding losses of about $11 billion a quarter before demanding a path to profit.

sources.title: OpenAI posts $10B revenue in Q3 with $10.9B operating loss (Storyboard18)
OpenAI hits $10 billion in quarterly revenue (Yahoo Finance)

2026-11-12-04.summary: OpenAI's revenue rose nearly 50% from the prior quarter to about $10 billion in the third quarter, according to figures reported by the Wall Street Journal, its first quarter above $10 billion and an annual run rate of about $50 billion. Its adjusted operating loss widened to $10.9 billion from $10.1 billion, though the loss per dollar of revenue improved, with the operating margin moving from about -150% to -109%. Enterprise revenue doubled from the prior quarter and now roughly equals consumer revenue. ChatGPT has about 1.2 billion weekly users and more than 100 million paid subscriptions.

2026-11-12-05.headline: Siemens Energy reports a record year, a €164 billion backlog and a 2030 target of 20% to 22% margins
numbers: Profit margin before special items: 12.4% (2030 target 20-22%)
2026-11-12-05.soWhat: Demand for gas turbines and grid equipment has outrun factory capacity, because data centers, electrification and grid upgrades all need the same scarce gear. That gives makers like Siemens Energy and GE Vernova pricing power and multi-year order books, and it is why gas turbines now earn higher margins than wind. Utilities and data-center developers lose bargaining power and face waits of years for equipment. The open question is how long the boom lasts once new factory capacity comes online across the industry.

sources.title: Siemens Energy Q4 FY2026 earnings release

2026-11-12-05.summary: Siemens Energy's revenue rose 15.5% on a comparable basis to €44.2 billion in fiscal 2026, and orders rose 18.8% to €68.1 billion, leaving a record backlog of €164 billion. Profit before special items more than doubled to €5.5 billion, a 12.4% margin, and net income reached €4.1 billion. Gas Services grew 20% and Grid Technologies 26%, while the Siemens Gamesa wind unit reached break-even as planned. For fiscal 2027 it guides 14% to 16% revenue growth, and by 2030 it targets a profit margin of 20% to 22%, plus up to €9 billion of further share buybacks.

2026-11-12-06.headline: Siemens books a record €108 billion of orders on data-center and rail demand and plans to spin off its Healthineers stake
2026-11-12-06.soWhat: Data centers are lifting demand far beyond chips: they need switchgear, cooling controls and building automation, which is where Siemens' Smart Infrastructure arm sits. A book-to-bill of 1.30 means orders are arriving faster than Siemens can turn them into sales, which supports several years of growth. Spinning off Healthineers makes Siemens a purer industrial and software company, which investors usually value more clearly than a conglomerate. The open question is whether data-center orders stay this strong if AI spending slows.

sources.title: Siemens raises mid-term targets after record €108 billion in orders (MLQ)

2026-11-12-06.summary: Siemens' comparable orders rose 25% to a record €108.2 billion in fiscal 2026, and revenue grew 8% to €83.4 billion, with fourth-quarter orders up 58% to €34.8 billion helped by a €2.4 billion German high-speed train order. Smart Infrastructure, which supplies power and building systems, won many large data-center contracts and lifted full-year orders 34% to €31.4 billion. Free cash flow hit a record €12.1 billion, and the dividend rises to €5.50 a share. Siemens plans to hand its 34.1% stake in Siemens Healthineers to its own shareholders during fiscal 2027 and raised its mid-term growth target to 7% to 11% a year.

2026-11-12-07.headline: UK economy grows 0.7% in the third quarter, its fastest in more than two years, as AI and software work lift services
2026-11-12-07.soWhat: Stronger growth makes the Bank of England's job harder: it raised rates this month with inflation heading toward 5%, and a resilient economy removes a reason to stop. Growth concentrated in software and AI work helps tech services and commercial property in London, while construction and energy-heavy industries lag. The open question is whether the higher energy bills now feeding through to households slow consumer spending enough to bring growth down next year.

sources.title: UK economy grows 0.7 per cent as AI lifts business investment (City AM)

2026-11-12-07.summary: The UK economy grew 0.7% between July and September, up from 0.5% in the second quarter and about 1.9% higher than a year earlier, according to the Office for National Statistics. Services grew 0.9%, led by computer programming, which the ONS linked to AI and cloud businesses, while production rose 0.1% and construction fell 0.7%. September alone grew 0.2%, against forecasts of no growth. The Office for Budget Responsibility expects the energy shock from the Iran war to slow growth to about 1% in 2027.

2026-11-12-08.headline: RWE's nine-month earnings rise 35% on new wind and solar capacity and strong trading, pointing to the top of its 2026 range
2026-11-12-08.soWhat: RWE shows how a utility in transition earns money from both sides: new wind and solar farms add steady contracted profits, while gas plants and the trading desk profit when volatile prices, like this year's war-driven spikes, reward flexible supply. Sharing big offshore projects with partners such as KKR lets it keep building without stretching its balance sheet. The open question is how much of the trading windfall repeats once energy prices calm down.

sources.title: RWE delivers an excellent earnings performance in the first three quarters

2026-11-12-08.summary: RWE's adjusted EBITDA rose 35% to €4.6 billion in the first nine months of 2026, and adjusted earnings per share rose 42% to €2.52, about 85% of its full-year target. Onshore wind and solar earned €1.5 billion and offshore wind €1.1 billion, both up about 20%, while gas and other flexible plants rose 25% to €1.3 billion. Energy trading jumped to €543 million from €150 million and will beat its full-year range. RWE now expects results toward the top of its €5.75 billion to €6.35 billion EBITDA guidance, has 13.5 GW under construction and won German capacity contracts for 2.5 GW of new gas plants.

2026-11-12-09.headline: Lilly wins China's first approval for an oral GLP-1 weight-loss pill, getting ahead of Novo Nordisk
numbers: Chinese adults overweight or obese: more than half
Lilly China supply-chain investment: $3B over 10 years
2026-11-12-09.soWhat: A pill is cheaper to make and easier to ship than an injection, which matters in a market where patients pay themselves and where scale will depend on price. Being first gives Lilly time to build doctor habits and distribution before Novo's pill arrives, and Lilly has committed $3 billion over 10 years to supply chains in China. Local makers of GLP-1 drugs and copies of semaglutide are the main threat to both. The open question is what price Lilly sets, since self-paying patients limit how much it can charge.

sources.title: Lilly beats Novo to China with an oral GLP-1 for obesity (pharmaphorum)
Lilly becomes first drugmaker to have a GLP-1 weight-loss pill approved in China (Daily Guardian/Reuters)
Premarket movers: Nvidia sinks; Lilly gains on China approval (Investing.com)

2026-11-12-09.summary: China's drug regulator has approved Eli Lilly's orforglipron, sold as Foundayo in the US and UK, for weight management in adults with obesity or who are overweight with a related condition. It is the first oral GLP-1 weight-loss medicine approved in China; Novo Nordisk's oral Wegovy is still under review there, though Novo's injectable semaglutide has been sold in China since 2024. More than half of Chinese adults are overweight or obese, but weight-loss drugs are paid for out of pocket. Lilly shares rose about 3% before the US open.

2026-11-12-10.headline: Western Union walks away from its $500 million Intermex deal over California's conditions, and Intermex says it will fight
2026-11-12-10.soWhat: Remittances to Latin America are a scale business with thin margins, and the deal was meant to cut overlapping agent networks and costs. California's condition to keep every agent location blocks exactly those savings, which shows how state regulators can reshape a deal even after federal clearance. Digital players such as Remitly and Wise keep gaining share while the two incumbents are distracted. The open question is whether a court agrees that Western Union had the right to exit.

sources.title: Western Union Announces Termination of Agreement to Acquire Intermex
Western Union, Intermex clash (Payments Dive)

2026-11-12-10.summary: Western Union terminated its agreement to buy remittance company International Money Express (Intermex), announced in August 2025 for about $500 million, effective just after midnight on November 12. California's financial regulator issued final conditions on November 10 that included barring cuts to California agent locations and tougher anti-fraud measures, which Western Union said would force material changes to its business model. Every other jurisdiction, 54 in all, had approved the deal, and neither side owes a break fee. Intermex rejects the termination, says it expects the deal to close and has threatened legal action.

2026-11-12-11.headline: Marsh agrees to buy investment consultant Wilshire, adding $221 billion under management
2026-11-12-11.soWhat: Large insurance brokers are building investment businesses because advising pension plans and running outsourced portfolios earn steady, fee-based income that fits next to brokerage and consulting. Wilshire adds model portfolios sold through financial advisers and alternative-investment skills, the fastest-growing part of wealth management. Smaller investment consultants face rivals with more scale and data. The open question is whether clients stay through the change of ownership, since the deal needs their consent.

sources.title: Marsh to acquire Wilshire (Mercer newsroom)

2026-11-12-11.summary: Marsh agreed to acquire Wilshire, an investment consulting, portfolio and index-analytics firm, from private-equity owners Motive Partners and CC Capital; terms were not disclosed. Wilshire manages $221 billion and advises on $1.6 trillion for pension plans, endowments, foundations and wealth advisers. The deal is Marsh's third major investments move in 2026 after buying AltamarCAM in March, and it is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027.

2026-11-12-12.headline: Munich Re raises its 2026 profit target to €6.6 billion even as third-quarter profit dips
2026-11-12-12.soWhat: Reinsurers have enjoyed several years of high prices after heavy catastrophe losses, and a quiet loss year lets that pricing turn into record profits. Raising guidance late in the year signals that catastrophe losses have stayed below budget. The flip side is that strong profits attract new capital, which pushes reinsurance prices down at the January renewals. The open question is how much prices fall at those renewals.

sources.title: Munich Re Q3 net result declines (RTTNews)

2026-11-12-12.summary: Munich Re's third-quarter net result fell to €1.74 billion from €2.0 billion a year earlier, while insurance revenue rose to €16.6 billion from €14.6 billion. The reinsurer raised its full-year 2026 net profit guidance to €6.6 billion from an original target of €6.3 billion. For the first nine months, insurance revenue rose to €46.6 billion from €45.2 billion.

2026-11-12-13.headline: Corteva cuts its 2026 outlook as Brazilian farmers delay buying, and sales in Latin America fall 31%
2026-11-12-13.soWhat: Brazil is the largest crop-protection market in the world, and its farmers buy on credit against the next harvest. When interest rates are high and crop prices low, they buy later and in smaller amounts, and distributors run down their stock before ordering more. That hits sellers of seeds and crop chemicals, including Bayer and Syngenta, as well as Corteva. The open question is whether the weakness is a one-season timing shift or a longer squeeze on Brazilian farm income.

sources.title: Corteva swings to Q3 loss, cuts FY26 outlook (RTTNews)
Corteva cuts 2026 guidance after Brazil weakness (Basis Report)

2026-11-12-13.summary: Corteva's pro forma third-quarter sales fell 9% to $1.59 billion, with organic sales in Latin America down 31% while North America rose 7% and Europe, Middle East and Africa rose 14%. The company blamed weak Brazilian conditions, high distributor inventories and farmers' tight access to credit. It cut its 2026 guidance to adjusted pro forma operating EBITDA of $1.1 billion to $1.125 billion and EPS of $0.76 to $0.80. Shares fell about 8% after the results.

2026-11-12-14.headline: B&M shares jump about 17% as UK sales return to growth and the discounter issues its first full-year profit guidance
2026-11-12-14.soWhat: Discounters make money on high volumes and tight costs, so a return to positive like-for-like sales quickly lifts profit because store costs are largely fixed. Shoppers squeezed by higher energy bills tend to trade down to discounters, which helps B&M against mid-market general retailers. The open question is whether the UK recovery holds through Christmas, the quarter that decides the year.

sources.title: B&M European Value Retail reports revenue growth in H1 (Investing.com)
Why is B&M European Value Retail stock surging today? (Investing.com)

2026-11-12-14.summary: UK discount retailer B&M's first-half revenue rose 3.6% to £2.85 billion and pre-tax profit rose 16.6% to £121 million. UK like-for-like sales grew 3.2% in the second quarter after falling 2.3% in the first, and French like-for-like sales rose 6.5%. Gross margin improved by 0.67 points to 37.2%. B&M guided full-year adjusted pre-tax profit of £280 million to £330 million, and its shares rose about 16.6% to 325p.

2026-11-12-15.headline: Air freight rates hit their 2026 high as the holiday peak arrives, up 28% on a year ago
numbers: Baltic Air Freight Index: +6.6% w/w, 2026 high
2026-11-12-15.soWhat: Air cargo is priced by supply and demand for scarce space, so a rush of goods in a few weeks lifts rates fast, and falling fuel costs then widen carrier margins. Cargo airlines, airlines with large belly-cargo operations and freight forwarders gain; e-commerce sellers and shippers of high-value goods pay more. The open question is how much rates drop after the holiday peak, as they usually do in January.

sources.title: Airfreight rates reach 2026 high on peak season demand (Air Cargo News)

2026-11-12-15.summary: The Baltic Air Freight Index rose 6.6% in a week to its highest level of 2026, and rates are 28.2% above a year earlier, according to price agency TAC. Outbound rates from Hong Kong rose 4.6% in the week and from Shanghai 5.7%, while Frankfurt jumped 9.9%. Rates climbed even though jet fuel prices fell 6.5% in a week. Demand is being driven by shipments for Black Friday, Thanksgiving and Christmas, and by less belly space on transatlantic passenger flights in winter.

2026-11-13-01.headline: IEA says the oil market is swinging back to surplus in the fourth quarter as Gulf exports recover
numbers: Q4 2026 supply: ~105 mb/d, ~1.7 mb/d above demand
OPEC+ October crude output: 41.23 mb/d (97% of pre-war)
2026-11-13-01.soWhat: A surplus forecast from the main agency that tracks oil balances shifts the debate from scarcity to how fast inventories rebuild, which usually pulls futures prices lower over time and squeezes producers that budgeted for $90-plus oil. Consumers and airlines gain if the call is right, while high-cost producers and OPEC+ face pressure to restrain output again. The IEA also flagged that diesel supply remains very tight, so crude and fuel prices can move apart. The open question is whether shipping through Hormuz stays open long enough for the rebuild to happen.

sources.title: World oil market is returning to surplus as Gulf exports recover, IEA says (Reuters via CP24)
Oil Market Report - November 2026 (IEA)

2026-11-13-01.summary: The International Energy Agency's November report says world oil supply in the fourth quarter will average about 105 million barrels a day, roughly 1.7 million above demand, after it had earlier forecast a deficit. Gulf producers are rebuilding exports through the Strait of Hormuz, and OPEC+ pumped 41.23 million barrels a day of crude in October, up about 2 million from September and 97% of the pre-war level. The agency sees 2026 demand falling 2.7 million barrels a day to 102.3 million because of high prices, then rebounding by 2 million in 2027. It expects a 2027 surplus of about 3.8 million barrels a day, and Brent hovered near $96 after the report.

2026-11-13-02.headline: US 10-year Treasury yield climbs above 5.1% as producer prices rise 6.5% a year and Bank of America expects three Fed hikes
numbers: Fed hikes expected by BofA: Dec, Jan, Mar
2026-11-13-02.soWhat: When long-term borrowing costs rise above 5%, every other price in the economy adjusts: mortgages, corporate bonds and the discount rate investors apply to future profits. Highly valued growth stocks and rate-sensitive sectors such as housing and small companies tend to lose most, while savers and banks with lots of floating-rate assets gain. The shift from expected rate cuts to expected hikes also strengthens the dollar, which hurts US exporters and countries that borrow in dollars. The open question is whether inflation cools fast enough for the Fed to stop after one or two moves.

sources.title: Newsquawk European Market Wrap, 13 November 2026
Stock market news for Nov. 12, 2026 (CNBC)

2026-11-13-02.summary: US producer prices rose 0.3% in October, a little below forecasts, but were still up 6.5% from a year earlier, with core producer prices up 5.0%. A day earlier, consumer prices rose 0.4% in the month, and jobless claims stayed low at 200,000. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed to about 5.17% on Friday, its highest since mid-October, and the dollar rose past 160 yen. Bank of America now expects Federal Reserve rate hikes in December, January and March, and the S&P 500 fell 0.35% on Thursday.

2026-11-13-03.headline: SpaceX and Tesla could announce a merger as soon as December, in what would be the largest deal ever
2026-11-13-03.soWhat: Combining a rocket, satellite internet and AI business with a carmaker would create one company spanning launch, connectivity, robotics and vehicles, which supporters argue lets Tesla's factories and SpaceX's cash flow fund each other. The deal would dwarf the previous record, Vodafone's $183 billion purchase of Mannesmann in 2000. The obstacles are governance and regulation: Tesla's large China business sits awkwardly next to SpaceX's US defense work, and a change of control would speed up vesting of large stock awards. The open question is how many SpaceX shares Tesla investors would receive and whether they approve.

sources.title: SpaceX could announce $1.5 trillion Tesla merger in December: report (Electrek)

2026-11-13-03.summary: Bloomberg reported on November 12 that SpaceX and Tesla are negotiating price and control in a combination that could be announced as soon as December or slip into early 2027. SpaceX is valued at more than $1.9 trillion after its June listing and Tesla at about $1.5 trillion, and the talks describe SpaceX absorbing Tesla. Both boards have set up special committees, and Tesla's shareholder meeting is on December 3. Tesla shares rose as much as 1.9% on the report, and neither company commented.

2026-11-13-04.headline: Cisco's revenue jumps 24% to a record $18.5 billion as AI data-center networking sales climb 43%
2026-11-13-04.soWhat: AI data centers need huge amounts of networking to connect thousands of chips, and Cisco's numbers show that spending is now reaching the equipment makers that sit beside the chip suppliers. This is good news for networking and optics suppliers and a sign that cloud budgets are still growing, but it also makes Cisco more dependent on a handful of very large buyers. Services barely grew, so the mix is shifting toward hardware sales that can be lumpier. The open question is how long hyperscalers keep raising capital spending at this pace.

sources.title: Cisco Reports First Quarter Earnings (Cisco)

2026-11-13-04.summary: Cisco's fiscal first-quarter revenue rose 24% to $18.5 billion, with product revenue up 32% and services up just 1%. Networking, its largest unit, grew 43% to $11.1 billion as cloud providers bought switches and optics to link AI chips. Cisco now expects about $9 billion of AI infrastructure revenue from hyperscalers in fiscal 2027, more than double last year. It raised full-year revenue guidance to $74.8 billion to $75.8 billion and adjusted EPS to $5.47 to $5.53.

2026-11-13-05.headline: Hancock Whitney agrees to buy Trustmark for about $3.2 billion, creating a $58 billion Gulf South bank
2026-11-13-05.soWhat: Regional banks are merging to spread rising technology, compliance and deposit costs over a bigger base. Buying a neighbor in overlapping markets lets the acquirer close branches and back-office functions, which is where most of the earnings gain comes from. The price is about 7% dilution to tangible book value per share, which the bank expects to earn back in about 2.8 years. Larger regional players gain scale, while smaller community banks face a tougher competitor.

sources.title: Hancock Whitney and Trustmark merger press release (SEC 8-K)

2026-11-13-05.summary: Hancock Whitney will acquire Mississippi-based Trustmark in an all-stock deal valued at about $3.2 billion, issuing 0.7463 of its shares for each Trustmark share. The combined bank will have about $58 billion of assets across six Southeastern states, with Hancock Whitney holders owning about 65%. Trustmark had $19.1 billion of assets at the end of September. The deal is expected to add about 7% to Hancock Whitney's 2028 earnings per share and to close late in the first quarter of 2027.

2026-11-13-06.headline: Applied Materials posts a record $10.4 billion quarter and guides higher as chipmakers add AI capacity
2026-11-13-06.soWhat: Equipment makers are paid when chipmakers build new capacity, so their orders are an early read on how much the industry plans to produce. Strong guidance says that the AI buildout is now lifting spending on leading-edge logic and memory fabs, not only on the chips themselves. Equipment suppliers and their component vendors benefit, while chipmakers carry the cost and risk if demand cools. The open question is whether export limits on China, historically a large buyer of tools, cut into future growth.

sources.title: Applied Materials posts record $10.41B revenue (Crypto Briefing)

2026-11-13-06.summary: Applied Materials, the largest maker of chip manufacturing equipment, reported fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $10.41 billion and adjusted EPS of $4.16, both above forecasts. Its semiconductor systems unit brought in $8 billion, up 64% from a year earlier. Full-year revenue rose 21% to $34.45 billion. It guided next-quarter revenue to about $11.1 billion, above the roughly $10.9 billion analysts expected.

2026-11-13-07.headline: US diesel stocks fall to about 99 million barrels, near a 23-year low, keeping pump prices above $6
2026-11-13-07.soWhat: Refiners earn the gap between product and crude prices, so when crude eases but diesel stays scarce, that gap widens and refiners' profits rise. Truckers, farmers, railroads and anyone who ships goods pay more, which feeds into freight rates and food prices. Diesel is tight because Gulf exports of refined products were disrupted and some refining capacity is offline, problems that more crude does not fix quickly. The open question is whether stocks recover before winter heating demand peaks.

sources.title: America's diesel stockpiles are running low (24/7 Wall St.)
World oil market is returning to surplus, IEA says (Reuters via CP24)

2026-11-13-07.summary: US distillate inventories, which include diesel and heating oil, are about 99.3 million barrels, which would be the lowest comparable weekly level since May 2003. The national average diesel price is about $6.13 a gallon, up about 60% from a year earlier and about $2 more than gasoline. Refineries are running near capacity and strong overseas margins keep US exports high, so stocks are slow to rebuild. The IEA said on Friday that tight diesel supply remains its main concern even as crude moves into surplus.

2026-11-13-08.headline: Allianz lifts its 2026 profit goal to about €18.6 billion as asset management offsets higher catastrophe losses
2026-11-13-08.soWhat: Large insurers own asset managers partly because the two businesses are hit by different shocks: a bad catastrophe quarter in insurance can be offset by fee income when markets are strong. Allianz shows that diversification at work, which supports steadier earnings and dividends than a pure insurer. Higher catastrophe losses also tend to push up reinsurance and home insurance prices in the next renewal round. The open question is whether asset management fees hold up if bond and equity markets weaken.

sources.title: Allianz Results 3Q 2026 (Allianz)

2026-11-13-08.summary: Allianz's third-quarter operating profit rose 6.2% to €4.71 billion, beating the €4.30 billion analysts expected. Asset management, which includes PIMCO and Allianz Global Investors, earned a record €1.12 billion, up 35%, while property-casualty profit fell 7.9% to €2.20 billion. Natural catastrophes added 5.1 points to the loss ratio, against 0.3 points a year earlier, pushing the combined ratio to 93.8%. Allianz raised the top of its 2026 operating profit range to about €18.6 billion, and its Solvency II ratio was 219%.

2026-11-13-09.headline: Richemont's profit rises 39% to €2.5 billion on jewellery, but shares fall as growth misses hopes
2026-11-13-09.soWhat: In luxury, jewellery has become the most reliable growth engine because it holds value and is less exposed to fashion cycles than handbags or watches. Richemont, with about three quarters of sales from jewellery, has gained from that shift while many fashion groups have struggled. Its main risk is the cost of gold, which raises input costs, and demand from Chinese buyers. Investors now expect so much growth that even strong results can disappoint.

sources.title: Richemont: half-year net profit climbs to 2.5 billion euros (FashionUnited)
Newsquawk European Market Wrap, 13 November 2026

2026-11-13-09.summary: Richemont, owner of Cartier and Van Cleef & Arpels, said first-half sales rose 16% to nearly €12.3 billion and net profit rose 39% to €2.5 billion. Jewellery sales grew 18% to €9.1 billion, while watches grew 9% to €1.7 billion. Sales rose 30% in Japan and 23% in the Americas but fell 2% in the Middle East and Africa. The shares fell 4.2% on Friday as jewellery came in slightly below forecasts and comments on China and gold prices weighed.

2026-11-13-10.headline: US existing-home sales drop 5.5% to their slowest pace since 2010 as mortgage rates top 7%
2026-11-13-10.soWhat: Most homeowners locked in much lower mortgage rates, so higher rates freeze the market: owners do not want to sell and buyers cannot afford to buy. Fewer sales hit businesses paid per transaction, such as real estate brokers, mortgage lenders, title insurers and movers, even while prices hold up. Rising inventory hints that prices could start to soften if rates stay high. With markets now expecting Fed hikes, a quick rebound looks unlikely.

sources.title: Existing-Home Sales Decreased 5.5% in October (NAR)
October existing-home sales sink to 16-year low (RISMedia)

2026-11-13-10.summary: Sales of previously owned US homes fell 5.5% in October to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.75 million, the lowest since August 2010, the National Association of Realtors said. Sales were 8.8% lower than a year earlier and fell in every region, most in the West. The median price still rose 0.4% to $416,700, and inventory rose to 1.59 million homes, or 5.1 months of supply. NAR put the average 30-year mortgage rate at 7.33% in October, up from 6.86% in September.

2026-11-13-11.headline: Canada plans to invest C$200 million in Woodfibre LNG to raise the plant's capacity by up to 24%
numbers: Original capacity: 2.1 Mtpa, all to BP
2026-11-13-11.soWhat: Canada wants to sell more gas to Asia and Europe to reduce its dependence on US buyers, and Pacific coast plants have a shorter shipping route to Asia than US Gulf Coast terminals. Adding capacity to a plant already under construction is usually cheaper per tonne than building a new one, which improves project returns. Woodfibre's cost has risen to about US$8.8 billion from an early estimate of US$5.1 billion, so extra output helps spread that cost. Gas producers in western Canada gain a new outlet for their gas.

sources.title: Canada to invest C$200 million in Woodfibre LNG (Reuters via BOE Report)
Pension funds face mounting legal pressure over LNG bets (National Observer)

2026-11-13-11.summary: Canada's government plans to invest C$200 million (about US$140 million) in the Woodfibre LNG export plant being built near Squamish, British Columbia, Reuters reported, citing a source. The plant, owned by Enbridge and Pacific Energy, was designed for 2.1 million tonnes a year, all contracted to BP. Cooling upgrades and floating storage would lift capacity to 2.5 to 2.6 million tonnes, and the owners are exploring a second phase. Operations are targeted for late 2027.

2026-11-13-12.headline: Rolls-Royce keeps its profit outlook and brings forward a £1.5 billion buyback as data centers lift engine orders
2026-11-13-12.soWhat: Rolls-Royce earns most of its civil profit from long-term service contracts paid per hour an engine flies, so higher flying hours translate directly into cash. Its smaller Power Systems unit is now riding the same data-center wave as turbine makers, since operators want on-site generators when the grid cannot connect them quickly. Strong cash flow lets the company return money to shareholders while still investing. The risk is that long-haul flying slows or maintenance costs rise faster than expected.

sources.title: Rolls-Royce trading update: guidance on track, £1.5bn buyback (Hargreaves Lansdown)
Rolls-Royce speeds up share buybacks with £1.5 billion top-up (The Market Reporter)

2026-11-13-12.summary: Rolls-Royce reaffirmed 2026 guidance for underlying operating profit of £4.7 billion to £4.9 billion and free cash flow of £3.8 billion to £4.0 billion. It will buy back £1.5 billion of shares by February 2027, bringing forward part of its existing £7 billion to £9 billion program. Power Systems orders rose 62% in the first nine months and its backlog hit a record £8.6 billion, with gas engine orders for power generation nearly tripling on data-center demand. Engine flying hours in civil aerospace reached 114% of 2019 levels.

2026-11-13-13.headline: Nissan's quarterly operating profit falls 96% and it cuts its sales outlook again on China
2026-11-13-13.soWhat: Nissan shows how foreign carmakers are being squeezed in China, where local brands with cheaper electric models are taking share fast. Losing volume hurts because car plants have high fixed costs, so profit falls faster than sales. Nissan's answer is to design cars in China with local suppliers and export them to other markets, using China's cost advantage rather than fighting it. The open question is whether cost cuts arrive fast enough to hit the full-year target.

sources.title: Nissan cuts sales forecast again on China woes (CNBC)

2026-11-13-13.summary: Nissan's July-September operating profit fell 96% to 2.1 billion yen (about $13 million), far below the roughly 55 billion yen analysts expected, as a one-off US emissions benefit from a year earlier did not repeat. Revenue rose 8.2% to 3.1 trillion yen. Nissan cut its full-year sales forecast to 2.97 to 3.0 million vehicles from 3.15 million, its second cut since August, but kept its operating profit target. Its restructuring plan, which cuts 15% of the workforce, has saved 365 billion yen so far.

2026-11-13-14.headline: Hapag-Lloyd raises its 2026 profit outlook again as container freight rates climb 28%
2026-11-13-14.soWhat: Container shipping has high fixed costs, so small changes in freight rates swing profits sharply: here a 28% rise in average rates turned a thin quarter into a very strong one. Rates are high because Middle East disruption and weather have tied up ships and capacity, not because demand jumped. Carriers gain, while importers and retailers pay more to ship goods ahead of the holidays. The open question is how quickly rates fall once routes normalize and new ships arrive.

sources.title: Hapag-Lloyd profit jumps as stronger freight rates drive guidance upgrade (FreightWaves)

2026-11-13-14.summary: Hapag-Lloyd's third-quarter EBIT jumped to $1.09 billion from $228 million a year earlier, as its average freight rate rose to $1,808 per container from $1,413. Volumes were flat at 3.38 million containers, so the gain came almost entirely from price. The German carrier raised 2026 EBIT guidance to $2.0 billion to $2.4 billion from $1.25 billion to $1.75 billion, saying the fourth quarter is going better than expected. It warned that rates are volatile and geopolitics remain a risk.

2026-11-13-15.headline: Wizz Air's half-year profit falls 67% as fuel costs jump a third despite 26% more passengers
2026-11-13-15.soWhat: Low-cost airlines compete on price, so they struggle to pass higher fuel costs on to passengers and profits shrink fast when jet fuel spikes. Growing capacity quickly can also push fares down, which is what happened here as unit revenue fell. Hedging softens the blow but locks in prices for only part of the year. Airlines with more premium traffic and stronger pricing power, such as large network carriers, are better placed.

sources.title: Wizz Air profit falls 66.6% as costs rise (Airways)
Wizz Air's profit tumbles 67% on rising jet fuel prices (Bloomberg)

2026-11-13-15.summary: Wizz Air's net profit for the six months to September fell 66.6% to €108.1 million, even though revenue rose 13.8% to €3.80 billion and passengers rose 26.2% to 46.1 million. Fuel costs climbed 33.7% to €1.24 billion, and revenue per seat-kilometre fell 2.9% while total cost per seat-kilometre rose 4.3%. The budget airline has hedged 82% of its fuel for the second half and expects non-fuel unit costs to rise by a mid-single-digit percentage. It gave no full-year profit forecast.

2026-11-13-16.headline: Telefónica returns to a profit and cuts debt by €1.6 billion after selling Latin American units
2026-11-13-16.soWhat: European telecom operators have struggled for years with heavy network spending and price competition, so many are selling non-core countries to cut debt and focus on markets where they are large. Telefónica's exit from most of Spanish-speaking Latin America leaves it centered on Spain, Brazil, Germany and the UK. Stronger home-market growth and lower debt give it more room to invest or consolidate. The open question is whether European regulators allow the in-market mergers operators want.

sources.title: Telefónica gana 464 millones hasta septiembre (Infobae/EP)

2026-11-13-16.summary: Telefónica earned €464 million in the first nine months, against a €1.08 billion loss a year earlier, and profit from continuing operations rose 21.6% to €1.33 billion. Revenue rose 2.8% to €24.8 billion, and third-quarter revenue rose 4.8% to €8.43 billion. Spain revenue grew 2.5%, its fastest in more than 15 years. Net debt fell 10.8% to €25.2 billion, and the company raised several 2026 targets.

2026-11-13-17.headline: Paysafe shares sink about 24% after a quarterly miss, a $203 million write-down and a guidance cut
2026-11-13-17.soWhat: Payment processors earn small fees on very large volumes, so a dip in volumes or pricing plus heavy debt can quickly wipe out earnings. A goodwill write-down means past acquisitions are now worth less than was paid, a common problem for firms that grew by buying. Larger, less indebted rivals with broader merchant bases are better placed in this environment. Higher interest rates make indebted payment companies more vulnerable.

sources.title: Why is Paysafe stock plunging today? (Investing.com)

2026-11-13-17.summary: Payments firm Paysafe reported adjusted third-quarter EPS of $0.44, short of the $0.55 expected, on revenue of $439.6 million. It booked a $203.3 million goodwill impairment, and adjusted EBITDA fell 17% to $105.7 million. Paysafe cut its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $1.45 to $1.54 from $1.90 to $2.03, citing market and currency headwinds and higher interest costs after an August refinancing. The shares fell about 24% before the open, near a 52-week low.

2026-11-13-18.headline: Sonova raises its outlook as AI-powered hearing aids drive faster sales
2026-11-13-18.soWhat: Hearing aids are a concentrated market where a few manufacturers compete mainly on technology, and each new chip platform drives a wave of upgrades from existing users. When a platform sells well, revenue grows faster than costs, which is why profit guidance rose more than sales guidance. An aging population supports steady long-term demand. Rivals without a comparable AI product risk losing share until their next launch.

sources.title: Sonova raises full-year forecasts on market share gains (Reuters via SRN News)

2026-11-13-18.summary: Swiss hearing-aid maker Sonova raised its full-year guidance for local-currency sales growth to 6% to 8%, from 5% to 8%, and for core operating profit growth to 10% to 13%, from 7% to 10%. It also raised its forecast for global hearing-aid market growth in 2026 to 3% to 5%. Customers are moving quickly to its new AI-powered Phonak EON platform. Asia-Pacific sales rose 11.4% to CHF 186.9 million, and the shares are up about 36% this year.

2026-11-14-01.headline: Nvidia's board reportedly approaches Arm CEO Rene Haas to succeed Jensen Huang, and chip stocks slide
numbers: Nvidia weekly losing streak: 6, longest since 2012
2026-11-14-01.soWhat: Nvidia sells most of the world's AI accelerators and sets the product schedule that cloud providers, server makers and memory suppliers plan around, so who runs it matters for the whole AI supply chain. Haas worked at Nvidia for about seven years before joining Arm, whose CPU designs sit inside Nvidia's Grace and Vera platforms, but hiring him would leave Arm without its leader, which is why Arm fell. The sell-off in AMD, Broadcom and data-center stocks shows investors treating Nvidia's leadership gap as a risk for the whole sector. The open question is whether Tuesday's results and guidance convince customers that the roadmap is unchanged.

sources.title: Arm shares slide as Nvidia succession search puts CEO Rene Haas in spotlight (Yahoo Finance)
Closing Look, Friday, November 13, 2026 (CappNotes)

2026-11-14-01.summary: The Financial Times reported on Friday that Nvidia's board has approached Arm chief executive Rene Haas as a possible successor to Jensen Huang, who resigned as CEO on Thursday. Haas has not been offered the job and is one of several candidates, while finance chief Colette Kress serves as interim CEO. Arm shares fell about 5% to 6.5%, AMD dropped 8.75% and Broadcom about 4.8%, while Nvidia slipped 2% to about $163, its sixth weekly decline in a row and the longest such run since 2012. Nvidia reports quarterly results on Tuesday, November 17.

2026-11-14-02.headline: Brent ends a second weekly loss near $96 as surplus signs outweigh Iranian claims of tanker mine strikes
numbers: Gulf oil exports, Oct: 18.4 mb/d, 26% below pre-war
2026-11-14-02.soWhat: The market is now pricing oil off how fast Gulf supply rebuilds, not off the risk of new attacks, so unconfirmed mine claims add only a brief premium. Producers still earn far more than before the war, since Brent traded near $72 in late February, but a falling price trend matters for 2027 budgets, dividends and buybacks. Shipping costs stay high because much of the extra Gulf output moves under US naval escort or through costly ship-to-ship transfers in the Gulf of Oman. The open question is whether exports keep rising if mine incidents become frequent enough to deter tanker owners.

sources.title: Brent Crude Settles $95.84 After Second Weekly Loss on Supply Surplus (Gate)
Live updates: tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz, Iran says (CBS News)

2026-11-14-02.summary: Brent crude settled at $95.84 a barrel on Friday, up 2 cents on the day but down about 2.5% for the week, its second weekly loss in a row, while US benchmark WTI settled at $88.56. Prices fell over the week as OPEC+ raised October output, US crude and fuel stocks rose, and the US naval blockade of Iranian ports eased fears of renewed direct conflict. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said a ship carrying LNG hit a mine on Friday and three oil tankers struck mines overnight, claims that could not be verified; the US says it has cleared the main shipping routes. Gulf oil exports excluding Oman reached 18.4 million barrels a day in October, still 26% below pre-war levels, according to the IEA.

2026-11-14-03.headline: Fed officials push for a December rate hike, and the two-year Treasury yield jumps 35 basis points in a week
numbers: Two-year yield: ~4.87% (+35 bp on the week)
December hike odds: ~90% for 25 bp, ~10–12% for 50 bp
2026-11-14-03.soWhat: Short-term rates feed directly into what banks pay for deposits, what companies pay on floating-rate loans and what homebuyers pay on mortgages, so a Fed that is raising rates tightens conditions across the economy. A stronger dollar hurts US exporters and multinationals that convert foreign profits back into dollars, and it makes dollar-priced commodities such as gold and oil dearer for other buyers. Stocks still rose about 2.5% on the week, which suggests investors expect growth to hold up for now. The open question is how far the Fed will go while producer prices are still rising 6.5% a year.

sources.title: Market Review: November 13, 2026 (Investrade)
Closing Look, Friday, November 13, 2026 (CappNotes)

2026-11-14-03.summary: Several Federal Reserve officials backed tighter policy after this week's hot inflation data: Governor Christopher Waller supports at least a quarter-point hike in December and said a half-point move should be considered, Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan sees at least two more increases, and Boston Fed President Susan Collins said more tightening is warranted soon. October producer prices rose 0.3% on the month, slightly below forecasts, but were up 6.5% from a year earlier. The two-year Treasury yield ended Friday near 4.87%, up about 35 basis points on the week, its biggest weekly jump since September 2024, and the 10-year yield closed near 5.15%. The dollar index rose about 1% on the week to around 103.4, its highest since April 2025.

2026-11-14-04.headline: FTC sues to block Covetrus's $3.5 billion purchase of MWI, its closest rival in veterinary supply
numbers: Court: US District Court, Southern District of New York
2026-11-14-04.soWhat: Distributors sit between drug and supply makers and thousands of clinics, earning thin margins on very large volumes, so scale in warehouses, delivery routes and purchasing is the main way to raise profit. That is exactly why regulators object: when the two leaders combine, clinics lose the ability to play one against the other on prices and rebates. If the FTC wins, Cencora would have to keep MWI or find another buyer, and clinics would keep their bargaining leverage. The open question is whether a court accepts the FTC's view that manufacturers selling direct and online sellers do not discipline the two distributors.

sources.title: FTC Sues to Block Veterinary Supplies Distributor Covetrus's $3.5 Billion Acquisition of Rival MWI (FTC)

2026-11-14-04.summary: The Federal Trade Commission and 13 state attorneys general sued on November 13 in federal court in New York to stop Covetrus from buying MWI Veterinary Supply from Cencora for $3.5 billion. The agency says the two are the largest distributors of drugs, vaccines and supplies to US veterinary clinics and large corporate vet groups, and that the deal would let the combined firm raise costs for clinics, cut service quality and push up prices for pet owners. The complaint describes a price war between the two, intensified by the online price-comparison platform Vetcove. It also names Covetrus's private-equity owners, Clayton, Dubilier & Rice and TPG, as defendants; the Commission voted 2-0 to sue.

2026-11-14-05.headline: Samsung is in talks to buy data-center cooling maker Modine, whose shares jump about 28%
numbers: Data-center unit growth: ~86% a year over 3 years
2026-11-14-05.soWhat: AI chips run so hot that cooling has become a bottleneck in data-center construction, so liquid-cooling and heat-rejection equipment now commands premium prices and long order books. For Samsung, Modine would add a US manufacturing base and customer list to FläktGroup, making it a supplier of the building around the chips as well as the memory inside them. A deal at a high price would also set a valuation benchmark for other cooling and power-equipment makers such as Vertiv. The open question is whether a rival bidder enters, which would push the price higher.

sources.title: Samsung reportedly in talks to buy data centre cooling firm Modine (The Next Web)
Closing Look, Friday, November 13, 2026 (CappNotes)

2026-11-14-05.summary: Samsung Electronics is in talks to acquire Modine Manufacturing, a Wisconsin maker of cooling systems for data centers, Bloomberg reported; a deal could come within weeks, though no final decision has been made. Modine was worth about $5.6 billion before the report, and its shares rose about 28%. Modine spun off its automotive business in October to become a pure thermal-management company, and its data-center unit has grown about 86% a year over the past three fiscal years, according to Bloomberg Intelligence. Samsung bought German cooling specialist FläktGroup for €1.5 billion last year, and Daikin, LG Electronics and Vertiv are also chasing the market.

2026-11-14-06.headline: TVA signs a $1.7 billion upfront capacity deal with a data center, charging about $1.5 million per megawatt
2026-11-14-06.soWhat: The central fight in US power today is who pays for the plants and lines that data centers need, and TVA's charge makes the newcomer pay a large share upfront. That lowers the risk that a utility builds capacity for a project that later shrinks or disappears, leaving households to cover the cost. Utilities facing voter anger over bills now have a working example of the model. The trade-off is that steep upfront charges could steer some projects to regions with cheaper terms.

sources.title: TVA signs a $1.7 billion data center capacity deal under its new charge (MLQ.ai)

2026-11-14-06.summary: The Tennessee Valley Authority disclosed in its annual report, filed November 13, that it signed its first agreement under a new Capacity Commitment Charge with an unnamed data-center customer, worth $1.7 billion in total payments. The charge is about $1.5 million per megawatt of requested capacity above 5 megawatts, which implies roughly 1.1 gigawatts; $31 million is due at signing and the rest over 59 installments. TVA says the charge covers the extra capacity costs of large new loads and shields existing customers from rising rates. The federal utility's net income rose 56% to $2.12 billion in the year to September 30, on operating revenue of $14.22 billion.

2026-11-14-07.headline: Metro Bank puts itself up for sale after its turnaround, hiring Morgan Stanley to run the process
2026-11-14-07.soWhat: Mid-sized UK banks struggle to match the largest lenders on funding costs and technology spending, so mergers are the usual route to better returns. A buyer would get Metro's branch-based deposit base and a fast-growing commercial loan book, both slow and costly to build from scratch. By running a formal process instead of waiting for an approach, the board is testing what the franchise is worth while profits are at a record. The open question is whether a bidder will pay a premium for a turnaround that is still young.

sources.title: Metro Bank puts itself up for sale after turnaround (City A.M.)

2026-11-14-07.summary: UK lender Metro Bank launched a formal sale process on November 12 and invited offers for the whole company, with Morgan Stanley running the process. It said it is not in talks with any bidder and has received no approach, and that it will keep its standalone plan if no deal emerges. The bank has shifted toward commercial and specialist lending since 2023: pre-tax profit rose 41% to £60.7 million in the first half, its best half-year on record, and its core target lending book grew 43% to £6.2 billion. It targets a return on tangible equity above 15% in 2027 and 18% in 2028, and runs 78 UK branches.

2026-11-14-08.headline: Cerebras raises its 2026 sales outlook as AI cloud revenue jumps 265%, and its shares rise 11%
2026-11-14-08.soWhat: Cerebras is shifting from selling chips and systems to renting AI inference as a cloud service, which brings recurring revenue but needs heavy spending on data centers and power. A $26.1 billion contracted backlog against under $1 billion of annual revenue shows how much of the AI buildout is being locked in through long contracts with cloud providers and model makers. If it delivers, buyers gain an alternative to Nvidia hardware for running AI models. The open question is whether Cerebras can finance and power new capacity fast enough to turn that backlog into revenue.

sources.title: Cerebras Systems Q3 2026 results, Form 8-K (SEC)
Closing Look, Friday, November 13, 2026 (CappNotes)

2026-11-14-08.summary: AI chipmaker Cerebras Systems reported third-quarter revenue of $210.8 million, up 55% from a year earlier, as revenue from its cloud and services business rose 265% to $141.9 million while hardware sales fell to $68.9 million. It posted a GAAP net loss of $161.2 million but core net income of $29.8 million, and raised its 2026 core revenue forecast to $940 million to $960 million from $880 million to $890 million. Cerebras said it has secured 700 megawatts of data-center capacity for delivery by the end of 2027, holds $26.1 billion of remaining performance obligations and expects to triple revenue in 2027. Its shares rose about 11% on Friday.

2026-11-14-09.headline: Canada threatens to sue Stellantis over selling its idled Brampton plant after moving Jeep output to Illinois
numbers: Jeep Compass production: moved to Illinois
2026-11-14-09.soWhat: Governments offer carmakers large subsidies to win plants, usually tied to promises on output and jobs, and this case tests whether those promises can be enforced when trade rules change. US tariffs make it cheaper for automakers to build vehicles for American buyers inside the US than to import them from Canada, which pulls investment south. If Ottawa recovers far more than $24 million, carmakers will face tougher terms on future aid everywhere; if not, subsidy agreements lose credibility. The open question is how much of the support Canada can legally claw back.

sources.title: Canada threatens Stellantis as Trump trade war reshapes Jeep production plans (CNBC)
