2026-11-14-09.summary: Canada's government served Stellantis with a formal notice of default, giving it 30 days to address Ottawa's concerns or face legal action, Industry Minister Mélanie Joly said on Friday. The dispute follows Stellantis's agreement to sell its idled Brampton, Ontario, assembly plant to armored-vehicle maker Roshel, after it dropped plans to build the Jeep Compass there and moved that production to Illinois amid US tariffs. Joly said the company owes hundreds of millions of dollars, while Stellantis Canada said it would return $24 million in federal support. Prime Minister Mark Carney called the situation unacceptable.

2026-11-14-10.headline: Goldman Sachs downgrades European insurers and energy stocks, betting that bond yields and oil prices will fall
numbers: Banks: cut to neutral; energy to underweight
2026-11-14-10.soWhat: Insurers invest premiums in bonds until claims are paid, so higher yields lift the income they earn on that money, a big reason European insurers have rallied. If yields fall, new cash is reinvested at lower rates and that tailwind fades, even if underwriting stays profitable. Energy stocks face a similar reversal as oil drifts down from its war highs. The open question is whether European yields actually fall while the US Fed is still raising rates.

sources.title: Goldman Sachs lifts 12-month target for European stocks on energy price relief (Reuters via AOL)
Closing Look, Friday, November 13, 2026 (CappNotes)

2026-11-14-10.summary: Goldman Sachs cut its rating on European insurers to underweight and on banks to neutral, saying both groups tend to move with bond yields, which it expects to decline. It also downgraded European energy stocks to underweight, expecting lower energy earnings to weigh on profit growth in 2027. Goldman raised its 12-month target for the STOXX 600 to 700 from 695, about 5% above Thursday's level, and expects European earnings growth to slow to 7% in 2027 from 18% in 2026. The STOXX 600 ended Friday at 664.14, little changed on the day.

2026-11-14-11.headline: Gold has its worst week since early June, falling more than 4% as markets price in Fed rate hikes
2026-11-14-11.soWhat: Gold miners' profits move sharply with the gold price because their costs are largely fixed, so a sustained drop squeezes margins quickly after a record run. Higher interest rates raise the cost of holding a metal that earns nothing, which is why gold trades against expectations for the Fed. Silver has fallen much further than gold because it depends more on industrial demand and speculative buying. The open question is whether central banks and other long-term buyers step in at lower prices.

sources.title: Rate hike bets kept gold on track for its worst week in four months (CNBC)
Market Review: November 13, 2026 (Investrade)

2026-11-14-11.summary: Spot gold rose 0.6% to about $3,899 an ounce on Friday but lost more than 4% over the week, its worst week since early June, after touching a more-than-one-year low on Thursday. Higher oil prices and a hotter-than-expected consumer price report raised expectations of more Fed tightening, which weighs on gold because it pays no interest. Silver ended near $49.91 an ounce, about 59% below its January high, and platinum near $1,512, with both posting weekly losses. Futures put the chance of a quarter-point Fed hike in December at about 89%.

2026-11-14-12.headline: Bitcoin falls below $70,000 for the first time since August as Strategy prepares to leave MSCI's indexes
numbers: Strategy premium to its bitcoin (mNAV): ~1.08x vs 3.4x peak
2026-11-14-12.soWhat: Strategy's model relies on selling new shares at a premium to its bitcoin holdings and using the cash to buy more coins, so a shrinking premium weakens one of the steadiest sources of bitcoin demand. Index exclusion removes a group of automatic buyers of its shares and could narrow that premium further. Rising interest rates also hurt assets that pay no income, as gold showed this week. The open question is whether other index providers follow MSCI.

sources.title: MSCI is dropping Strategy from its index, and the exclusion could hit its bitcoin-buying machine (CoinDesk)
Closing Look, Friday, November 13, 2026 (CappNotes)

2026-11-14-12.summary: Bitcoin fell about 4% on Friday to around $68,000, below $70,000 for the first time since late August, and was heading for a sixth straight weekly decline. MSCI said this week it will remove Strategy, the largest corporate holder of bitcoin with 850,364 coins, from its global equity indexes after the close on November 30, under a new screen for non-operating companies. Strategy and BloFin Research estimate index funds will sell about 13 million shares, worth roughly $1.6 billion. Strategy's market value is now only about 1.08 times the value of its bitcoin, down from a peak of 3.4 times in November 2024, and its shares fell about 2.4% on Friday.

2026-11-14-13.headline: Lilly starts building a $3.5 billion Pennsylvania plant for next-generation obesity drugs
2026-11-14-13.soWhat: In obesity drugs, manufacturing capacity has mattered as much as the science, because shortages of injectable pens limited sales of the first wave of GLP-1 medicines. Building ahead of approval lets Lilly launch retatrutide at scale if regulators clear it, protecting its lead over Novo Nordisk. Domestic plants also shorten supply chains for its largest market. The cost is that billions are committed before the drug has been approved.

sources.title: Eli Lilly launches construction of $3.5bn manufacturing site (MarketScreener)

2026-11-14-13.summary: Eli Lilly began construction of a $3.5 billion manufacturing site in Pennsylvania's Lehigh Valley, part of a $50 billion plan to expand its US drug production. The plant will make injectable medicines and devices, mainly to raise output of next-generation obesity treatments such as retatrutide, which acts on three hormone receptors (GIP, GLP-1 and glucagon). It is one of 10 new US sites Lilly has announced since 2020 and is expected to create about 2,000 construction jobs and 850 permanent roles.

2026-11-14-14.headline: Asics shares fall 14%, the most since 2024, as it holds its profit forecast below expectations
2026-11-14-14.soWhat: Asics has grown from a running-shoe brand into a fashion and lifestyle name, and its faster-growing SportStyle and Onitsuka Tiger lines sell at higher prices. When a stock is priced for repeated upgrades, holding guidance steady reads as slowing momentum, even with sales up about 29%. Rising costs make it harder to turn that growth into profit. The open question is whether spinning off Onitsuka Tiger unlocks value or removes the group's fastest-growing brand.

sources.title: Asics shares down on Q3 report (Yahoo Finance)

2026-11-14-14.summary: Shares of Japanese sportswear maker Asics fell 14.3% to ¥4,180 in Tokyo on Friday, their steepest drop since August 2024, after third-quarter results disappointed investors. Cumulative net sales through the third quarter rose to ¥805.1 billion from ¥625 billion a year earlier, with SportStyle sales up 70% and Onitsuka Tiger up 34.6%. But Asics kept its full-year operating profit forecast at ¥195 billion, below the analyst average of about ¥199.7 billion. It also reaffirmed plans to spin off Onitsuka Tiger in January 2027.

2026-11-14-15.headline: Flowers Foods cuts its outlook again as bread volumes fall 7% under squeezed household budgets
2026-11-14-15.soWhat: Packaged bread is a mature, slow-growing category where profit depends on keeping bakeries and delivery routes full, so falling volume quickly hits margins. Price increases offset part of the decline, but each lost loaf spreads fixed bakery and route costs over fewer sales, while Flowers is spending more on marketing to defend its brands. The squeeze shows how exposed mid-priced food brands are when shoppers trim spending. The open question is whether the Nature's Own relaunch can stabilize volumes before deeper cost cuts are needed.

sources.title: Flowers Foods Q3 2026 results, Form 8-K exhibit (SEC)
Market Review: November 13, 2026 (Investrade)

2026-11-14-15.summary: Flowers Foods, maker of Nature's Own and Dave's Killer Bread, said third-quarter net sales fell 4.7% to $1.169 billion, as a 7.0% drop in volume outweighed a 2.3% gain from pricing and mix. Net income fell 63.6% to $14.4 million and adjusted EBITDA dropped 33.2% to $78.9 million, hit by lower volumes and higher marketing and logistics costs. The company cut its 2026 adjusted EPS forecast to $0.63 to $0.68 from $0.75 to $0.85, its second cut in a row, and its shares fell about 8% on Friday. Management cited pressure on household budgets and heavier promotions across the category.

2026-11-15-01.headline: Ukraine strikes another Russian refinery after hitting nine this month, and some Russian regions bring back fuel rationing
numbers: Russian refineries hit in November: 9 before Sunday (Bloomberg tally)
Their combined capacity: ~2.6M barrels/day, ~40% of Russia's total
2026-11-15-01.soWhat: These strikes hit the middle of the oil chain: Russia can still pump crude, but loses the ability to turn it into diesel and gasoline. That leaves less Russian diesel for export and more crude to sell abroad, which keeps fuel margins high for refiners elsewhere even while crude prices fall. Diesel users such as trucking firms and airlines bear the cost, with US diesel stocks already near a 23-year low. The open question is how fast Russia can repair the damaged primary units.

sources.title: Rigzone (Bloomberg): Ukraine hits 9th Russian oil refinery since start of November
Kyiv Independent: Ukraine strikes major Russian petrochemical and oil refining plants

2026-11-15-01.summary: Ukraine's General Staff said its drones hit the TAIF-NK refinery in Nizhnekamsk, Tatarstan, overnight on November 15, striking its only primary crude-processing unit, along with Sibur's Nizhnekamskneftekhim petrochemical plant. On Friday Ukraine hit Lukoil's Volgograd refinery, which has about 300,000 barrels a day of nameplate capacity, damaging four primary processing units, a hydrotreater, six storage tanks and a loading rack. Bloomberg counts nine Russian refineries hit since the start of November, including Omsk, the country's largest, with combined capacity of about 2.6 million barrels a day, roughly 40% of Russia's total. Some of the plants still run at reduced rates, and some Russian regions have reintroduced fuel rationing. The IEA expects Russian refining to be severely curtailed through year-end.

2026-11-15-02.headline: FDA rejects Summit's ivonescimab, delaying the first US approval of a PD-1xVEGF cancer drug
2026-11-15-02.soWhat: The FDA is asking new cancer drugs to show that patients live longer, not only that tumors grow more slowly, and that raises the cost and time for the whole PD-1xVEGF class, which many see as the next challenger to Merck's Keytruda. Developers with strong survival data gain relative value, while single-drug biotechs like Summit lose time and need more cash for new trials. Keytruda is approved in more than 40 uses, so any challenger needs many trials to compete broadly. The open question is whether trials in other lung cancer types show a clear survival benefit.

sources.title: BioSpace: Summit's PD-1xVEGF rejected by FDA in lung cancer
Fierce Pharma: FDA rejects Summit's ivonescimab

2026-11-15-02.summary: The FDA issued a complete response letter declining Summit Therapeutics' application for ivonescimab with chemotherapy in previously treated EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer, around its November 14 decision date. The agency said the Phase 3 HARMONi trial's gain in progression-free survival, without a statistically significant overall survival benefit, does not show a positive benefit-risk profile. Summit had shown the FDA updated data in September with a slight survival benefit in the global population. The drug comes from China's Akeso, which has sold it in China for this use since 2024. Analysts expect the PD-1xVEGF drug class to reach about $30 billion of sales by 2032, and Evaluate had forecast $4.4 billion for ivonescimab by 2030.

2026-11-15-03.headline: Microsoft restores Outlook and Teams after a global outage of more than 24 hours, one of its longest
2026-11-15-03.soWhat: Microsoft 365 bundles email, identity, security and AI tools, so one infrastructure fault stopped whole organizations, which Gartner described as concentration risk from a tightly coupled design. The outage strengthens the case for backup communication tools, multi-vendor setups and outage insurance, a modest opening for rival workplace software. Microsoft's shares closed flat, a sign that high switching costs keep customers in place even after a bad failure. The open question is whether large customers push for service credits or contract changes once Microsoft publishes its incident report.

sources.title: Reuters via Euronext: Microsoft restores service to Outlook and Teams after global outage
CIO Dive: Microsoft outage and enterprise resiliency

2026-11-15-03.summary: Microsoft said on Saturday, November 14, that its services had fully recovered from a global Microsoft 365 outage that began on Thursday afternoon and hit Exchange Online email, Outlook, Teams and the Copilot assistant. It blamed server issues tied to an earlier network capacity upgrade and ruled out a cyberattack or AI agents. Downdetector logged more than 7.4 million reports worldwide, peaking near 20,000 a minute. The disruption reached government bodies including the UK's NHS, exchange operator Euronext, Maersk and Indian airlines, and Richemont briefly delayed its results. Estimated insured losses are $300 million to $500 million, against $400 million to $1.5 billion for the 2024 CrowdStrike outage.

2026-11-15-04.headline: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet with Visa, Mastercard and Amex so its AI agents can pay for purchases
numbers: OpenAI cut of transactions at launch: 0%
Launch market: US Pro subscribers only
2026-11-15-04.soWhat: Agent shopping puts a new layer between shoppers and stores, and the card networks are moving early so that those purchases still run on their rails, using tokens to keep card data safe. For merchants, an agent that compares offers weakens brand loyalty and advertising, which is why Amazon blocks agents from buying on its site and United Airlines plans to block agent bookings. OpenAI gives up fees for now to build volume and trust. The open question is who carries fraud and dispute costs when an agent buys the wrong thing.

sources.title: CNBC: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet for dots purchases
gHacks: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet so agents can pay without seeing card details

2026-11-15-04.summary: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet on November 13, letting its "dots" personal agents buy items for users with stored cards. The card networks Visa, Mastercard and American Express issue a token for each approved purchase, so neither the agent nor the merchant sees the card number, and every purchase needs the user's approval. It starts with US ChatGPT Pro subscribers aged 18 or over. OpenAI is not taking a cut of transactions at launch, and cardholders keep their usual rewards and protections. ChatGPT has more than 1.2 billion weekly users and nearly 100 million paying users.

2026-11-15-05.headline: SpaceX catches a Starship upper stage returning from orbit for the first time, though the booster catch is aborted
2026-11-15-05.soWhat: Rockets are expensive mainly because most of the hardware is thrown away, so catching both stages would let SpaceX reuse the whole vehicle and cut the cost of each launch. Cheaper heavy launches matter most for Starlink, whose larger V3 satellites fly on Starship, and they put price pressure on rival launch firms. A working ship catch also strengthens SpaceX's hand as it discusses a merger with Tesla. The open question is how much refurbishment a caught ship needs before it can fly again.

sources.title: drohnen.de: Starship Flight 15, Ship 42 caught by the tower
Space.com: Starship Flight 15 aborts booster catch

2026-11-15-05.summary: Starship Flight 15 launched from Starbase, Texas, on Friday, November 13, and its upper stage, Ship 42, reached an orbit of about 275 km and deployed all 26 Starlink V3 satellites. After about 22.5 hours, the longest Starship flight so far, the launch tower's arms caught the ship on Saturday afternoon, the first time an upper stage has been recovered from orbit this way. The Super Heavy booster aborted its own tower catch after its guidance system flagged a problem and came down in the Gulf of Mexico. SpaceX is investigating the booster abort.

2026-11-15-06.headline: A nationwide FAA ground stop caused by network failure adds pressure for a $30 billion air traffic upgrade
numbers: Flights scheduled after 4 p.m. ET: ~11,000 (1.5M passengers)
Funding request: $30.1B, incl. $10.1B for air traffic control
2026-11-15-06.soWhat: Air traffic control is a government monopoly, so its failures land on airlines as lost revenue, crew overtime and rebooking costs they cannot avoid. The upgrade money is a large opportunity for telecom, radar and software contractors, but the GAO found in September that the FAA lacks a reliable cost estimate and an integrated schedule, a sign of execution risk. The open question is whether Congress approves the request and whether the FAA can finish the first phase by its December 2028 target.

sources.title: Reuters via AOL: US flight shutdown exposes deepening air traffic control problems

2026-11-15-06.summary: The FAA halted departures at US airports for more than four hours on Friday, November 13, after a communication failure hit all of its en-route air traffic control centers. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed overloaded switches and routers in the FAA's legacy network. More than 1.5 million passengers were booked on about 11,000 flights scheduled after 4 p.m. Eastern, according to Cirium, and it was the first nationwide ground stop since January 2023. The same day the administration asked Congress for $30.1 billion for airports and air traffic control, including $10.1 billion for modernization, on top of $12.5 billion approved in July 2025. A 2024 GAO report rated 51 of 138 air traffic systems unsustainable.

2026-11-15-07.headline: MSC nears a deal for about 80% of German cruise-ship builder Meyer Werft from the state
numbers: Possible signing: as early as Tuesday, Nov 17
2026-11-15-07.soWhat: For MSC, which also runs MSC Cruises, owning a shipyard brings a key supplier in house, giving it more control over building slots and costs for future ships. For Germany, the deal offers an exit from a rescue in which taxpayers took on most of the risk. Cruise shipbuilding is concentrated in a few European yards, including Fincantieri and Chantiers de l'Atlantique, so a yard tied to one cruise line may win fewer orders from rival lines. The open question is the price and whether the state attaches job or site guarantees.

sources.title: Investing.com via Yahoo Finance: MSC nears deal for 80% stake in German shipbuilder Meyer Werft, Spiegel reports

2026-11-15-07.summary: Swiss shipping group MSC is close to securing the right to buy about 80% of Meyer Werft, Der Spiegel reported on Saturday, November 14, and an agreement could be signed as early as Tuesday. The stake is held by Germany's federal government and the state of Lower Saxony, about 40% each, after they rescued the Papenburg shipyard at the end of 2024 with €400 million of equity. The Meyer family, which founded the business in 1795, keeps the other 20% and is working with MSC on a joint ownership setup that could let it raise its stake. No price was reported.

2026-11-15-08.headline: COP31's first week ends split on fossil fuels, as host Turkey pushes for 35% of energy use to be electric by 2035
numbers: Proposed target: electricity at 35% of energy use by 2035
Electricity's share today: a little over 20%
2026-11-15-08.soWhat: A global electrification goal would shift investment from fuel supply toward power generation, grids and electric equipment, which favors utilities, grid suppliers and makers of heat pumps and electric vehicles over fuel sellers. With the US absent and oil producers resisting, any deal is likely to be voluntary, so companies will take their signals from national policies more than from the summit text. The open question is whether the final text mentions fossil fuels at all.

sources.title: The Open Press: COP31 first week ends deadlocked on fossil fuels
US News (Reuters): COP31 talks face early friction over future of fossil fuels

2026-11-15-08.summary: The UN climate talks in Antalya entered their final week with large fossil fuel producers and consumers resisting firm new targets or language on moving away from oil, gas and coal. Host Turkey wants electricity to supply 35% of world energy use by 2035, up from a little over a fifth now, and European leaders back the idea. The COP31 presidency published options for the final decision on Friday, and lead negotiator Australia plans a draft text early next week. Saudi Arabia and Russia traditionally resist limits on fossil fuels, India opposes steps it says could limit development, and the United States, the largest oil consumer, is skipping the talks for a second year.

2026-11-15-09.headline: Jensen Huang's exit leaves a gap in AI startup funding, where Nvidia joined 105 rounds this year
2026-11-15-09.soWhat: Nvidia's investments worked partly like vendor financing: money went to cloud and model startups that then bought Nvidia chips, supporting both its sales and those startups' valuations. A pullback would raise the cost of capital for smaller AI clouds and open-weight model makers and could slow some GPU orders. It also gives rival chipmakers and Big Tech an opening to win customers with their own funding. The open question is whether Nvidia's next CEO keeps investing as a sales tool or cuts it back as a risk.

sources.title: TechCrunch: Jensen Huang's departure blasts big hole in AI startup funding

2026-11-15-09.summary: Nvidia took part in 105 startup funding rounds in 2026, often as the largest investor, according to PitchBook data cited by TechCrunch. Its bets included CoreWeave before its listing, Crusoe's $1.4 billion Series E and an $800 million check into Reflection AI, and it agreed to buy Hugging Face for $13 billion, a deal expected to close in 2027. Founders and venture investors say most big investment decisions came from Jensen Huang, and expect interim CEO Colette Kress to be more selective and write smaller checks. One investor said infrastructure startups needing $100 million to $500 million of GPUs often raised about half of that from Nvidia.

2026-11-15-10.headline: China's higher foreign-currency reserve rule for banks takes effect as Beijing leans against a rising yuan
numbers: Yuan fixing after the announcement: ~6.71 per dollar
China October activity data: due Nov 16
2026-11-15-10.soWhat: A rapidly rising yuan cuts what Chinese exporters earn when they convert dollar sales into yuan, at a time when exports are carrying China's growth. Raising the reserve ratio is a mild brake that signals Beijing wants a slower climb rather than a reversal. For foreign companies, a firm yuan makes selling into China cheaper and makes Chinese goods slightly less competitive abroad. The open question is what Monday's data show about domestic demand.

sources.title: investingLive: China's PBOC lifts FX reserve ratio to 6%
Yicai Global: China's forex RRR hike to likely freeze foreign currency liquidity

2026-11-15-10.summary: From November 15, Chinese banks must hold 6% of their foreign-currency deposits as reserves, up from 4%, the first increase since December 2021. The People's Bank of China says the move strengthens management of foreign-exchange liquidity, and markets read it as an effort to slow the yuan's gains by making dollars scarcer onshore. After the announcement the central bank set its daily rate near 6.71 yuan per dollar, weaker than the roughly 6.66 analysts expected. Earlier in 2026 it cut its risk reserve on forward currency sales to zero, also to cool appreciation. China's October output and retail sales data are due on Monday, November 16.

2026-11-16-01.headline: Anthropic enters its IPO week with orders reportedly six times the shares on offer, as AI stocks slide
numbers: Valuation at top of range: ~$1.4 trillion fully diluted
Early demand: ~6x the shares on offer (Bloomberg)
2026-11-16-01.soWhat: An IPO this size is a price-discovery event for the whole AI industry. If public investors pay up for a model maker that sells mainly to businesses, it supports the spending of cloud and chip suppliers whose growth depends on companies like Anthropic. A weak debut would make it harder for other AI labs to raise money and could slow orders down the chain. The open question is whether strong order books hold if Nvidia's results on Tuesday disappoint.

sources.title: CNBC: Anthropic IPO guide: the price range, date and more
Startup Fortune: Anthropic's $64 billion IPO lands in the middle of an AI selloff
ABC News: ASX business live, 16 November 2026

2026-11-16-01.summary: Anthropic plans to price its Nasdaq listing on Wednesday, November 18, and start trading under the ticker ANT on Thursday. It is selling 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each, which would raise up to about $64 billion and value the company at about $1.4 trillion on a fully diluted basis. Bloomberg reported that early orders were about six times the shares available, and up to 20% of the offering can go to retail investors. The deal lands in a weak market: the Nasdaq fell 5.5% the week before the roadshow, and Nvidia, which reports on Tuesday, has lost about a third of its value since early October.

2026-11-16-02.headline: Diamondback buys the 40% of its Double Eagle Midland Basin partnership it did not own, for $2.15 billion plus stock
numbers: Net acres: ~176,000 in the Midland Basin
2026-11-16-02.soWhat: US shale growth now comes mostly from buying, not from finding new rock. Diamondback already operates these acres, so it gets more oil and a deeper list of future wells without adding a rig, which keeps costs flat while cash flow rises. Paying about 4 times EBITDA is cheap if oil stays near $90, but the stock portion shares that oil-price risk with the sellers. The open question is how the inventory looks if Brent falls toward the $78 that some banks forecast for late 2027.

sources.title: Diamondback Energy press release via Manila Times/GlobeNewswire: Core Midland Basin acquisition
Crypto Briefing: Diamondback Energy to acquire Double Eagle assets

2026-11-16-02.summary: Diamondback Energy agreed to buy subsidiaries of Double Eagle IV and Double Eagle V, giving it full ownership of a partnership on about 176,000 net acres in the core of the Midland Basin in West Texas. It will pay $2.15 billion in cash plus about 15.56 million of its own shares, valuing the deal at about 4.0 times expected 2027 EBITDA. The assets should produce about 35,000 barrels of oil a day in 2027 (92,000 barrels of oil equivalent including gas) and include more than 1,200 gross drilling locations, 68% of them undeveloped. The deal is expected to close on December 21.

2026-11-16-03.headline: Japan's economy shrinks at a 0.1% annual pace in the third quarter as costly oil and a weak yen hit consumers
2026-11-16-03.soWhat: Japan imports almost all its oil, so the Gulf conflict works like a tax on its households and a transfer to energy exporters. A weak yen makes it worse by raising the cost of every imported barrel and every ton of food. Companies building data centers and automation are still spending, so the split is between strong corporate investment and squeezed consumers. The open question is whether the government's proposed food tax cut passes, given worries about public debt.

sources.title: AP via KSAT: Japan's economy contracts slightly as oil prices remain high
BigGo Finance: Japan's July-September GDP falls 0.1% annualized

2026-11-16-03.summary: Japan's real GDP fell at an annualized 0.1% in July to September, its first contraction in four quarters, against a forecast of 0.3% growth. Private consumption, more than half of the economy, fell at an annualized 1.1% as prices rose and bad weather kept shoppers home. Net exports subtracted 0.6 percentage point because the import bill jumped with oil prices. Business investment held up, rising at an annualized 6.8% on digital and data-center spending, while the dollar trades near 160 yen.

2026-11-16-04.headline: J&J agrees to buy eye-disease biotech Ollin for $2.2 billion upfront, with Blackstone paying for late-stage trials
numbers: Total with milestones: up to ~$3.3 billion
2026-11-16-04.soWhat: Retinal disease drugs are a large, recurring market because patients need injections for years, so a drug that works faster or needs fewer injections can take share from Roche and Regeneron. The Blackstone deal shows how big drugmakers now share development risk: J&J keeps the upside but moves part of the Phase 3 cost off its books in return for royalties. The open question is whether the early advantage over Vabysmo holds in larger trials.

sources.title: CNBC: J&J to buy eye disease biotech Ollin Biosciences for up to $3.3 billion
CNBC: Stocks making the biggest moves, November 16

2026-11-16-04.summary: Johnson & Johnson will pay $2.2 billion upfront for Ollin Biosciences, plus up to about $1.13 billion in milestone payments, for a total of up to about $3.3 billion. Ollin's lead drug, OLN324, is an antibody that blocks two drivers of retinal disease (VEGF and Ang2) and is entering global Phase 3 trials in wet macular degeneration and diabetic macular edema. In a 164-patient study it showed faster and larger improvements than Roche's Vabysmo, the market leader. Blackstone Life Sciences will give J&J $750 million over several years to fund the late-stage trials in exchange for future payments and royalties. J&J shares rose 1.4%.

2026-11-16-05.headline: China's October data miss forecasts, with retail sales up just 0.4% and investment down 8.1% this year
2026-11-16-05.soWhat: China is producing far more than its own consumers buy, so the gap is filled by exports. That keeps pressure on factory prices worldwide and invites more trade defenses, with Citi expecting further EU measures. Weak domestic demand also hurts sellers of commodities, cars and consumer brands that rely on Chinese shoppers. The open question is whether Beijing adds stimulus before the year ends; some economists expect it will not.

sources.title: CNBC: China's slowdown deepens in October
InvestingLive: China factory output slows to 4.8% in October

2026-11-16-05.summary: China's retail sales rose 0.4% from a year earlier in October, below the 0.8% expected and down from 1.1% in September. Industrial output grew 4.8%, short of the 5.3% forecast. Fixed-asset investment fell 8.1% in the first ten months, worse than the expected 7% drop, and unemployment edged down to 5.1%. Exports remain strong on demand for AI hardware, but households are cutting back, and Goldman Sachs expects growth to slow to 4.6% this year.

2026-11-16-06.headline: Canadian Natural agrees to buy Montney gas producer Advantage Energy for about C$2.5 billion
2026-11-16-06.soWhat: Canadian Natural is buying gas next to land it already runs, so it can share plants, roads and crews and cut the cost per unit. Western Canadian gas is gaining value as new LNG export plants on the Pacific coast give it a route to Asian buyers, at a time when Gulf LNG supply is disrupted. For smaller producers, the premium shows that scale buyers will pay for well-run infrastructure. The open question is whether competition authorities approve and whether Canadian gas prices hold up as LNG capacity ramps.

sources.title: Advantage Energy release via BOE Report: Agreement to be acquired by Canadian Natural
Rallies.ai: Canadian Natural agrees to acquire Advantage Energy for $2.53 billion

2026-11-16-06.summary: Canadian Natural Resources will pay C$13.55 a share in cash for Advantage Energy, a 25% premium to Friday's close. Including debt and convertible debentures, the deal is worth about C$2.53 billion. Advantage produced about 87,000 barrels of oil equivalent a day in the third quarter, mostly natural gas, from Montney and Charlie Lake land in Alberta next to Canadian Natural's own operations. It owns the 425 million cubic feet a day Glacier gas plant and a new 75 million cubic feet a day plant. Closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027.

2026-11-16-07.headline: Blackstone's data-center trust buys 75% of 13 new AWS-leased campuses valued at $5 billion
numbers: Lease: 12 years + two 10-year options, 2.75% annual increases
2026-11-16-07.soWhat: Cloud companies are selling stakes in finished data centers so they can recycle cash into the next buildings and chips. Investors get long, inflation-linked rent from a top-rated tenant, which looks like a bond with a property attached. That turns AI infrastructure into a real-estate asset class open to income funds. The open question is how the trust funds the purchase and whether a 7% starting yield is enough if bond yields stay above 5%.

sources.title: Mugglehead: Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust agrees to US$5B deal

2026-11-16-07.summary: Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust (BXDC) agreed to buy a 75.1% stake in two data-center campuses in northern Indiana and Mississippi, valued at $5 billion including costs. The 13 buildings were completed this year and have 647 megawatts of capacity. They are leased to Amazon Web Services for 12 years, with two 10-year renewal options, rent rising 2.75% a year, and a starting yield of about 7%. Financing has not yet been disclosed.

2026-11-16-08.headline: L3Harris shares fall 4% after the US Transportation Secretary blames its network work for Friday's nationwide flight halt
numbers: Top-6 airline cancellation rate: 32% Fri, 30% Sat
2026-11-16-08.soWhat: The FAA does not own the network that carries air traffic data; it rents it from a contractor, so one company's error can stop the whole country. Government services contracts are usually steady earners, but a high-profile failure can cost a contractor future work and invite penalties. Airlines bear the immediate cost in refunds, crew overtime and lost tickets. The open question is whether Congress funds a replacement network and who wins that contract.

sources.title: CNBC: Stocks making the biggest moves, November 16
Fox Business: Sean Duffy says L3Harris work may have caused FAA nationwide ground stop

2026-11-16-08.summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said maintenance by L3Harris, which owns and runs the FAA's telecom network, likely caused Friday's nationwide ground stop of nearly five hours. He said a router at a remote site, where L3Harris was switching copper lines to fiber, flooded the network with data and the failure spread nationwide; investigators have not decided whether it was installation error or faulty equipment. Cancellation rates at the six largest US airlines reached 32% on Friday and 30% on Saturday, according to FlightAware data analyzed by UBS. Duffy asked Congress for $50 billion to overhaul the system, and airline shares fell more than 1%.

2026-11-16-09.headline: China's refineries cut runs 8% from a year ago as crude piles up in storage, and Brent slips to about $95
numbers: China refinery runs: -8.1% y/y in October
2026-11-16-09.soWhat: The world's largest crude importer is processing less and storing more, which means weaker demand for fuel at home and less need for new cargoes. For refiners elsewhere, fewer Chinese fuel exports help margins, while producers face a softer market. China's stockpiling also acts as a buffer that can cap prices if Gulf flows improve. The open question is whether new tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz reverse the slide.

sources.title: CNBC: Oil falls as recovering Middle East exports bolster surplus outlook
ABC News: ASX business live, 16 November 2026

2026-11-16-09.summary: Chinese refinery throughput fell 2% from September and 8.1% from a year earlier in October, while crude inventories grew by about 492,000 barrels a day, according to Reuters calculations. Brent fell 0.7% to $95.15 a barrel on Monday and WTI to $88.19, after both dropped more than 13% last week. The IEA now expects fourth-quarter supply of 105 million barrels a day, 1.7 million above demand, as Gulf exports recover despite reported tanker mine strikes. Goldman Sachs expects Brent to average $88 in 2027.

2026-11-16-10.headline: European gas falls below €90 per MWh, but storage is only about 71% full as winter starts
numbers: Gulf LNG disrupted: ~1/5 of global exports
2026-11-16-10.soWhat: Low storage means Europe will depend on spot LNG cargoes all winter, which gives sellers with flexible supply, mostly US exporters and traders, strong pricing power. Gas plants set the power price in many hours, so gas costs flow straight into electricity bills and industrial costs for chemicals and steel makers. The open question is how cold the winter gets, since a long cold spell could drain storage fast.

sources.title: Trading Economics: European natural gas prices drop further

2026-11-16-10.summary: Europe's benchmark TTF gas price fell below €90 per megawatt-hour on Monday, extending Friday's losses after a week of gains. EU storage is about 70.6% full, against a five-year average of 89% for this time of year, and Germany's is about 57%. The Gulf conflict has disrupted nearly a fifth of global LNG exports, so Europe is competing with Asia for cargoes, and outages at Norway's Troll and Asgard fields have cut pipeline supply. Colder weather is forecast from November 17.

2026-11-16-11.headline: Lilly makes its 15th acquisition of the year, buying blood-cancer startup Calytrix for up to $1.5 billion
2026-11-16-11.soWhat: Lilly is using cash from its obesity drugs to buy early-stage science, paying mostly on milestones so it pays in full only if the drug works. Private biotechs and their venture backers gain a ready buyer, which supports funding for new startups. A drug that targets the mutation itself, rather than easing symptoms, could change how these blood cancers are treated. The open question is whether the antibody works in patients, since it has not yet shown clinical data.

sources.title: Yahoo Finance: Lilly adds to buyout streak with $1.5B purchase of Calytrix
Bloomberg: Eli Lilly to acquire Calytrix Bio in deal worth up to $1.5 billion

2026-11-16-11.summary: Eli Lilly agreed to buy Calytrix Bio, a private biotech in Wellesley, Massachusetts, for up to $1.5 billion in cash, including an undisclosed upfront payment and milestone payments. Calytrix is developing an antibody that targets a protein made by mutations in the CALR gene, which drive myelofibrosis and essential thrombocythemia, two slow-growing blood cancers. Including this deal, Lilly has spent more than $30 billion on 15 acquisitions this year, mostly private startups. It follows Lilly's $2.3 billion purchase of Ajax Therapeutics in the same disease area.

2026-11-16-12.headline: Aramark guides 20% to 25% EPS growth after record contract wins, but shares fall 5% on a fourth-quarter miss
2026-11-16-12.soWhat: Contract caterers earn thin margins on each meal but make money from scale and long contracts with schools, hospitals, stadiums and offices. High retention and new wins matter more than any single quarter, because each contract runs for years. Rising food and labor costs are the main risk, since prices can only be reset at contract renewals. The open question is whether profit grows as fast as revenue as new contracts start up.

sources.title: Aramark Q4 fiscal 2026 results (SEC exhibit 99.1)
CNBC: Stocks making the biggest moves, November 16

2026-11-16-12.summary: Food and facilities services company Aramark reported fourth-quarter revenue of $5.3 billion, up 5%, or 12% organically after adjusting for an extra week a year earlier. Adjusted EPS of $0.71 rose 25% but missed the $0.75 analysts expected. For the year, revenue rose 9% to $20.1 billion, it won a record $1.9 billion of annual new business, and client retention reached about 97%. It expects fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS to grow 20% to 25%, raised its dividend 17% and approved a $1 billion buyback.

2026-11-16-13.headline: Take-Two rises as Jefferies says GTA VI pre-orders point to the top of a 40-50 million unit range ahead of Thursday's launch
2026-11-16-13.soWhat: A blockbuster game has very high upfront costs and very low costs for each extra copy, so sales beyond break-even are almost pure profit. The bigger prize is the online mode that follows, where players keep spending on in-game items for years. Other publishers may delay their own releases to avoid competing for players' time and money. The open question is how well sales hold after launch week, which the company has said it will report once it has data.

sources.title: CNBC: Stocks making the biggest moves, November 16
Investing.com: Take-Two shares rise premarket as Jefferies sees strong GTA VI pre-orders

2026-11-16-13.summary: Take-Two Interactive shares rose more than 3% on Monday ahead of the November 19 release of Grand Theft Auto VI. Jefferies said pre-orders are pushing first-year unit sales toward the top of its 40 million to 50 million range and kept its $300 price target. Take-Two said on November 9 that pre-orders were running far above its initial expectations. The standard edition costs $79.99, and the company expects $8 billion to $8.2 billion of net bookings in its fiscal year ending March 2027.

2026-11-16-14.headline: Adore Beauty shares crash about 36% as a new warehouse's problems cut its profit forecast by half
2026-11-16-14.soWhat: For an online retailer, the warehouse is the store: if stock is missing or deliveries slip, customers simply buy elsewhere. A new automated warehouse is meant to cut labor costs, but the switch-over is a risky moment, and a small retailer has little cushion. Larger rivals with steady logistics gain share during the disruption. The open question is whether the bank relaxes its covenants, since that decides how much room the company has to recover.

sources.title: ABC News: ASX business live, 16 November 2026
Retail News Asia: Adore Beauty cuts EBITDA forecast to between $4 million and $6.5 million

2026-11-16-14.summary: Australian online beauty retailer Adore Beauty cut its fiscal 2027 underlying EBITDA guidance to A$4.0 million to A$6.5 million, from A$9 million to A$13 million. Product revenue fell 8% in the first 20 weeks of the year after the launch of its new national distribution center disrupted stock and deliveries, though sales rose 3% in the latest eight weeks. It also blamed heavy promotions across the sector and the fixed costs of new stores, and said it is in talks with its bank about loan covenants. The shares fell about 36% to a record low of A$0.17.

2026-11-16-15.headline: Australian farm supplier Elders nearly triples profit to A$144 million after buying Delta Agribusiness
2026-11-16-15.soWhat: Rural services is a scale business: a bigger network of branches can buy farm inputs more cheaply and spread its costs across more customers. Buying Delta added stores and agronomists, so most of the profit jump came from consolidation rather than better farm conditions. Farmers have fewer independent suppliers to choose from as the industry consolidates. The open question is how earnings hold if a dry season or weaker cattle prices cut farm spending.

sources.title: ABC News: ASX business live, 16 November 2026

2026-11-16-15.summary: Elders, which sells seed, fertilizer and chemicals to farmers and runs livestock, wool and real-estate agencies, reported a 187% rise in statutory profit to A$144 million for its fiscal 2026. Underlying sales revenue rose 31% to A$4.0 billion. Delta Agribusiness, bought for A$475 million in November 2025, added A$43.6 million of underlying pre-tax earnings. The company held its dividend at 36 cents and the shares rose 7.5%, the best performance in the ASX 200 on Monday.

2026-11-16-16.headline: Copper trades near a four-month low and UBS cuts its gold forecast by 10% as rate-hike bets weigh on metals
2026-11-16-16.soWhat: Metals are being hit from two sides: higher expected interest rates make non-yielding gold less attractive, and weak Chinese demand undercuts copper. For miners, lower prices squeeze cash flow just as many are spending on new copper projects for electrification and data centers. Buyers such as wire makers and electronics firms get some relief on input costs. The open question is whether the Fed actually raises rates in December.

sources.title: ABC News: ASX business live, 16 November 2026

2026-11-16-16.summary: Three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange fell 1.6% to $13,371.50 a ton on Friday, near a four-month low, and Goldman Sachs said its 2027 forecast of $15,400 now faces downside risk. Spot gold slipped to about $3,869 an ounce on Monday after losing 4.5% last week. UBS cut its fourth-quarter gold forecast 10% to $4,500 and expects $5,000 by the end of 2027. Mining shares fell, with BHP down 2.8% in Sydney.

2026-11-17-01.headline: US requires licenses for AI-chip exports to five countries and for overseas data centers that rent large compute to Chinese firms
numbers: License trigger: >12 million TPP of compute for Chinese firms
Compliance window for existing sites: 90 days
Nvidia revenue from customers outside US, Taiwan, China: ~1.3%
2026-11-17-01.soWhat: For years Chinese AI companies have rented Nvidia-class chips in data centers in Southeast Asia instead of importing them directly, and this rule targets that route. The direct revenue at stake looks small: Nvidia's customers headquartered outside the US, Taiwan and China were about 1.3% of its revenue last quarter. The bigger effect falls on Malaysian and Singaporean data-center builders and on cloud providers whose tenants are Chinese, who now face license reviews and slower sales. US cloud companies gain, because their exemption makes them the easiest suppliers in those markets.

sources.title: Techi: US chip rule names five countries; customers based there are at most 1.3% of Nvidia revenue
Eurasia Business News: Nasdaq slides 2.5% as Nvidia turmoil and chip restrictions hit tech
Yahoo Finance / 24/7 Wall St: Stock market today, November 17

2026-11-17-01.summary: The Commerce Department filed a rule on Monday that requires export licenses for advanced AI chips sent to Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and Brazil, which it sees as higher-risk routes for diversion to China. Overseas data centers will also need a license to give Chinese-headquartered companies more than 12 million TPP of computing power, which one analysis equates to about 760 H100 chips. US-headquartered buyers are exempt if exporters file reports, and existing facilities get 90 days to comply. Chip stocks fell on the news: the Nasdaq dropped 2.5% on Monday, and on Tuesday AMD, Intel and Micron fell between about 5.5% and 7.6% in early trading.

2026-11-17-02.headline: Quebecor makes a C$31 billion cash-and-stock offer for Telus, Canada's second-largest telecom group
numbers: Offer per share: C$19.45 vs C$12.14 prior close
Annual savings target: ~C$160M operating + C$235M capital
2026-11-17-02.soWhat: The deal would merge two of Canada's four largest wireless carriers and undo the structure the government created when it made Rogers sell Freedom Mobile to Quebecor in 2023 to keep a fourth national competitor. Quebecor says wireless prices fell 35.4% in the three years after that sale, which is the competition regulators will want to protect. Scale gives a combined group lower network costs per customer, but consumers could lose a price-cutting rival. Quebecor's share drop shows investors think it may overpay or be forced to sell Freedom; one analyst sees a low chance of approval unless Freedom is divested.

sources.title: BNN Bloomberg: Telus sees 'serious concerns' with Quebecor's $31B takeover bid
Radio Canada International: Quebecor makes $31B offer to acquire Telus

2026-11-17-02.summary: Quebecor, which owns Videotron and Freedom Mobile, offered Telus shareholders C$6.35 in cash plus 0.17 Quebecor shares per share, which it values at C$19.45, against Telus's Friday close of C$12.14. Quebecor estimates about C$160 million a year of operating savings and C$235 million a year of capital savings. Telus formed a special committee and said the offer does not reflect its value, calling regulation the biggest hurdle. On Monday Telus shares rose about 13% to C$13.70, while Quebecor fell about 15% to C$65.25.

2026-11-17-03.headline: Brent falls 3.6% to $92.44 as Hormuz tanker traffic recovers and the IEA forecasts a supply surplus
2026-11-17-03.soWhat: For producers, the price is moving back toward the level they plan budgets around. Most shale and offshore projects still earn strong margins at $90, but the windfall that paid for buybacks and acquisitions in October is shrinking. Refiners and airlines gain as crude costs fall, while governments that released emergency stocks can slow those releases. The open question is whether shipping attacks in the strait keep a risk premium in prices once surplus barrels arrive.

The IEA now expects fourth-quarter oil supply of about 105 million barrels a day, 1.7 million above demand, after earlier forecasting a deficit. 2026-11-17-04.headline: Global stocks extend an AI-led selloff, with the Nasdaq down 2.5% and Seoul down 2.6%, as the dollar hits a 19-month high
2026-11-17-04.soWhat: The AI trade now drives a large share of global stock market value, so doubts about one company's leadership and new export rules ripple from Wall Street to Seoul and Taipei, where chipmakers dominate the indexes. A stronger dollar adds pressure on emerging markets and on commodities priced in dollars. Higher rates make long-dated growth stories less valuable, which is why AI names fall hardest. The open question is whether this week's Nvidia results and Anthropic's IPO steady the trade or extend the decline.

2026-11-17-05.headline: Disney beats forecasts with revenue up 16% to $25.9 billion, raises its dividend 33% and targets $3 billion of cost cuts
2026-11-17-05.soWhat: The results show Disney's streaming business has moved from a loss-maker to a real profit contributor, which changes how the company balances TV networks, parks and direct-to-consumer services. Parks remain the largest single profit engine, and steady pricing there funds both the dividend and the content budget. A $3 billion cost program alongside record content spending signals that media companies now compete on spending efficiently, not just spending more. Investors' muted reaction suggests the extra week flattered the quarter and growth is expected to slow.

2026-11-17-06.headline: Home Depot grows sales 4.9% to $43.4 billion and names its CFO as CEO, but warns of a cautious housing market
2026-11-17-06.soWhat: Home improvement spending follows housing turnover: people renovate when they buy, sell or refinance a home, and high mortgage rates keep many owners in place. Home Depot is leaning on professional contractors, who keep working on repairs and maintenance, and on online sales, up about 13%, to grow while do-it-yourself customers hold back. Large chains with scale in supply and delivery keep gaining share from smaller hardware stores in a flat market. The open question is when rates fall enough to restart home sales and bigger projects.

2026-11-17-07.headline: Gas flows into US LNG plants hit a record 21.8 Bcf as Qatar extends its force majeure through December

2026-11-17-07.soWhat: LNG plants run on long-term contracts that pay a fixed liquefaction fee, but when global supply is short, the cargoes they can sell spot earn large margins. With Qatar's output constrained, US plants have become Europe's main swing supplier going into winter, which benefits US exporters and gas producers in Texas and Louisiana. European utilities and industry pay the price through higher gas costs while storage is low. The EU's ban on Russian LNG from January 1 removes another source, so new US capacity such as Golden Pass matters even more.

2026-11-17-08.headline: Deutsche Bank shares fall as much as 6% after reports based on 15 million leaked internal records
2026-11-17-08.soWhat: Banks depend on trust from regulators and counterparties, so a large leak about past controls can cost more than any fine, through higher funding costs, closer supervision or lost business. Deutsche Bank has paid penalties before for weak anti-money-laundering controls, which makes regulators likely to look again. The bank has rebuilt profits in recent years, and its share price had been rewarded for that turnaround. The open question is whether the reports reveal new problems that lead to fresh regulatory action or only revisit known history.

2026-11-17-09.headline: US retail sales rise just 0.2% in October as shoppers turn cautious before the holidays
2026-11-17-09.soWhat: Retail sales are not adjusted for inflation, so with prices still rising, a 0.2% gain means shoppers bought fewer goods in real terms. Spending is shifting toward online sellers and away from big-ticket items like cars and furniture, which depend on credit and are hurt by high interest rates. That pattern favors large online and discount retailers going into the holidays, and squeezes specialty chains. For the Fed, soft spending eases some inflation pressure, but rising import prices keep the pressure on.

2026-11-17-10.headline: ULA's Vulcan rocket fails for the first time, destroying 40 Amazon Leo internet satellites
2026-11-17-10.soWhat: Launch capacity is the bottleneck for every satellite network that wants to compete with SpaceX's Starlink. With Vulcan grounded and Blue Origin's New Glenn also out of service, Amazon has few non-SpaceX rockets left, which slows its rollout and weakens its bargaining power. The Pentagon depends on Vulcan for many national security missions, so the failure also strengthens SpaceX's position in government launch contracts. The open question is whether the cause traces to the shared BE-4 engine, which would also delay New Glenn.

It was the first outright failure of a ULA rocket since the Boeing and Lockheed Martin venture was formed in 2006, and the first Vulcan flight in nine months; the cause is not yet known. The launch would have taken Amazon to 436 satellites launched, against more than 3,300 needed for the full network. Amazon has booked 38 Vulcan flights, and the Space Force had already paused national security launches on Vulcan.

2026-11-17-11.headline: Tyson's beef unit loses $514 million in the quarter as the US cattle shortage deepens, while chicken stays profitable
2026-11-17-11.soWhat: Beef packers are squeezed because the US cattle herd is at multi-decade lows: ranchers charge record prices for cattle, but packers cannot pass all of it on to shoppers. Chicken works differently, because birds grow in weeks rather than years, so supply responds quickly and margins recover faster. That is why diversified protein companies lean on chicken and packaged foods while beef plants are closed or slowed. The open question is when ranchers start rebuilding herds, which first tightens supply further because heifers are held back from slaughter.

2026-11-17-12.headline: Amazon plans $7 billion more for Indian wind and solar by 2030 and signs four projects totaling 934 MW
2026-11-17-12.soWhat: Large tech companies have become some of the biggest buyers of clean power, and their long-term purchase contracts give developers the guaranteed revenue they need to borrow and build. India is attractive because its solar costs are among the lowest in the world and Amazon is expanding data centers there. Developers like ReNew and Waaree gain steady demand, while state grids must add transmission to move power from windy and sunny regions to cities. The open question is whether India's grid can connect new projects fast enough.

2026-11-17-13.soWhat: Wealth managers earn fees as a percentage of client assets, so revenue is recurring and grows with markets and new money, which is why private equity and sovereign funds pay high prices for them. The UK market is fragmented, and buyers usually use a platform like this to acquire smaller firms and spread fixed costs such as compliance and technology. That helps margins but leaves JD with slow growth, because Chinese consumers are still cautious and its core electronics business depends on government trade-in subsidies. EU carmakers would be hit hardest because the UK is their largest export market. A delay would buy time for new European battery plants to ramp up.

Rivals gain when big buyers hedge; Microsoft said the turmoil could speed demand for alternative chips from AMD and Broadcom. Extrapolation turns a few coding errors in a sample into a repayment across an entire contract, which makes aggressive coding a financial liability and could cut margins for years. Humana is the most exposed because Medicare Advantage is most of its business, while UnitedHealth has the largest share of enrollment at about 29%. The open question is how much of the rule survives the comment period and likely court challenges.

2026-11-19-04.headline: Fed minutes show almost all officials expect more rate hikes, and markets price a December increase at about 90%
2026-11-19-04.soWhat: Higher short-term rates raise borrowing costs for companies, home buyers and governments at a time when US 10-year yields are already above 5%. Banks can earn more on deposits and loans, but sectors that depend on cheap financing, such as real estate, utilities and long-duration growth stocks, lose. A stronger dollar from higher US rates also squeezes commodity prices and emerging-market borrowers. The open question is whether the Fed moves by 25 or 50 basis points in December, which depends on the next inflation reports.

Falling gasoline prices help consumers and airlines heading into winter. The open question is whether continued attacks near Hormuz keep a risk premium in Brent once the expected surplus arrives.

2026-11-19-06.headline: Walmart raises its outlook for the third time as revenue grows 5.2% to $188.8 billion and US online sales jump 23%
2026-11-19-06.soWhat: Walmart is growing profit faster than sales because it now earns more from high-margin streams such as advertising and membership fees, on top of thin grocery margins. Its online scale lets it deliver more orders from stores at a lower cost per order, which squeezes smaller grocers and regional chains. Slowing US comparable sales show shoppers remain careful, so price cuts are being used to defend traffic. The open question is how much fuel and freight costs will eat into margins once one-time tariff refunds fade.

2026-11-19-07.headline: EnQuest sells its whole UK North Sea business to TotalEnergies-backed NEO NEXT+ for up to $960 million
2026-11-19-07.soWhat: The UK North Sea is a mature basin where small and mid-sized producers face high windfall taxes and large clean-up bills as old fields shut. EnQuest gets cash to repay debt and redeploy into Southeast Asia, which it sees as higher-return. The deal shows how UK fiscal policy is pushing consolidation, and the open question is whether further tax changes slow new investment and speed up field closures.

2026-11-19-08.headline: Palo Alto Networks grows revenue 39% to $3.44 billion and agrees to buy AI start-up Applied Compute for $4.5 billion in stock

Large platforms gain against smaller point-product vendors, which find it harder to compete on breadth. The open question is whether security firms can turn AI model hosting into lasting revenue or whether it remains a feature that clouds give away.

2026-11-19-09.headline: Target posts its best sales growth in five years with comparable sales up 5.6%, while TJX lifts its full-year outlook
2026-11-19-09.soWhat: Both results show shoppers are still spending but moving toward value: Target won traffic back with price cuts, and off-price stores gain when department stores have excess stock to sell cheaply. Tariff refunds are giving retailers a one-time profit boost this year, which flatters reported earnings. Weaker department stores and specialty chains lose share to discounters and off-price stores. The open question is whether the sales pickup lasts through the holiday season once price cuts and refunds stop helping.

2026-11-19-10.headline: UK inflation rises to 3.6% and eurozone inflation sits at 4.0%, the highest in three years
2026-11-19-10.soWhat: When headline inflation rises but core stays steady, the pressure is coming mostly from energy rather than from wages and services, which makes central banks less sure whether to raise rates. Households and energy-intensive industries such as chemicals and steel feel the squeeze first, while energy producers benefit. The European Central Bank and Bank of England have to weigh weak growth against the risk that high energy costs spread into wages. The open question is whether falling oil prices this month pull headline inflation back down quickly enough to avoid rate rises.

2026-11-19-10.summary: UK consumer prices rose 3.6% in the year to October, up from 3.5% in September but below the 3.7% expected, while core inflation held at 2.8% and services inflation was 3.7%. Eurozone inflation was 4.0% in October, up from 3.8% and the highest since 2023, with core inflation steady at 2.5%. The gap between headline and core inflation in both places reflects energy prices pushed up by the Iran conflict. European shares fell 1% on Wednesday.

2026-11-19-11.headline: EQT buys Flatiron Energy, a 24 GWh battery storage developer in the US Northeast
2026-11-19-11.soWhat: Batteries are the fastest-growing part of the power transition because they store cheap solar and wind output and release it at peak times, which grids short of capacity will pay for. In crowded Northeast markets, the scarce assets are permitted sites and grid connections, so a developer with both is worth more than the batteries themselves. Infrastructure funds like EQT want the long-term contracted cash flows, while utilities facing data-center demand gain fast capacity. The open question is how quickly the 24 GWh pipeline can win contracts and connect to the grid.

2026-11-19-11.summary: EQT's Transition Infrastructure fund agreed on November 17 to buy Flatiron Energy from Hull Street Energy, which invested in 2022. Flatiron has grown its portfolio nearly tenfold since then to 24 gigawatt-hours of battery storage, holds 6 GWh of long-term contracts and has 2 GWh under construction. It works in New England, New York and the Mid-Atlantic, focusing on dense urban markets where sites and grid connections are hard to secure. Financial terms were not disclosed, and completion is expected in the fourth quarter of 2026.

2026-11-19-12.headline: Tencent misses revenue forecasts at CNY 207 billion as it steps up AI spending, with capex 47% above estimates
2026-11-19-12.soWhat: Tencent's core businesses of games, ads and payments still grow, but heavy spending on AI chips and data centers is starting to weigh on operating profit, a pattern seen across big platforms. Advertisers benefit from better AI targeting, while investors must wait longer for returns on the new spending. Chinese rivals building AI models face pressure to match the outlay. The open question is whether AI lifts ad and cloud revenue fast enough to justify capex running well above forecasts.

Capital spending reached CNY 81.4 billion against CNY 55.4 billion expected, and WeChat users rose to 1.45 billion.

2026-11-19-13.headline: SQM's lithium price falls 10% in a quarter and it warns of a further substantial drop
2026-11-19-13.soWhat: Lithium shows how a commodity can fall even when demand grows fast: new mines and refineries in China, Australia and Africa have added supply faster than battery makers need it. Low-cost producers such as SQM, which pump lithium brine in Chile's Atacama desert, stay profitable when prices drop, while higher-cost hard-rock miners get squeezed and may delay projects. Battery and electric-car makers gain from cheaper raw materials. The open question is how long it takes for high-cost supply to shut and prices to find a floor.

Adjusted EBITDA was $1.03 billion, below the $1.11 billion expected, and the company warned fourth-quarter prices could fall substantially. It still expects lithium demand to grow 30% in 2026 and kept its production guidance of 280,000 to 290,000 tonnes.

2026-11-19-14.headline: GSK wins early US approval for Nelkarmi, a second lung cancer drug from its $10.6 billion Nuvalent purchase
2026-11-19-14.soWhat: Large drug makers are buying late-stage cancer assets to replace revenue from older drugs that are losing patent protection. Approval in later-line patients is a foothold; the bigger prize is moving to first-line treatment, where patients stay on drug longer and sales are larger. Incumbent ALK drugs, such as Pfizer's Lorbrena and Roche's Alecensa, face a new rival. The open question is whether the Phase 3 first-line trial shows a clear advantage.

The approval came ahead of the November 27 target date and rests on the single-arm ALKOVE-1 trial. GSK gained the drug through its $10.6 billion acquisition of Nuvalent, and analysts expect about $1 billion of annual sales by 2032. A Phase 3 trial is testing it in patients who have not had earlier ALK treatment.

2026-11-19-15.headline: UPS agrees to buy Australian healthcare courier Smartways Logistics, reportedly for about A$600 million
2026-11-19-15.soWhat: Healthcare logistics pays more than ordinary parcels because shipments are urgent, temperature-controlled and regulated, and customers rarely switch providers. UPS is buying into this niche to offset slower growth and lower margins in its main parcel business. Smaller specialist couriers become takeover targets, while rivals such as FedEx and DHL face a stronger competitor in Asia-Pacific healthcare. The open question is whether UPS can grow these bolt-on businesses fast enough to change its overall margin.

2026-11-19-15.summary: UPS agreed to acquire Smartways Logistics, a healthcare courier in Australia and New Zealand owned by private equity firm The Riverside Company. Terms were not disclosed, but the Australian Financial Review reported an offer of about A$600 million ($405 million). The deal is expected to close in the first half of 2027.

2026-11-19-16.headline: Alstom swings to a €954 million half-year loss on problem train contracts and cuts its margin target to about 1%
2026-11-19-16.soWhat: Rolling-stock makers sign long fixed-price contracts years before delivery, so cost overruns and late trains hit profit and cash long after the order is booked. A strong order book does not guarantee profit if contracts were priced too tightly. Rivals such as Siemens Mobility and Stadler can win on reliability, while rail operators face delays. The open question is whether Alstom can fix the troubled programs without raising new equity.

2026-11-19-17.headline: California bans robotaxis from freeways after Waymo cars enter a construction zone, and Waymo suspends freeway service
numbers: Scope: all robotaxi operators on California freeways
2026-11-19-17.soWhat: Freeway access matters to robotaxi economics because airport trips and longer rides are among the most valuable fares. Losing it limits how much of the ride-hailing market driverless services can serve in California, which helps human-driven services such as Uber and Lyft in the short run. Regulators are showing that one incident can change rules for the whole industry, which raises the cost of expansion for every operator. The open question is what safety evidence regulators will require to lift the ban.

2026-11-19-18.headline: GTA VI launches with a reported 15.9 million pre-orders, three-quarters on PlayStation 5
2026-11-19-18.soWhat: A single blockbuster can drive a publisher's revenue for years because sales continue long after launch and online play adds spending on in-game items. Sony benefits most because most buyers play on its console, which can lift hardware sales and its share of digital store revenue. Retailers and other publishers may see spending shift toward one title during the holiday season. The open question is how fast the online mode grows, since that recurring spending decides long-term profit.

2026-11-19-19.headline: Rakuten Bank shares fall 19% after Rakuten Securities discloses a breach that may affect 11 million accounts

2026-11-19-19.soWhat: Online banks and brokers depend on trust because customers can move money with a few clicks. A breach at one unit can hit the whole group when businesses share customer data and branding, which is why the bank fell more than the brokerage parent. Regulators may demand costly security upgrades, and rivals such as SBI can win customers who leave. The open question is whether the breach led to actual fraud losses, which would raise the cost far beyond fixing systems.

2026-11-20-01.headline: Asian chip stocks crash, with Taiwan down 6.2% to cap its worst week since 1991 after a 2% fall on Wall Street
numbers: Taiex: -6.2% on the day, -17.5% on the week
2026-11-20-01.soWhat: Asian markets are far more concentrated in chip and AI hardware stocks than the US, so a change in sentiment about AI spending hits them hardest. The fall shows how much of this year's equity gains rested on a single theme: the same companies that supplied the AI build-out now carry the most downside if spending slows. Higher bond yields and expected Fed hikes add pressure, because they raise the discount rate applied to growth stocks. The open question is whether AI customers actually cut orders or whether this is only a repricing of expectations.

2026-11-20-02.headline: TPG and Corpay agree to take BILL private for $63.25 a share, about $6 billion
2026-11-20-02.soWhat: This is the same pairing that bought AvidXchange, another bill-payment software firm, for $2.2 billion, so TPG and Corpay are assembling a larger platform for business payments outside the public market. Small-business payment software earns from subscriptions plus a cut of each payment, but public investors have marked the sector down as growth slowed and AI tools threaten to commoditize parts of it. Buyers such as private equity can pay a premium, cut costs and integrate the pieces without quarterly scrutiny. The modest premium and the share drop show that some holders hoped for more, which makes rival bids unlikely.

BILL serves nearly 500,000 businesses, and activist investor Starboard Value has agreed to vote for the deal. BILL shares fell about 3% to $62, and closing is expected in the first half of 2027.

2026-11-20-03.headline: Intuit sells Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion, less than a third of the $12 billion it paid in 2021
2026-11-20-03.soWhat: The sale is a clear marker of how far valuations have fallen for slow-growing software brands since the 2021 peak, when buyers paid for growth that did not arrive. It also shows a split in the software market: platform owners like Intuit are narrowing their focus to products they can rebuild around AI, while specialist owners like Bending Spoons buy steady, cash-generating brands cheaply and run them for profit. Mailchimp's small-business customers are price-sensitive and face many cheaper tools, so its new owner is likely to push margin over growth.

Intuit's own quarterly revenue rose 12% to $4.35 billion and beat forecasts, but its full-year guidance came in below expectations and the shares fell about 15% after hours. Bending Spoons, which buys mature software brands such as Evernote, Vimeo and WeTransfer and cuts costs, also reported revenue up 125% to $780 million.

2026-11-20-04.headline: UniCredit and Germany reach broad agreement that clears the way for its takeover of Commerzbank
2026-11-20-04.soWhat: This would be the largest cross-border bank takeover in the euro area since the financial crisis and a test case for the long-promised consolidation of Europe's fragmented banking market. The logic is cost: combining overlapping branches, IT and head offices can lift returns well above what either bank earns alone. The losers are likely to be Commerzbank staff, since UniCredit has signaled thousands of job cuts and has promised only to discuss job protection. The open question is whether Berlin now sells its remaining stake to UniCredit.

2026-11-20-04.summary: After two years of resistance, the German government and UniCredit announced a broad agreement on UniCredit's takeover of Commerzbank, the country's second-largest listed bank, valued at about €41 billion. In a letter to the finance minister, UniCredit committed to keep Commerzbank's headquarters and listing in Frankfurt, keep key decisions in Germany, keep supporting small and midsize companies, and hold talks with staff representatives on protecting jobs. UniCredit already owns close to 50% of Commerzbank, and the German state still holds about 12% from the financial-crisis bailout. The EU approved the takeover on Monday, and UniCredit hopes to get final regulatory approvals this month.

2026-11-20-05.headline: Oil heads for a third straight weekly loss, with Brent near $90 as Hormuz exports return to pre-war levels
2026-11-20-05.soWhat: Upstream producers are paid the market price, so a fall from the mid-$90s to about $90 cuts cash flow directly, and the decline is steeper for US producers selling against WTI. The market is now pricing in the end of the war premium, which shifts the balance of power back to OPEC+: if supply keeps recovering, the group must decide whether to cut output to defend prices or keep volumes and accept lower prices. A falling market also hurts US shale more than Gulf producers, because shale wells cost more to drill and decline faster.

sources.title: CNBC: Oil prices set for third straight weekly decline on Middle East export flows

2026-11-20-05.summary: Brent crude fell about 1.8% to $90.33 a barrel on Friday and was on track for a weekly decline of about 6%, while US WTI fell to $81.59 and was set to lose about 8% for the week. Shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have returned to roughly pre-war levels, which has fed expectations of a supply surplus. Risks remain: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two tankers hit naval mines in the strait, and there has been roughly one attack on tankers per day in November. OPEC+ ministers meet from November 29 to set 2027 output policy.

2026-11-20-06.headline: P&G plans to cut 20% to 30% of its manufacturing and supply workforce by 2030 as it automates factories
2026-11-20-06.soWhat: Consumer-goods makers face higher input costs and shoppers who are resisting further price increases, so cutting cost is the main lever left to protect margins. Automation is now cheap and reliable enough to replace a large share of factory and warehouse labor, and P&G's scale lets it spread the investment over huge volumes. The winners are automation and software suppliers; the losers are plant workers and smaller rivals that cannot match the cost savings. The open question is how much of the savings P&G keeps as profit and how much it reinvests in lower prices and marketing.

The plan is part of a productivity program the company says can save up to $10 billion over fiscal 2027 to 2030. About 52,000 people worked in P&G manufacturing in 2025, close to half of its staff. P&G has also stopped manufacturing and commercial operations in some markets such as Pakistan and Bangladesh.

2026-11-20-07.headline: The US, China and Russia pledge to raise refined fuel output, but name no volumes or dates
2026-11-20-07.soWhat: Refiners earn the spread between crude and the fuels they make, and that spread has been unusually wide because refining capacity, not crude, has been the bottleneck. More output from Chinese and Russian plants would narrow diesel and jet fuel margins, which would help airlines, truckers and fuel importers and hurt refiners that have been earning windfall cracks. China holds the most spare refining capacity, but it has limited fuel exports with quotas to protect its own market. The open question is whether the pledge turns into larger Chinese export quotas and repaired Russian refineries, or stays a statement.

The statement gives no production targets, no specific products and no timeline. Refined fuel markets, diesel in particular, have been tight because of the wars in Ukraine and Iran, and Russian refineries have been under drone attack. Oil prices eased toward $90 a barrel after the meeting.

2026-11-20-08.soWhat: Medicare Advantage is the most profitable business for big US health insurers, and it depends on two government levers: risk-adjusted payments for sicker patients and star-rating bonuses. The audit rule and lower star ratings hit both at once, which is why investors are cutting valuations before any money is repaid. Political talk of a government-run plan adds a long-term risk premium even if legislation is unlikely soon. The comment period on the audit rule runs to January 19, 2027, so the final cost is still unknown.

UnitedHealth, which covers more than 9 million Medicare Advantage members, also sued CMS over lower 2027 star ratings, joining at least 14 other plans.

2026-11-20-09.headline: US Senate passes a 62-33 bill to speed permits for power plants and transmission lines and make data centers pay for their power
2026-11-20-09.soWhat: Power demand from data centers is growing faster than the grid can be expanded, and long permitting for transmission lines is one of the main bottlenecks. Faster approvals would help developers, grid builders and equipment makers get projects into service sooner, which matters because utilities only earn a return once assets are in service. Making data centers pay their own costs aims to stop households from subsidizing grid upgrades for big tech, a growing political issue as power bills rise. The open question is whether the House accepts the Senate version.

sources.title: AP via Click2Houston: Senate backs bill to speed up permitting reviews, force data centers to pay for energy costs

2026-11-20-09.summary: The US Senate passed a bipartisan permitting bill 62 to 33, with 15 Democrats voting in favor. Both clean-energy and oil and gas industry groups support it, while environmental groups oppose it. The bill now goes to the House, which passed a narrower version last year.

2026-11-20-10.headline: Codelco cuts its 2027 copper premium for China to about $250-$280 a ton as its Chilean sales to China drop 38%
2026-11-20-10.soWhat: Producers sell most copper on annual contracts at the exchange price plus a premium that reflects how scarce physical metal is in a region. Codelco priced too high this year and lost Chinese market share to other suppliers, so it is cutting to win volume back. The record spot premium shows physical metal is still tight in China even as futures prices fall, which helps whoever has metal available now. A proposed 15% US tariff on refined copper from 2027 could change these flows again.
