2026-11-20-11.headline: SK Hynix will become Kioxia's largest shareholder with a 14.1% stake by converting ¥129 billion of bonds
2026-11-20-11.soWhat: Kioxia and SK Hynix compete in NAND flash, the memory used in phones and data-center storage, so a rival becoming the top shareholder matters to regulators and to Kioxia's management. Under 2018 commitments, SK Hynix must keep its voting share below 15% until 2028, which limits its influence for now. The stake is a cheap option on future consolidation in a market where only a handful of makers remain and AI storage demand has lifted prices. Kioxia's other partner, Sandisk, which co-owns its factories, has the most to watch.

2026-11-20-12.headline: Telus calls Quebecor's C$31 billion offer too low as BCE talks raise the prospect of a bidding war
2026-11-20-12.soWhat: Canada has three national carriers and a smaller fourth, and wireless prices are among the highest in the developed world, so any merger will be judged on competition. Telus carries heavy debt and cut its dividend in half this year, which is why a buyer can bid at a large premium while still paying a low price relative to the company's assets. A Bell-Telus combination would save more cost but faces a much harder review than a deal with Quebecor. The open question is whether Bell bids formally, which would force Quebecor to raise its offer.

2026-11-20-13.headline: Ross Stores grows comparable sales 8% on rising traffic, but guides to slower holiday growth
2026-11-20-13.soWhat: Off-price chains buy surplus branded goods cheaply from other retailers and brands and sell them at a discount, so they gain when department stores have excess stock and shoppers trade down. Ross's traffic growth, alongside strong results this week from TJX and Walmart, shows value-focused retailers taking share while full-price apparel chains struggle. The slower holiday guide reflects a tough comparison against last year's 9% gain. The open question is how long consumers keep trading down as inflation and interest rates stay high.

Ross raised its full-year EPS forecast to $8.75 to $8.84 but expects fourth-quarter comparable sales growth of only 4% to 5%, and the shares fell on the cautious outlook. It opened 51 stores in the quarter and now has 2,377.

2026-11-20-14.headline: Zurich lifts its estimate of capital savings from the £8.1 billion Beazley deal by 80% to $1.8 billion
2026-11-20-14.soWhat: Insurers must hold capital against the risks they write, and a larger, more diversified book needs less capital per dollar of premium, so freed capital can be returned to shareholders or used to grow. That is why the capital synergy is ten times the cost synergy and drives the deal's economics. Scale also matters in specialty lines such as cyber and marine, where brokers favor carriers that can take large risks alone. Smaller Lloyd's specialists face a stronger competitor as specialty pricing softens.

sources.title: Insurance Business: Zurich lifts Beazley capital synergy estimate 80% after deal close
Reinsurance News: Zurich raises Beazley deal capital synergies estimate to $1.8bn

2026-11-20-14.summary: At its investor day, Zurich Insurance raised its estimate of capital synergies from buying specialty insurer Beazley to about $1.8 billion within two years, up from $1 billion at announcement. It also raised its estimate of medium-term revenue opportunities to about $1.5 billion from $1 billion, while keeping cost synergies at more than $150 million. The £8.1 billion deal closed on October 1 and creates the world's largest specialty insurer, with about $15 billion of combined specialty premiums. Underwriters will face brokers as one team from April 2027.

2026-11-20-15.headline: Accor will buy out Ennismore's minority owners for about €1.6 billion, valuing its lifestyle-hotel arm at €3.7 billion
numbers: Price: ~€1.6B in three tranches to Jan 2028
Share of Accor: ~5% of rooms, ~20% of recurring EBITDA
2026-11-20-15.soWhat: Big hotel groups make most of their money from fees for managing and franchising hotels that others own, and lifestyle brands command higher fees and room rates than standard ones. Ennismore's outsized profit share shows why Accor wants full control of that growth rather than sharing it or floating the unit. Paying 18 times EBITDA is a bet that lifestyle hotels keep growing faster than the market. The open question is whether Accor later brings in partners or lists Ennismore, which it has not ruled out.

sources.title: Hospitality Net: Accor to increase its stake in Ennismore
Hotel Management: Accor to increase Ennismore stake in $1.76B deal

2026-11-20-15.summary: Accor agreed to buy out minority shareholders in Ennismore, its lifestyle-hotel business, for about €1.6 billion in three tranches through January 2028. The deal values Ennismore's equity at about €3.7 billion, roughly 18 times expected 2027 EBITDA, compared with about €1.7 billion when Qatari investors came in during 2022. Ennismore is only about 5% of Accor's rooms but about 20% of its recurring EBITDA. Accor will fund the deal partly with at least €500 million of asset sales and a new credit line, and says the structure protects its investment-grade rating.

2026-11-20-16.headline: Bank Indonesia unexpectedly raises rates to 6% to defend the rupiah as the Fed leans toward more hikes
2026-11-20-16.soWhat: When the Fed is expected to raise rates, money flows out of emerging markets toward higher US yields, weakening their currencies and raising the cost of imported fuel and goods. Central banks such as Indonesia's then raise rates to protect the currency even when domestic inflation is under control, which slows lending and growth. That is how US tightening spreads around the world. Companies with dollar debt and importers gain from a steadier rupiah, while borrowers and property developers face higher costs.

sources.title: Bank Indonesia: BI-Rate raised to 6.00% (news release)
Investortrust: Bank Indonesia hikes policy rate 25 bps to 6%

2026-11-20-16.summary: Bank Indonesia raised its benchmark rate by 0.25 points to 6.00%, its first hike after four months on hold. Most economists polled by Reuters had expected no change. The central bank called the move pre-emptive, aimed at steadying the rupiah, which stood at about 18,245 per dollar after hitting a record low, against pressure from high oil prices, expected US rate increases and a strong dollar. Inflation was 3.23% in October, inside its 1.5% to 3.5% target band, and the economy grew 5.47% in the third quarter.

2026-11-21-01.headline: The S&P 500 and Dow fall into a correction as a 5.3% Nasdaq plunge wipes out its gains for 2026
numbers: Nasdaq Composite: -5.3%; Nasdaq-100 19.8% below its Oct 6 record
2026-11-21-01.soWhat: The sell-off has moved from a few AI leaders to the whole market, because AI and chip stocks now make up a large share of the main US indexes. Investors are questioning whether the very large spending on data centers will earn enough return, and a likely Fed rate hike in December raises the discount rate applied to future profits. Defensive areas such as consumer staples held up, which is the usual pattern when money leaves high-growth stocks. The open question is whether companies actually cut AI orders, or whether this is only a reset of very high expectations.

sources.title: UPI: Dow, S&P 500 enter correction as Nasdaq plunges in AI stock sell-off
TradingKey: Nasdaq plunges 5%, erasing all year-to-date gains
Stock Market Watch: Market Digest, Friday, November 20, 2026

2026-11-21-01.summary: US stocks had their worst day in months on Friday as the sell-off in AI and chip stocks accelerated. The S&P 500 fell 3.7% to 6,910 and the Dow lost 1.9% to 48,147, both closing more than 10% below their recent highs, the usual definition of a correction. The Nasdaq Composite dropped 5.3% and gave up its gains for the year, while the Nasdaq-100 ended 19.8% below its October 6 record, close to the 20% line that marks a bear market. The Philadelphia chip index fell 10.7% with all 30 members down, the VIX fear gauge jumped 26% to about 36, and gold fell about 4% as investors sold winners to cover losses.

2026-11-21-02.headline: Nvidia falls 14% after a report that the SEC is examining its accounting
numbers: Hugging Face deal under DOJ review: $12.9B
Singapore-billed sales: reportedly near half of revenue before the reporting change
2026-11-21-02.soWhat: Nvidia is the largest single supplier to the AI build-out, so any doubt about the quality of its reported numbers spreads to the whole chip and data center chain. Accounting questions matter more than a weak quarter because investors value the company on the assumption that its revenue and margins are reliable. An SEC inquiry often ends without charges, but it can take months, and the uncertainty lands while the company has no permanent leader. The open question is what the SEC is actually looking at, which may not become clear for some time.

sources.title: Reuters via Investing.com: Nvidia's accounting is a focus of US SEC investigation, sources say
TradingKey: Nvidia tumbles 13% as AI stock selloff deepens

2026-11-21-02.summary: Nvidia shares fell about 14% on Friday after Reuters reported, citing two people briefed on the matter, that SEC enforcement staff are examining potential accounting issues at the company. The Wall Street Journal had reported the investigation earlier in the week without identifying its focus, and it is not known when it began or which matters it covers. Last year Nvidia changed how it reports revenue by region, using customers' headquarters instead of billing addresses, which removed Singapore from its breakdown after reports that Singapore-billed sales had approached half of revenue. The Justice Department is also reviewing Nvidia's $12.9 billion purchase of Hugging Face, and the company is run by an interim chief executive after its co-founder left this month.

2026-11-21-03.headline: Broadcom drops more than 11% on reports that Google is cutting orders for its TPU chips and buying memory directly
numbers: Reported cut to 2027 TPU 8i shipments: ~1M units (~20%)
Bernstein estimate of Google's savings: ~$50B over the chips' life
2026-11-21-03.soWhat: Big cloud companies design their own AI chips to rely less on Nvidia, and they pay partners such as Broadcom to turn those designs into finished products. If Google takes over buying memory and moves volume to a cheaper partner, part of the margin Broadcom earns on each chip moves back to Google. Memory makers could face tougher price talks, because they would deal directly with a large, cost-focused buyer. The open question is whether other cloud giants copy Google, which would shrink the fees that custom-chip partners can charge.

sources.title: MLQ.ai: Broadcom falls 11% after analyst Ming-Chi Kuo says Google cut 2027 orders for its TPU chips
TradingKey: Nasdaq plunges 5% as AI stock selloff deepens
DigiTimes: Google looks to bypass Broadcom with direct HBM purchases

2026-11-21-03.summary: Broadcom shares fell more than 11% on Friday after analyst Ming-Chi Kuo said Google had cut planned 2027 shipments of the Broadcom-designed TPU 8i chip by about 1 million units, roughly 20% of expected volume. Kuo said Google plans to ship more of the TPU 8t, which is designed with MediaTek. Separate industry reports say Google wants to buy high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for its chips directly from memory makers instead of through Broadcom, which today handles design, packaging and memory purchasing. Bernstein estimates the change could save Google about $50 billion over the life of the chips; Google has not confirmed either report.

2026-11-21-04.headline: Brent posts a third straight weekly loss near $92.60 as Gulf crude reaches Asia and fuel margins collapse
numbers: Weekly change: about -3% to -4%, third straight loss
Singapore gasoline margin: ~$1/bbl vs record $50.50 on Oct 1
Tanker hits near Hormuz: about one a day
2026-11-21-04.soWhat: Crude prices depend on two things: whether barrels can physically reach buyers, and whether refiners want them. Both have turned bearish, because tankers are moving again and the collapse in Asian gasoline margins means refiners earn little for each extra barrel they process, so they buy less crude. Producers selling into Asia lose pricing power, while airlines, shippers and fuel importers gain from cheaper energy. The open question is whether attacks near Hormuz or the Red Sea escalate enough to disrupt flows again, which is still the main upside risk to prices.

sources.title: NPR: S&P 500 sinks and the Nasdaq composite goes negative for the year
WAM: Oil prices settle higher, Brent set for weekly loss
Archyde (Oilprice.com): Brent set to close week down as Gulf supply flows to Asia outweigh Hormuz strikes

2026-11-21-04.summary: Brent crude settled up 0.6% at $92.57 a barrel on Friday but fell about 3% to 4% over the week, its third weekly loss in a row, while US WTI ended near $84. Gulf crude is reaching Asian buyers in large volumes even though Iranian drones still hit about one tanker a day near the Strait of Hormuz, so supply fears are fading. Further down the chain, the margin for turning crude into gasoline in Singapore fell to about $1 a barrel, from a record $50.50 on October 1. Brent has traded between about $90 and $100 in recent weeks.

2026-11-21-05.headline: Anthropic shares fall 8.5% on their second day of trading, ending close to the $83 IPO price
numbers: IPO proceeds incl. extra shares: $93.5B, a record
2026-11-21-05.soWhat: Anthropic's weak second day shows how fast demand for AI listings can cool when the wider market falls, even for a company with fast-growing revenue. A price close to the IPO level matters for later deals: OpenAI has said it may list next year, and many AI and data center companies have already pushed their listings into 2027. Index funds may have to buy the shares later, which could support the price. The open question is whether investors will keep paying about 40 times sales for AI model makers when chip stocks are falling.

sources.title: Reuters via SRN News: Anthropic's post-debut stumble delivers reality check for AI trade
UPI: Dow, S&P 500 enter correction as Nasdaq plunges in AI stock sell-off

2026-11-21-05.summary: Anthropic shares fell 8.5% to $88.91 on Friday, giving back much of the 17% first-day gain from Thursday's Nasdaq debut and ending not far above the $83 offer price. Including extra shares bought by its underwriters, the IPO raised $93.5 billion, above SpaceX's $85.7 billion, making it the largest listing on record. At Friday's price the company is valued at about $1.6 trillion fully diluted, or roughly 40 times its sales over the past year. Morgan Stanley, which had been supporting the price after the listing, closed that position, and options trading on the shares starts next week.

2026-11-21-06.headline: A Missouri judge gives final approval to Bayer's $7.25 billion settlement of Roundup cancer claims
numbers: Settlement: up to $7.25B over up to 21 years
2026-11-21-06.soWhat: Roundup litigation has hung over Bayer's crop science business for almost a decade, and this deal turns an open-ended legal risk into a capped payment spread over many years. Together with a June Supreme Court ruling that blocks state claims that cancer warnings were missing, it narrows the main route plaintiffs used to win large jury awards. That frees cash and management attention for the core seeds and crop chemicals business, where Bayer competes with Corteva and Syngenta. The open question is whether objectors appeal, which would delay the settlement taking effect.

sources.title: PBS NewsHour: Court approves $7.25 billion Bayer settlement over claims Roundup weed killer caused cancer
St. Louis Public Radio: St. Louis judge gives final approval to $7.25 billion Roundup settlement

2026-11-21-06.summary: A state judge in St. Louis gave final approval on Friday to Bayer's class settlement of claims that its Roundup weedkiller causes non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Bayer will pay up to $7.25 billion over as long as 21 years into a fund, with average awards ranging from $10,000 to $165,000 depending on exposure, age at diagnosis and severity. The deal comes on top of the $16 billion Bayer had already set aside for Roundup litigation, which covers about 200,000 claims since it bought Monsanto in 2018. The ruling can be appealed, and payments would pause during any appeal; about 200 federal cases sit outside the settlement.

2026-11-21-07.headline: Sanofi weighs a takeover of Insmed, a lung-disease drugmaker worth about $26 billion
numbers: Insmed share move on the report: about +16%
2026-11-21-07.soWhat: Large drugmakers are buying companies with approved or late-stage medicines to replace sales they will lose as patents expire, and they will pay high prices for products already on the market. Insmed's lead drug treats bronchiectasis, a chronic lung disease, which would fit Sanofi's push in respiratory and immune diseases. At Insmed's current value, a deal would be more than twice the size of Sun Pharma's $11.75 billion purchase of Organon, so far the year's largest drug deal. The open question is whether other buyers compete, since a public report often draws rival interest.

sources.title: Reuters via Yahoo Finance: Sanofi weighs takeover of US drugmaker Insmed, Bloomberg News reports
Fierce Pharma: Sun's $11.75B Organon buy

2026-11-21-07.summary: Sanofi is considering buying US drugmaker Insmed and is working with advisers, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter. Insmed's shares rose about 16% on the report, giving it a market value of about $26.3 billion. Deliberations are ongoing and any deal could still be weeks away. Neither company commented.

2026-11-21-08.headline: Private credit defaults nearly double to 1.5% in the third quarter, with small borrowers hit hardest
2026-11-21-08.soWhat: Private credit funds lend directly to mid-sized companies, mostly at floating rates, so higher interest rates raise borrowers' costs straight away. The numbers show the strain sitting with smaller and debt-funded companies, such as healthcare provider groups built through acquisitions, while larger borrowers still cope. Fund managers charge fees on assets, so rising defaults hurt their investors first, but they also make it harder to raise new money and to sell these funds to individual investors. The open question is whether more Fed rate hikes push the stress from small borrowers to larger ones.

sources.title: Alternative Credit Investor: Private credit default rate nearly doubles in Q3
Houlihan Lokey: Size-weighted defaults in private credit nearly doubled in the third quarter

2026-11-21-08.summary: Defaults on private credit loans rose to 1.5% of outstanding principal in the third quarter from 0.8% in the second, according to Houlihan Lokey's quarterly DataBank report. Counted by number of borrowers, the rate rose to 3.7% from 2.5%, and for companies with less than $100 million of EBITDA it reached 5.0%. Healthcare was the weakest sector, with 7.1% of borrowers in default, while software borrowers stayed healthy at about 1%. About 7% of loans are now valued below 90 cents on the dollar, and 15.1% of borrowers earn less than they owe in interest.

2026-11-21-09.headline: MasTec agrees to buy mechanical contractor Murphy for about $1.25 billion, and its shares fall more than 10%
2026-11-21-09.soWhat: Data centers and new factories need far more mechanical and electrical work than offices, so contractors with skilled union crews have become scarce and valuable. Buying firms like Murphy lets MasTec sell a larger part of each project, from power lines to cooling systems, as these sites get bigger. Investors reacted badly because the deal adds debt just as AI stocks are falling and doubts are growing about how long the data center boom lasts. The open question is whether the order backlog holds if large tech companies slow their spending.

sources.title: RTTNews: MasTec to acquire Murphy Corp in $1.25 bln deal
Quantisnow: MasTec to buy Murphy for $1.25 billion in cash and shares fall over 10%
MasTec: Definitive agreement to acquire Murphy Corporation

2026-11-21-09.summary: MasTec agreed on Friday to buy Murphy Corporation, a 119-year-old mechanical, plumbing and process contractor, for about $1.25 billion in cash plus an earnout tied to the next three years of results. Murphy expects about $775 million of revenue and $140 million of adjusted EBITDA in 2026, so the price is roughly 9 times EBITDA. Its 1,600 staff, including 1,200 union craft workers, serve data centers, hospitals, drug plants, and aviation and defense sites. It is MasTec's third debt-funded deal since July, after the $1.65 billion purchase of electrical contractor Superior Group, and its shares fell more than 10%.

2026-11-21-10.headline: ABB considers listing its robotics unit if it cannot rescue the $5.4 billion sale that China blocked
numbers: China share of the robotics unit: ~30%
2026-11-21-10.soWhat: Industrial robots are a strategic technology for China, which is both the largest buyer of robots and home to fast-growing local rivals, so Beijing now treats foreign control of a major supplier as a security matter. The case shows that cross-border deals can fail even after competition approval, because security reviews are a separate and less predictable hurdle. Splitting off the China business would save the deal but give SoftBank a smaller company cut off from its biggest market. It is the second big deal China has blocked this year, after Meta was ordered to unwind its purchase of Manus.

sources.title: Reuters via Yahoo Finance: ABB considers robotics listing if sale to SoftBank fails, sources say
SCMP: China blocks SoftBank's US$5.4 billion takeover of ABB's robotics division

2026-11-21-10.summary: ABB is weighing a stock market listing or spin-off of its robotics business if it cannot save its $5.4 billion sale to SoftBank, Reuters reported, citing sources. China blocked the deal this month in a foreign investment security review, reportedly over SoftBank's ties to Western companies such as OpenAI and the risk of data flowing to the US. One rescue option is to carve out the China business, about 30% of the robotics unit, and sell it to a Chinese buyer or list it separately. China is ABB's largest robotics market, with about 15,000 staff in the country, and talks could run into next year.

2026-11-21-11.headline: Los Angeles and Long Beach port employers reach a tentative deal with security guards, avoiding a strike
numbers: Cargo through affected terminals: ~85% of Long Beach, ~33% of Los Angeles
2026-11-21-11.soWhat: Los Angeles and Long Beach are the busiest US container ports, so even a small union can stop large flows of goods if other workers honor its picket lines. A strike in the peak holiday season, with imports near record levels, would have pushed delays through trucking, rail and warehouses and could have taken weeks to clear. The deal removes that risk for retailers and manufacturers. The main dockworker contract runs to 2028, so the larger labor risk on the West Coast is some years away.

sources.title: Reuters via KFGO: Southern California port employers, watchmen union reach tentative deal
gCaptain: More than 110 trade groups urge deal as LA-Long Beach port strike deadline nears

2026-11-21-11.summary: The Pacific Maritime Association, which represents terminal operators at the Los Angeles and Long Beach ports, reached a tentative agreement on Saturday with ILWU Local 26, the union for about 250 port security guards. The old contract was due to expire at 12:01 a.m. Saturday, and the union had already voted to authorize a strike after more than a year of talks. The six terminals involved handle about 85% of Long Beach's cargo and a third of Los Angeles', and other dockworkers could have refused to cross picket lines. More than 110 business groups had urged a deal; members still need to ratify it.

2026-11-21-12.headline: Databricks is in early talks to raise funds at about $225 billion, up from $190 billion in August
2026-11-21-12.soWhat: Databricks sells software that stores and prepares company data for analysis and AI, which makes it a supplier to the AI boom rather than a bet on a single model. A higher private valuation during a public sell-off shows investors still pay up for software with strong growth and paying business customers. Staying private lets Databricks avoid public market swings while competing with Snowflake and the big cloud providers. The open question is whether the round closes at that price if the public market slide continues.

sources.title: Reuters via MarketScreener: Databricks in early talks to raise funds at $225 billion valuation, WSJ reports

2026-11-21-12.summary: Data and AI software company Databricks is in early talks to raise several billion dollars at a valuation of about $225 billion, the Wall Street Journal reported, and terms could still change. In August it said it had raised $5 billion at a $190 billion valuation. Its Lakehouse data warehousing business has passed a $1.5 billion annual revenue run-rate, and its newer Lakebase database has passed $100 million. The report came on the same day AI stocks sold off sharply.

2026-11-21-13.headline: BJ's raises its outlook as sales jump 17.7%, though most of the comparable growth comes from gasoline
2026-11-21-13.soWhat: Warehouse clubs earn most of their profit from membership fees, which is why they can sell goods at thin margins and still make money. The gap between 13.5% and 4.1% comparable growth shows how much higher fuel prices lift reported sales without adding much profit, so the figure excluding gasoline is the better measure of demand. Rising membership income and online sales suggest cost-conscious shoppers are moving to clubs, which helps BJ's, Costco and Sam's Club at the expense of supermarkets. Merchandise margin fell about 1.7 percentage points on promotions, the price of winning those shoppers.

sources.title: BJ's Wholesale Club: Third quarter fiscal 2026 results (SEC filing)

2026-11-21-13.summary: BJ's Wholesale Club grew net sales 17.7% to $6.15 billion in the quarter to October 31, and comparable club sales rose 13.5%. Excluding gasoline, comparable sales rose a more modest 4.1%, while digitally enabled sales grew 38%. Membership fee income rose 9.5% to $138.4 million, and earnings per share rose 50% to $1.73, helped by about $240 million from a card-fee legal settlement. BJ's raised its full-year forecast to 2.5% to 3.0% comparable growth excluding gasoline and adjusted EPS of $5.10 to $5.30.

2026-11-21-14.headline: Prosecutors probe Mark Walter's insurers over more than $20 billion of undisclosed lending to related companies
numbers: Delaware Life related-party holdings: ~$1.4B first reported, ≥$17B after re-check
Insurers bought by private equity since the pandemic: ~50
2026-11-21-14.soWhat: Life and annuity insurers hold customers' money for decades and invest it, and many owned by private equity now put a large share into private loans, often to related companies. When those links are not disclosed, regulators and customers cannot judge how safe the money is, which is why this case is a test for state-based supervision. About 50 insurers have been bought by private equity firms since the pandemic, so tighter rules on affiliate lending would affect a large part of the annuity market. The open question is whether regulators respond with stricter disclosure and capital rules, which would raise costs for these owners.

sources.title: Claims Journal: Probe of Mark Walter's insurers spotlights gaps in regulatory patchwork
InvestmentNews: Walter fallout tests state annuity regulators

2026-11-21-14.summary: Federal prosecutors are investigating Delaware Life and Clear Spring Life, insurers controlled by Mark Walter's Group 1001, which did not disclose that more than $20 billion of their investments went to entities that finance Walter's other ventures. Lending to affiliates is allowed but must be disclosed; Delaware Life first reported about $1.4 billion of such holdings, then at least $17 billion after a re-check. Delaware's regulator oversees about $1.2 billion of life premiums per staff member, more than any other state, and is also reviewing Aquarian's delayed $4.1 billion bid for Brighthouse Financial. No wrongdoing has been alleged, and Group 1001 says it is cooperating and financially strong.

2026-11-21-15.headline: Boeing leaves the door open to more layoffs as 737 output stalls at 42 jets a month
numbers: Planned cut: 5% of ~50,000 commercial airplane staff
2026-11-21-15.soWhat: Planemakers carry heavy fixed costs in factories and staff, so profit depends on raising output; every month at a lower rate leaves costs spread over fewer jets. Cutting jobs while the order backlog is large shows Boeing is focused on cash, but it risks losing skilled workers it will need when output does rise. Airlines waiting for jets keep older planes longer, which helps lessors and engine-repair firms and keeps fares firm. The open question is whether regulators approve the higher rate in early 2027 as now planned.

sources.title: Reuters via SRN News: Boeing leaves open possibility of more layoffs amid stalled production plans

2026-11-21-15.summary: Boeing declined to tell its engineers' union whether more layoffs will follow a round of notices due on December 9, the union said. Earlier this month the company announced plans to cut 5% of the roughly 50,000 staff in its commercial airplanes division through attrition and layoffs. It blames 737 MAX output rising more slowly than planned: the move from 42 to 47 jets a month, once due this summer, is now expected in early 2027. The SPEEA union, with about 17,000 members, approved a four-year contract in October with a 10% raise on signing and 4% a year after.

2026-11-21-16.headline: The US Commerce Department asked battery startup Pure Lithium to give the government a 51% stake, Reuters reports
numbers: Proposed plant funding: ~$1B from Japan's $550B pledge
Largest agreed US government stake: 15% of MP Materials
2026-11-21-16.soWhat: The US government is moving from giving grants and loans to strategic industries to taking ownership stakes, which changes who controls the companies and their technology. A majority stake would go much further than past deals, and it would make any startup in batteries, chips or minerals weigh public money against loss of control. Some of these stakes are paid for with CHIPS Act money, and critics say that law never allowed the government to own companies. The open question is whether courts or Congress set limits on how far this approach can go.

sources.title: Reuters via SRN News: Lutnick asked battery startup Pure Lithium to accept US takeover, documents and source say

2026-11-21-16.summary: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick asked Pure Lithium in July to hand the US government a 51% controlling stake, according to documents and a source cited by Reuters. In return, about $1 billion of Japan's $550 billion US investment pledge would fund a plant that Pure Lithium would run but not own. The company rejected the proposal in August, warning that 51% was far outside precedent, and its 9.9% counteroffer was turned down. The administration has taken stakes in Intel, MP Materials (15%, its largest), USA Rare Earth and Korea Zinc, but has not yet taken majority control of any company.

2026-11-22-01.headline: Zscaler jumps 18% after hours on a report that CrowdStrike is in talks to buy it
2026-11-22-01.soWhat: CrowdStrike is strongest in protecting laptops, servers and cloud workloads, while Zscaler routes and checks company network traffic under a zero-trust model, so together they would cover most of what a large company buys for security. Security buyers want fewer vendors, and a combined platform could sell more products to each customer, which squeezes smaller single-product rivals. The shares split the usual way: the target gains a takeover premium, and the buyer falls on worries about dilution and the cost of integration. The open question is whether a deal of this size would face antitrust review now that the security market is consolidating fast, after Google bought Wiz for $32 billion and Palo Alto Networks bought CyberArk for $25 billion.

sources.title: Yahoo Finance: Zscaler stock soars 18% on CrowdStrike takeover report
Bloomberg: CrowdStrike's talks with Zscaler show AI-led cyber consolidation

2026-11-22-01.summary: Bloomberg reported on Friday evening that CrowdStrike is in talks to acquire Zscaler, citing people familiar with the matter. Zscaler, worth about $32 billion and down about 13% this year, rose about 18% in extended trading, while CrowdStrike, worth about $235 billion after roughly doubling this year, fell more than 8%. No price, financing or timetable has been disclosed, and there is no guarantee of a deal. The two already work together: in September they expanded a partnership to connect their platforms and share threat data.

2026-11-22-02.headline: European power for the next three months trades near €200 per MWh, double last winter, and two German suppliers stop delivering
numbers: Front-month to three-month power: ~€200/MWh, ~2x last winter
German day-ahead: above €300/MWh three times in two weeks
Verbund spot-power hit: €120M in nine months
UK price cap forecast for January: +26% to £2,166
2026-11-22-02.soWhat: In most of Europe, gas plants are the last plants needed to meet demand, so they set the wholesale price, and a tripling in gas passes straight into power. Small retail suppliers fail first because they sell fixed-price tariffs to households but buy power at short notice, so a price spike wipes out their thin margins, much as dozens collapsed in 2022. Generators with nuclear, coal or hydro output earn more when prices rise, while energy-heavy industry such as steel and chemicals loses: Feralpi's German steel plant has repeatedly stopped production this autumn. The open question is how cold the winter gets, because gas storage started the season well below normal.

sources.title: Energy Connects (Bloomberg): Europe's power market is flashing a warning to its economy
Clean Energy Wire: Germany plans to ready coal and oil power plants for gas emergency

2026-11-22-02.summary: European gas prices are about three times their level of a year ago because the Middle East war has cut supply and Europe competes with Asia for LNG cargoes. Power contracts for each of the next three months trade around €200 per megawatt-hour, roughly double last winter, and German day-ahead prices settled above €300 three times in two weeks. Two small German suppliers, Grüüün and Stromee, stopped supplying their customers. Austria's Verbund took a €120 million hit from buying costly spot power when its hydro output was low, and the UK price cap is forecast to rise 26% to £2,166 a year in January. Germany is drafting a law to bring 7.45 GW of reserve coal plants and 805 MW of oil plants back to the market if it declares a gas emergency.

2026-11-22-03.headline: Bitcoin falls to about $55,300, its lowest since September 2024, as crypto stocks lose 20% to 35% in a week
numbers: Bitcoin low: ~$55,300 (lowest since Sept 2024); weekly fall ~12%
Spot bitcoin ETF outflows: ~$1.25B in the week, ~$3.59B in November
Strategy shares: -30.3% in the week; average bitcoin cost $75,452
2026-11-22-03.soWhat: Bitcoin now trades like a high-risk tech asset, so the AI-led stock sell-off and expectations of a December Fed hike pulled it down with the Nasdaq. Companies whose earnings depend on crypto prices lose twice: exchanges such as Coinbase earn less trading revenue when prices and activity fall, and bitcoin holders such as Strategy see their main asset shrink. Bitcoin is now about 20% below Strategy's average purchase price of $75,452, which makes it harder for the company to keep raising money to buy more. The open question is whether ETF outflows keep going, because those funds were the main new buyers of the last two years.

sources.title: CEO Economy: Crypto week in review, Nov 21 2026
Archyde: Bitcoin fell to approximately $55,300 on Saturday

2026-11-22-03.summary: Bitcoin dropped to about $55,300 early on Saturday, its lowest level since September 2024, before recovering to about $60,100 by the evening, still down about 12% on the week. It has lost more than half its value since its record of about $126,200 in October 2025. Leveraged futures positions worth more than $2 billion were liquidated in 24 hours, and US spot bitcoin funds lost about $1.25 billion in the week, including a record one-day outflow of $541 million from BlackRock's IBIT. Shares of crypto companies fell hard: Strategy lost 30.3%, Coinbase 20.1% and Robinhood 20.2%.

2026-11-22-04.headline: Oracle says its OpenAI data center build-out is fully funded after a $20 billion stock and debt raise
numbers: OpenAI contract: ~$300B over 5 years from 2027, ~4.5 GW
2026-11-22-04.soWhat: Oracle has to build and pay for the data centers before OpenAI pays anything, because OpenAI pays only once the hardware is running, so the main risk for Oracle is financing, not demand. Saying the money is secured removes one worry, but it was raised partly by selling new shares below recent prices, which dilutes existing owners, and partly with more debt on top of about $167 billion already owed. The deal links Oracle's results closely to one customer's ability to keep raising money. The open question is how much of the $300 billion commitment is backed by financing beyond this raise, which Oracle did not say.

sources.title: Startup Fortune: Oracle says its $300 billion OpenAI buildout is fully funded after a $20 billion raise
FourWeekMBA: Oracle says OpenAI deal fully funded

2026-11-22-04.summary: Oracle said on Friday that the financing it set out at its investor day, including vendor financing, is now in place for its infrastructure contract with OpenAI. The last piece was a raise of about $20 billion this month, split roughly evenly between $10 billion of new shares sold at $116 and $10 billion of notes. The contract is reported at about $300 billion over five years from 2027 for about 4.5 gigawatts of computing capacity. Oracle had negative free cash flow of $23.7 billion in fiscal 2026, and its shares, which closed well below the $116 offer price, rose as much as 3.3% after hours.

2026-11-22-05.headline: Trump threatens a 'tremendous tax' on US companies that build AI data centers abroad
numbers: Tax rate, timeline, legal basis: none given
Example named: Google's data centers in Finland
2026-11-22-05.soWhat: US cloud and AI companies build abroad to be near overseas customers, meet local data-residency rules and find cheaper or faster power, so a tax would raise their costs or slow their foreign growth. The policy pulls in two directions: it pushes more construction into the US just as local opposition to data centers, and their demand on power grids, is rising. Countries that have courted US data center investment, in the Nordics, the Gulf and Asia, could lose projects to domestic sites or to non-US builders. The open question is whether this becomes a real rule, since no mechanism has been proposed and Democrats will control both houses of Congress.

sources.title: NBC News: Trump threatens companies that build AI data centers overseas
Yahoo News: Trump threatens a 'tremendous tax' on tech companies building data centers outside the US

2026-11-22-05.summary: President Trump said on Friday that the US will not allow its companies to build data centers outside the country and that it will put heavy penalties on those that try. He gave no tax rate, timeline or legal basis, and said he had not yet told his own staff about the plan. He has criticized Google for investing in data centers in Finland and suggested building in states such as West Virginia instead. The remarks came after midterm elections in which voters backed candidates who promised to limit data centers, and as the S&P 500 had fallen about 9% since November 4.

2026-11-22-06.headline: US stocks enter a holiday-shortened week in a correction, with markets pricing a December Fed hike at about 95%
2026-11-22-06.soWhat: When the few large AI stocks that drove the rally fall, the whole index falls with them, so the market now depends on whether the wider economy stays solid. Higher expected rates hurt in two ways: they raise borrowing costs for companies and households, and they make future profits worth less today, which hits fast-growing stocks hardest. Assets that pay no income, such as gold and bitcoin, have also sold off because holding them costs more when cash earns more. The open question is whether this week's data shows inflation easing enough for the Fed to stop after December.

sources.title: Kitco (Reuters): Wall St Week Ahead, Black Friday brings consumer spending into focus
Khaleej Times: Gold holds near 14-month low as Fed hike bets weigh

2026-11-22-06.summary: The S&P 500 ended Friday 11.6% below its October 6 record, confirming a correction, and the technology sector has fallen about 19% since that peak. Markets put the chance of a quarter-point Fed rate increase in December at about 95%, which has lifted the dollar to its highest since April 2025 and pushed gold down to a 14-month low near $3,693 an ounce. The coming week brings an inflation reading, consumer confidence and revised third-quarter GDP, with US markets closed on Thursday for Thanksgiving. Investors are looking to consumer spending, about two-thirds of the US economy, for signs that growth is holding up outside AI.

2026-11-22-07.headline: Holiday sales are forecast to rise 4.2%, but the NRF expects fewer Thanksgiving-weekend shoppers than last year
numbers: Holiday sales forecast: +4.2% nominal, +2.2% real (Oxford Economics)
US gasoline: $3.72/gal vs ~$4.30 a month ago (AAA)
2026-11-22-07.soWhat: Retailers make a large share of their annual profit in the last two months of the year, so the season decides whether they meet their full-year targets. Sales rising in dollars but only half as fast in volume means much of the growth is higher prices, and fewer people shopping in stores over the holiday weekend favors large chains with strong online businesses. Cheaper gasoline than a month ago leaves households a little more to spend, which helps discounters and big-box stores most. The open question is whether falling share prices make wealthier households, who drive a large part of spending, cut back.

sources.title: Kitco (Reuters): Wall St Week Ahead, Black Friday brings consumer spending into focus

2026-11-22-07.summary: Oxford Economics expects US holiday retail sales in November and December to rise 4.2%, or about 2.2% after inflation, excluding cars, gasoline and restaurants. The National Retail Federation expects 182.7 million people to shop over the five days from Thanksgiving to Cyber Monday, down from 186.9 million last year, with Black Friday the busiest day. Walmart and Target gave upbeat holiday comments in their results this week, and October retail sales rose moderately. Gasoline averaged $3.72 a gallon on Thursday, down from nearly $4.30 a month earlier but up from $3.09 a year ago.

2026-11-22-08.headline: US gasoline falls about 13% in a month to $3.72 a gallon as crude eases, ahead of the Thanksgiving driving peak
numbers: US gasoline: $3.72/gal, vs ~$4.30 a month ago and $3.09 a year ago
2026-11-22-08.soWhat: Pump prices follow crude with a lag of a few weeks, because refiners and stations pass on changes in their own input costs gradually, so the fall in oil since October is now reaching drivers. Refiners' profit depends on the gap between crude and fuel prices, and that gap has narrowed as China, Russia and the US promise more fuel output. Cheaper fuel helps airlines, trucking companies and households, and it lowers headline inflation, which matters for the Fed. The open question is whether OPEC+ changes its plans at its November 29 meeting, where it is due to set 2027 output targets.

sources.title: Kitco (Reuters): Wall St Week Ahead

Engineering News: OPEC+ keeps December oil output targets steady ahead of tougher call for 2027

2026-11-22-08.summary: The US average gasoline price was $3.72 a gallon on Thursday, according to AAA, down from nearly $4.30 a month earlier but still well above $3.09 a year ago. The drop follows crude: Brent ended the week near $92 a barrel and WTI near $83 after three weekly losses, as Gulf exports through Hormuz recovered. AAA expects about 72.9 million Americans to drive for Thanksgiving, nearly 90% of holiday travelers. US natural gas futures ended near $3.27 per million British thermal units, while Europe's TTF benchmark rose to about €85.8 per MWh.

2026-11-22-09.headline: Sanofi wins early US approval for Infilbray, the first drug for the brain symptoms of type 3 Gaucher disease
numbers: Phase 3 trial: 43 patients, superior to Cerezyme
Approved: Nov 18, about a week before the Nov 25 target date
2026-11-22-09.soWhat: Rare-disease drugs treat few patients but can charge high prices and keep them for years, because there are few or no alternatives and patients stay on treatment for life. Sanofi already leads the Gaucher market, so the new pill lets it defend that franchise against enzyme therapies from Takeda and Pfizer and extend it to patients the old drugs could not help. An approval ahead of schedule also signals that the FDA will move quickly on drugs that fill a clear gap. The open question is pricing, because a pill that replaces part of an infusion business could take sales from Sanofi's own products.

sources.title: MedCity News: Sanofi Gaucher disease type 3 drug venglustat (Infilbray) FDA approval
NeurologyLive: FDA approves venglustat, first therapy for neurological manifestations of type 3 Gaucher disease

2026-11-22-09.summary: The FDA approved Sanofi's venglustat, sold as Infilbray, on November 18, a week before its target date, for adults and children weighing at least 15 kg. It is the first treatment for the neurological symptoms of type 3 Gaucher disease, a rare inherited disorder. Infilbray is a once-daily pill designed to reach the brain, and in a 43-patient Phase 3 trial it beat Sanofi's own enzyme infusion Cerezyme on a combined measure of movement and thinking. Cerezyme and Sanofi's older Gaucher pill Cerdelga together sold more than €1 billion in 2025; the price of Infilbray has not been disclosed.

2026-11-22-10.headline: Volkswagen opens German wage talks on Tuesday seeking a two-year pay freeze, against the union's demand for 5%
2026-11-22-10.soWhat: German car plants have some of the highest labor costs in the industry, while Volkswagen faces weak sales in China, cheaper Chinese electric cars and tariffs, so wages are one of the few large costs it can control directly. A freeze would protect margins, but strikes in January would stop production and cost more than the savings in the short run. Suppliers and German towns that depend on the plants carry much of the risk. The open question is how far each side moves, since both opening positions are far apart and Bloomberg reports the proposals are likely to soften.

sources.title: Finimize: Volkswagen draws a hard line ahead of wage talks
Automotive World: Volkswagen and IG Metall to begin talks on 24 November

2026-11-22-10.summary: Volkswagen and the IG Metall union start collective bargaining in Emden on November 24. The carmaker wants a two-year pay freeze, fewer bonuses, and the right to extend working hours when demand requires without automatically raising pay. IG Metall is asking for a 5% raise over 12 months and says strikes could begin in January. Volkswagen has ended most of its existing wage agreements, and its restructuring includes plans for 100,000 job cuts and the possible closure of one of its four German plants from the early 2030s.

2026-11-22-11.headline: Nvidia nears a deal to buy diffusion-model startup Inception for more than $500 million, The Information reports
numbers: Nvidia one-day share move on SEC report: about -14%
Hugging Face deal under DOJ review: $12.9B
2026-11-22-11.soWhat: Nvidia earns most of its money selling chips, but it also builds software and models that make its hardware more useful, which keeps developers tied to its platform. Diffusion models generate text in parallel rather than one word at a time, which could make AI answers faster and cheaper to serve, and owning that know-how helps Nvidia design for it. At $500 million the price is small next to Nvidia's cash flow, so this is a purchase of talent and ideas, not revenue. The open question is whether regulators, already reviewing its $12.9 billion Hugging Face deal, will look closely at a run of small AI purchases.

sources.title: Newsquawk: Nvidia is near to acquiring diffusion AI developer Inception, per The Information
The Information: Nvidia nears acquisition of diffusion AI developer for more than $500 million

2026-11-22-11.summary: Nvidia is close to acquiring Inception, a startup that builds language models using diffusion, the technique behind many image generators, for more than $500 million, according to The Information. The deal would add to Nvidia's own open models, called Nemotron. Neither company has confirmed it. The report came in a week when Nvidia's shares fell about 14% in one day after a report that the SEC is examining its accounting.

2026-11-22-12.headline: AAA expects 81.5 million Thanksgiving travelers, the first decline in four years, as domestic airfares jump 17%
2026-11-22-12.soWhat: For airlines, a 17% rise in fares with only slightly fewer passengers means much more revenue per seat, since holiday flights are nearly full anyway. The risk is that high fares push price-sensitive travelers to drive or stay home, which shifts spending toward hotels near home, gasoline and road trips. Cruise lines and rail, the only growing modes, benefit from travelers who book whole packages in advance. The open question is whether the air traffic control problems of recent weeks cause delays during the peak.

sources.title: Fox Weather: AAA expects over 81 million Americans to travel for Thanksgiving

2026-11-22-12.summary: AAA expects about 81.5 million Americans to travel at least 50 miles between November 24 and 30, slightly below last year's 81.6 million, ending a three-year run of records. About 72.9 million will drive and 5.96 million will fly domestically, both slightly fewer than last year, while bus, train and cruise travel is expected to rise 4.1% to about 2.6 million. Round-trip domestic airfares average $800, up 17% from last year, based on AAA booking data. AAA said higher travel costs explain part of the dip.

2026-11-22-13.headline: Kraken's parent Payward agrees to buy venture firm Tribe Capital, which manages $2.7 billion
2026-11-22-13.soWhat: Crypto exchanges earn most of their money from trading fees, which fall sharply when prices drop, as they have this month, so they are adding businesses with steadier income. Asset managers earn fees on the money they manage whether markets rise or fall, and private-market funds charge higher fees than public ones. Payward also plans to build private-market products on its trading platform, competing with brokers that are opening private investing to ordinary investors. The open question is how the deal will be judged, since the buyer's co-CEO founded the firm being bought and the price is not public.

sources.title: The Block: Kraken parent Payward to acquire Tribe Capital

2026-11-22-13.summary: Payward, the parent of crypto exchange Kraken, agreed to buy Tribe Capital, a venture capital firm and asset manager with $2.7 billion of assets under management. Tribe invests in early- and late-stage private companies in AI, software and financial infrastructure, and will sit inside Payward's asset management arm. Terms were not disclosed, and the deal is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027. Tribe was co-founded by Arjun Sethi, who is now Kraken's co-CEO, and had invested in Kraken before he took that role.

2026-11-22-14.headline: Freedom Holding's revenue rises 81% to $910 million as its banking and insurance arms nearly triple
2026-11-22-14.soWhat: The results show a broker turning itself into a full financial group: banking and insurance now each bring in more revenue than brokerage. Lending and insurance income are steadier than trading commissions, but they need more capital and carry credit and claims risk, which is one reason profit grew far more slowly than revenue. The open question is whether profit margins recover once the expansion costs level off.

sources.title: Cyprus Mail: Freedom Holding increases revenue by 81 per cent to $910.1 million

2026-11-22-14.summary: Freedom Holding, a Kazakhstan-focused financial group listed on Nasdaq, grew net revenue 81% to $910.1 million in the quarter to September 30, from $503.6 million a year earlier. Banking revenue rose 182% to $298.1 million and insurance revenue 133% to $299.2 million, while brokerage, its original business, fell 5% to $222.2 million. Net income rose 29% to $46.1 million, a much slower increase than revenue. Its client base grew to 9.3 million from 8.7 million, and total assets reached $16.6 billion.

2026-11-23-01.headline: Nvidia jumps about 30% after its board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO, lifting chip and AI stocks
2026-11-23-01.soWhat: Nvidia's swing shows how much of its value investors tie to one founder at a time when it sells most of the world's AI chips. The return removes a leadership gap for its biggest customers and suppliers, but the open investigation and the new export-control committee mean governance risk has not gone away. The rebound also spread to neoclouds such as CoreWeave, whose borrowing and growth depend on confidence in Nvidia's supply. The open question is whether the board's review ends cleanly or brings new findings.

sources.title: Fox News live: Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO
Yahoo Finance live: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang
CNBC: Stock market today live updates

2026-11-23-01.summary: Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as president, CEO and director on Monday, eleven days after he resigned. CFO Colette Kress, who served as interim CEO, returns to the finance role, and an independent board committee will continue its investigation with Huang's cooperation. The board also created a National Security and Export Control Committee and is hiring a new chief compliance officer. Nvidia shares rose about 30% in Monday trading to roughly $163, after falling 14% to $125.53 on Friday and more than 30% since the scandal began. CoreWeave rose about 29% and Micron about 14% as chip stocks rebounded from their worst week since 2001.

2026-11-23-02.headline: CrowdStrike agrees to buy Zscaler for $43.9 billion in stock, creating a security platform with over $10 billion of recurring revenue
numbers: Combined recurring revenue: >$10B; revenue synergies: ~$1B a year
2026-11-23-02.soWhat: The deal joins the leader in protecting laptops and servers with the leader in cloud network security, the two biggest pieces of a company's security budget. Buyers increasingly want one platform rather than dozens of point tools, so the merged firm can bundle products and squeeze smaller rivals such as Netskope and the network-security units of Cisco and Fortinet. Palo Alto Networks, the main platform rival, now faces a competitor of similar breadth. Paying in stock spreads the risk, but CrowdStrike holders take on dilution and a large integration.

sources.title: ABC News/AP: CrowdStrike to acquire Zscaler in $44B deal
CNBC: Stock market today live updates
Fox News live: AI, tech and markets

2026-11-23-02.summary: CrowdStrike will buy Zscaler in an all-stock deal valued at about $43.9 billion, confirming talks reported on Sunday. Zscaler holders get 1.135 CrowdStrike shares per share, a 34% premium to Friday's close, and will own about 15.9% of the combined company. The two firms already share about 2,000 customers, and CrowdStrike plans to sell to roughly 8,000 Zscaler customers that do not yet use it, targeting about $1 billion of yearly revenue synergies. Zscaler's founder and his affiliates, who control about 34% of its shares, agreed to vote for the deal, which should close in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal 2028. CrowdStrike fell about 8% and Zscaler rose about 13% in early trading.

2026-11-23-03.headline: Vår Energi buys ConocoPhillips' Norway business for $4.4 billion, taking over the historic Ekofisk fields
numbers: New output target: >500,000 boe/d into the mid-2030s
2026-11-23-03.soWhat: The deal shows how the North Sea is being consolidated by focused regional producers while US majors redeploy capital to cheaper shale and LNG. About 75% of the reserves are in fields where Vår already holds stakes, so it can cut overlapping costs and take control of operations rather than just paying its share. Norway's tax system, which lets companies deduct investment quickly, makes mature fields more valuable to a local taxpayer than to an outsider. Vår has hedged about 80% of the extra gas at around $110 per barrel equivalent, protecting the cash it needs to keep paying dividends.

sources.title: Offshore Energy: $4.4 billion play for ConocoPhillips' Norwegian assets
Ground News: Vår Energi acquires ConocoPhillips Norwegian operations

2026-11-23-03.summary: Vår Energi, the Norwegian producer controlled by Eni, agreed to buy ConocoPhillips' Norwegian upstream business and related UK infrastructure for an enterprise value of $4.425 billion. Because cash generated since January 1 counts toward the price, it expects to pay about $2.5 billion at completion, around the end of the first quarter of 2027. The package covers stakes in 13 producing fields, operatorship of the Greater Ekofisk Area, the Norpipe pipeline and the Teesside oil terminal in the UK, with 414 million barrels of oil equivalent of proven and probable reserves. Vår expects $700 million to $1 billion of after-tax synergies and raised its long-term output target to above 500,000 barrels a day into the mid-2030s. It will fund the deal from $7.5 billion of available liquidity and lifted its fourth-quarter dividend guidance to $450 million.

2026-11-23-04.headline: Health insurers fall again as Medicare proposes a Star Ratings overhaul that could cut about $107 billion of bonus payments over ten years
numbers: Members in 4-star-plus plans: 51.5% now, 28% under the proposal
2026-11-23-04.soWhat: Star bonuses are a large part of Medicare Advantage profit, so fewer high-rated plans means lower revenue per member for insurers. Coming a week after a plan to claw back past overpayments through audits, it signals a tougher regulator, which hurts the most Medicare-heavy insurers, UnitedHealth and Humana, more than diversified ones like Elevance. Insurers can respond by cutting extra benefits such as dental and vision cover or raising cost-sharing, which would push some seniors back to traditional Medicare. The changes would not bite until 2031, leaving years for lobbying and litigation.

sources.title: Investing.com: Health insurer stocks slide as Medicare Advantage proposal threatens payments

2026-11-23-04.summary: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services proposed changes to the Star Ratings that decide which Medicare Advantage plans earn quality bonus payments, starting with the 2030 ratings that set 2031 bonuses. TD Cowen estimates the change would cut payments to plans by about $107 billion from 2028 to 2037, including about $11.5 billion in 2031. Mizuho estimates the share of members in plans rated four stars or more, the level that earns bonuses, would fall to 28% from 51.5% if the rule is adopted unchanged. UnitedHealth fell 6.5%, Humana 5.1% and CVS Health 4.5% before the market opened, while Elevance, which has less Medicare exposure, fell 1.1%. It is still a proposal, and analysts expect pushback and possible lawsuits.

2026-11-23-05.headline: US stocks rebound about 4% after their worst week in six years, while Korea's Kospi drops 3.3%
numbers: Odds of a Dec 9 Fed hike: ~92%
2026-11-23-05.soWhat: The rebound came from Nvidia's leadership news rather than any change in the bigger worries: high rates, a likely Fed hike and doubts about returns on AI spending. Korea's fall shows how exposed memory-chip exporters are, even with chip exports up sharply this month. Volatility is still near its highest since the 2025 tariff shock, so companies planning share sales or IPOs face an uncertain window. The open question is whether this week's earnings from Dell, HPE and Workday support or undercut the AI spending story.

On Friday the S&P 500 fell 3.7% and the Nasdaq 5.3%, leaving the S&P more than 10% below its October 6 peak, about $8 trillion of lost value. In Asia, South Korea's Kospi fell as much as 5.8% before closing 3.3% lower at 4,708.54, led by Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, while Taiwan's market rose 2.2% and Japan was closed for a holiday. The 10-year US Treasury yield stood near 4.96%, and markets still price about a 92% chance that the Fed raises rates on December 9.

2026-11-23-06.headline: Tata Steel moves to take control of APL Apollo, India's biggest steel-tube maker, in a deal worth up to about $3.5 billion
numbers: Open offer: up to 26% at ₹2,301.40 a share
Assets sold to APL Apollo: up to ₹280B (~$3B)
2026-11-23-06.soWhat: Steelmakers earn steadier and higher margins when they sell finished products such as tubes and coated sheet rather than plain coil, whose price swings with the cycle. Taking control of APL Apollo gives Tata Steel a large customer for its coil and a brand in construction tubes, a fast-growing market in India. The swap structure means Tata pays little net cash, but APL Apollo's minority holders fell sharply because the open-offer price is a modest premium and the company takes on Tata's assets at a full price. Rival steelmakers such as JSW Steel may face pressure to build their own downstream reach.

sources.title: Yahoo Finance/Investing.com: Tata Steel to acquire 26.4% in APL Apollo Tubes for $1.67 billion
CNBC: Stock market today live updates

2026-11-23-06.summary: Tata Steel agreed to buy about 26.4% of APL Apollo Tubes from its founding family at 2,100 rupees a share, about 155 billion rupees ($1.67 billion), in three tranches ending by March 2028. It must also offer to buy up to another 26% from public shareholders at 2,301.40 rupees a share, up to about 168 billion rupees, which would take it to about 52%. In return, APL Apollo will buy Tata Steel's tubes business and its Tata Steel Colors unit for up to 280 billion rupees (about $3 billion), which largely offsets the cost. Tata Steel expects the share of its steel sold as finished downstream products to rise to about 53% from 35%. Tata Steel fell about 5% and APL Apollo more than 16% in early trading.

2026-11-23-07.headline: Brent holds near $92 as Gulf attacks offset a growing supply surplus ahead of the November 29 OPEC+ meeting
numbers: IEA 2027: supply 108.1 mb/d vs demand 104.3 mb/d
2026-11-23-07.soWhat: The market is weighing two opposite forces: physical risk to Gulf shipping, which adds a premium, and rising OPEC+ and US supply, which points to lower prices next year. That leaves OPEC+ with a hard choice on November 29: keep raising output to win market share or pause to defend prices. Producers with high costs and refiners with fixed crude contracts are most exposed if a surplus arrives. The open question is whether attacks on Gulf infrastructure spread from ships to refineries and export terminals.

sources.title: Discovery Alert: Brent slips to $91.97 as oil outlook ignores Gulf attacks
Yahoo Finance live: markets on November 23

2026-11-23-07.summary: Brent crude traded at about $91.97 a barrel on Monday morning, down 0.65%, and WTI near $82.92, after both fell for a third straight week (Brent 4%, WTI 5%). Over the weekend Yemen's Houthis claimed a direct hit on Saudi Arabia's Rabigh refinery on the Red Sea, which Saudi authorities have not confirmed, and the UK maritime agency reported several attacks on ships in the Gulf and near Hormuz. The IEA expects 2027 supply of 108.1 million barrels a day against demand of 104.3 million, a large surplus, while OPEC sees 2027 demand at 108.3 million. OPEC+ meets on November 29 to set its 2027 output policy.

2026-11-23-08.headline: Euro-zone growth holds at 51.7 as Germany hits a four-year high and France slumps
numbers: France: sharpest contraction in six months
2026-11-23-08.soWhat: A PMI above 50 means more firms report growth than decline, so Europe is still expanding, but almost entirely because of German industry. France's weakness is a warning for banks, retailers and builders exposed to French demand. Slowing price growth is welcome for the European Central Bank, which faces euro-zone inflation of 4.0%. The open question is whether German factories can keep growing if US demand and AI-linked spending slow.

sources.title: RTÉ: Euro zone growth holds steady but France clouds outlook
CNBC: Stock market today live updates

2026-11-23-08.summary: The S&P Global flash composite PMI for the euro zone held at 51.7 in November, a fifth month of growth but just below the 51.9 economists expected. Germany's private sector reached 55.0, its fastest growth since March 2022, with manufacturing growing at the quickest pace in more than five years. France posted its sharpest contraction in six months, and its business outlook fell to near the worst since 2012 outside the pandemic, partly on uncertainty before the 2027 presidential election. Across the bloc, services fell to a five-month low of 51.2 while manufacturing rose to 52.9, and output price growth slowed to its weakest since August.

2026-11-23-09.headline: Texas Pacific Land buys EagleRock for about $3 billion in stock to grow its Permian land and water business
numbers: Surface land: ~1M acres plus 105,000 acres of water dedications
2026-11-23-09.soWhat: Texas Pacific Land does not drill wells: it earns royalties on oil pumped from its land, fees for pipelines and roads that cross it, and charges for supplying and disposing of water. Permian wells bring up several barrels of salty water for every barrel of oil, so water handling is a growing, fee-based business that earns money as long as drilling continues. Scale matters because one network can serve many producers at lower cost per barrel. The deal adds exposure to Permian activity, which depends on oil prices staying high enough for producers to keep drilling.

sources.title: Investing.com: TPL to acquire EagleRock Land for $3 billion in all-stock deal
BOE Report: Texas Pacific Land to buy EagleRock in $3 billion deal

2026-11-23-09.summary: Texas Pacific Land agreed to buy EagleRock Land in an all-stock deal worth about $3 billion, or about $23.56 for each EagleRock share (0.0831 new shares each). The combined company would own about 1 million acres of Permian Basin surface land plus 105,000 acres of water-service dedications in the Delaware and Midland basins. Its water network would rise by 49% to about 1.5 million barrels a day of capacity. TPL holders will own about 86%, the company expects about $45 million of yearly benefits, and closing is planned for the first half of 2027.

2026-11-23-10.headline: Julius Baer's profit rises 17% to a record on market gains, but new client money slows
2026-11-23-10.soWhat: Private banks earn fees and interest as a share of client assets, so rising markets lift profit even when new money slows. Net new money is the better test of future growth, and Julius Baer's is weakening as it cleans up its client book after large credit losses in recent years, with less than 2.5% of assets left to exit. Rivals such as UBS and the big US wealth managers are competing hard for the same rich clients in Asia and the Middle East. Recent stock market falls show the risk: the same leverage to markets works in reverse.

sources.title: CNBC: Stock market today live updates
RTTNews: Julius Baer assets rise 6% in first 10 months
Finimize: Julius Baer's de-risking slowed new money inflows

2026-11-23-10.summary: Swiss private bank Julius Baer reported adjusted pre-tax profit of about CHF 1.3 billion ($1.55 billion) for the first ten months of 2026, up 17%. Assets under management reached a record CHF 553 billion at the end of October, up 6% this year, helped by rising stock markets and a stronger dollar. Net new money fell to CHF 8.5 billion from CHF 11.7 billion a year earlier, an annualized growth rate of 2% against 2.8%, as the bank keeps exiting riskier clients. The gross margin slipped to 82 basis points from 83, and a share buyback of up to CHF 600 million is under way.

2026-11-23-11.headline: Intesa Sanpaolo's €34.6 billion offer for Monte dei Paschi opens on Tuesday, the next step in Italy's bank consolidation
2026-11-23-11.soWhat: Italy's largest bank buying a rival that only recently bought Mediobanca would reshape the country's banking map, leaving fewer, larger lenders. The logic is cost savings from merging branches and IT, plus more capital to fund dividends and buybacks. Smaller banks such as BPER and insurer Unipol gain by picking up assets that competition authorities or the buyer do not want. The open question is how Rome uses its golden power veto, which it has used before to shape bank deals.

sources.title: Il Sole 24 Ore: Focus on banks amid Intesa-MPS takeover bid and UniCredit-Commerz merger

2026-11-23-11.summary: Intesa Sanpaolo's public offer for Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena opens on November 24 and runs until January 22, valuing MPS at €34.6 billion and aiming to delist it. MPS's board called the price fair from a financial point of view but said it does not fully reflect the group's value. According to Il Sole 24 Ore, announced commitments cover 35-40% of MPS's capital, and success would set off a further bid for Mediobanca, with some assets then sold to Unipol and folded into BPER Banca. Separately, UniCredit awaits Polish approval, expected by the end of November, before moving to take control of Commerzbank in the first quarter of 2027.

2026-11-23-12.headline: Abu Dhabi's IRH agrees terms for a £353 million takeover of titanium miner Kenmare
2026-11-23-12.soWhat: Kenmare runs the Moma mine in Mozambique, which produces titanium minerals and zircon used in paint pigments, plastics and ceramic tiles. Weak pigment demand has pushed down prices and Kenmare's valuation, letting a state-backed buyer pick up a long-life mine at a low price. Gulf state investors are building portfolios of mines in Africa to secure minerals, competing with Chinese buyers. The gap between the share price and the offer shows doubt that the Mozambican approvals will come through.

sources.title: RTÉ: Kenmare Resources receives possible cash offer from IRH
Miningmx: Kenmare board leans toward £353m takeover offer

2026-11-23-12.summary: Kenmare Resources agreed in principle to a possible cash offer of 380 pence a share from Abu Dhabi's International Resources Holding (IRH), valuing it at about £352.8 million. The price is a 52% premium to the 250 pence close on November 20, and Kenmare's board said it is unanimously minded to recommend it. Shares jumped more than 22% but stayed well below the offer price because conditions remain, including Mozambican government consents and a tax ruling. IRH must make a firm offer or walk away by December 15, and may lend Kenmare up to $25 million until then. The price is far below a 530 pence proposal from a consortium last year.

2026-11-23-13.headline: Tesla proposes a $3.1 billion polysilicon plant in Texas to make the raw material for solar panels at home
2026-11-23-13.soWhat: Polysilicon is the first step of the solar supply chain, and China makes the vast majority of it, which leaves US panel makers exposed to tariffs and import bans. Building it at home would give Tesla's solar and storage business a supply that qualifies for US manufacturing credits and avoids forced-labor import rules. The plant only makes sense with subsidies, because Chinese polysilicon is far cheaper. The open question is whether US policy support lasts long enough for a 2030 start to pay off.

sources.title: PV Tech: Tesla plans US$3.1 billion polysilicon facility in Texas by 2030
GV Wire/Reuters: Tesla proposes $3.1 billion Texas polysilicon plant

2026-11-23-13.summary: Tesla has applied for a Texas tax incentive for a $3.1 billion plant near Robstown in Nueces County to make solar-grade polysilicon, a material mostly produced in China. The cost includes about $1.5 billion for engineering and construction and $1.4 billion for equipment, with building planned from 2027 and operations from 2030. Tesla told officials it would not invest in Texas without a property-tax deal under the state's JETI program, and it has not made a final investment decision. The plant would supply a separate $10.1 billion Tesla factory near Houston that would make solar ingots, wafers and cells.

2026-11-23-14.headline: Kymera jumps about 29% as its eczema pill matches injectable results in a mid-stage trial
2026-11-23-14.soWhat: Eczema and asthma treatment is dominated by Sanofi and Regeneron's injectable Dupixent, which blocks the same allergy signaling pathway that KT-621 targets. A pill with similar results would be easier for patients and could take share, which is why big drugmakers watch oral rivals closely. Data at this stage still has to hold up in larger Phase 3 trials, and safety over longer use is the key unknown. Strong results also make Kymera a likely partnership or takeover target.

sources.title: Investing.com: Kymera shares jump 29% after positive midstage eczema trial
Dermatology Times: Oral STAT6 degrader KT-621 meets Phase 2b goals

2026-11-23-14.summary: Kymera Therapeutics said its oral drug KT-621, which breaks down the STAT6 protein that drives allergic inflammation, met all goals in a Phase 2b trial in moderate-to-severe eczema. At the middle dose, eczema severity scores fell 72% after 16 weeks against 27% on placebo, and 62% of patients reached a 75% improvement against 22%. Shares rose about 29% before the market opened, adding close to $3 billion of market value. Kymera plans a first Phase 3 trial by mid-2027 and expects asthma data in late 2027.

2026-11-23-15.headline: OKX and NYSE owner ICE launch 24/7 tokenized stock trading, but 56 of the 62 companies first proposed refused
2026-11-23-15.soWhat: Tokenization promises trading at any hour and faster settlement, and having ICE involved gives the idea mainstream backing. But listed companies want control over where and how their shares trade, and the objections show they will not accept it without a say. For now the market is small and dominated by crypto companies, so traditional exchanges and brokers face little threat. The open question is whether the SEC makes the exemption permanent and whether issuers start tokenizing their own shares.

sources.title: CNBC: Stock market today live updates
Cointelegraph: OKXICE to launch 24/7 tokenized stock trading despite issuer objections

2026-11-23-15.summary: OKXICE, a venture between crypto exchange OKX and NYSE owner Intercontinental Exchange, began offering round-the-clock trading of tokenized stocks to eligible US customers on Monday. It operates under a temporary SEC 'Innovation Exemption' that lets companies block third-party tokens of their shares by objecting within 30 days, and 56 of the 62 companies it first proposed did so, including JPMorgan, McDonald's and Coca-Cola. The venue instead opens with more than 70 assets, including 59 ETFs and tokens of crypto-linked firms such as Coinbase, Circle, Robinhood and Strategy. Tokenized stocks and ETFs worldwide were worth about $3.88 billion in mid-November.

2026-11-24-01.headline: Sanofi agrees to buy Insmed for $41 billion in cash, the biggest pharma deal in three years
numbers: Premium: ~17% to Monday's close, ~46% to pre-leak price
2026-11-24-01.soWhat: Large drugmakers buy launched, fast-growing medicines to replace sales they will lose when patents expire, and Sanofi's biggest seller, Dupixent, faces that cliff early next decade. Paying roughly 38 times Brinsupri's year-to-date sales shows how scarce proven growth assets are, which rewards biotech investors and raises takeover values for other mid-sized respiratory companies. The open question is whether Brinsupri keeps growing fast enough to justify the price, since Sanofi only expects the deal to add to earnings per share by the end of 2028.

sources.title: Sanofi press release (SEC Form 6-K)
Startup Fortune: Sanofi agrees to buy Insmed for $175 a share
CNBC: Stocks making the biggest moves Tuesday

2026-11-24-01.summary: Sanofi will pay $175 a share in cash for Insmed, an equity value of about $41 billion (€37.6 billion). The price is about 17% above Monday's close of $149.09 and roughly 46% above where the stock traded before talks were reported on November 19. Insmed's main drug, Brinsupri, a pill for the lung disease bronchiectasis launched in the US in August 2025, brought in $1.09 billion of sales in the first nine months of 2026. Sanofi also gets Arikayce, an inhaled antibiotic with $434 million of 2025 sales, and a late-stage inhaled drug called TPIP. The deal is funded with cash and new debt and is expected to close in the first half of 2027.

2026-11-24-02.headline: US prepares new tariffs on China, the EU and 14 other economies to replace levies struck down by the Supreme Court
numbers: Economies under investigation: 16 (China, EU and 14 others)
Nasdaq 100 futures: about -2.4% on the report
China's paused retaliatory tariff: 24% (pause runs to January)
2026-11-24-02.soWhat: Section 301 tariffs follow a formal investigation, which makes them harder to overturn in court than the emergency tariffs that were struck down and are now being refunded to importers. For companies that source from China, the relief from those refunds may be short-lived, and planning for 2027 prices and supply chains gets harder. The open question is how high the rates go and whether China responds by ending its pause on a 24% retaliatory tariff, which it extended only to January.

sources.title: TMGM: US prepares new tariffs on China and other trading partners (WSJ)
Bloomberg: US readies tariff hike on China, EU goods
Yahoo Finance: China extends pause on 24% US tariffs to January

2026-11-24-02.summary: The US is preparing to raise tariffs on China, the European Union and other trading partners, the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer could publish the findings of a months-long trade investigation covering China, the EU and 14 other countries as soon as this week. The case argues that government subsidies have created excess factory capacity that lets producers sell cheaply abroad, and China is expected to face the highest rates. Bloomberg reported the new duties would use Section 301 trade law to replace tariffs the Supreme Court struck down. Nasdaq 100 futures fell about 2.4% on the report, giving back part of Monday's rally.

2026-11-24-03.headline: Brent slips below $90 to a three-month low as Libyan and Gulf supply outweighs Hormuz attacks
2026-11-24-03.soWhat: The market is now pricing a coming glut more heavily than the risk of disruption, which is why even mine strikes on tankers no longer lift prices for long. That squeezes producers with higher costs and puts pressure on OPEC+ to choose between cutting output to defend prices and holding market share.
