Refiners and fuel buyers gain if crude stays cheap while product prices hold. The open question is whether OPEC+ trims its 2027 targets on Sunday or lets prices fall toward the high $70s.

sources.title: Korea Times (Reuters): Oil falls around 3% on increased Middle East flows, Libyan pipeline restart
CNBC: Stock market live updates, Nov 24

2026-11-24-03.summary: Brent crude fell 2.8% to $89.95 a barrel on Monday and US crude (WTI) fell 3.2% to $80.73, after touching their lowest levels since late August. The restart of Libya's Sharara oil pipeline and rising flows from the Middle East outweighed attacks on shipping and refineries in the Gulf. Prices stayed near those lows on Tuesday, with Brent around $89, even after three tankers hit naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz. JPMorgan expects a supply surplus to push prices into the high $70s in the first half of 2027. OPEC+ ministers meet on November 29 to set output policy for 2027.

2026-11-24-04.headline: Dick's, Abercrombie, Kohl's and Best Buy beat forecasts and raise outlooks heading into the holidays
numbers: Best Buy comparable sales: +6.1%, best in five years
2026-11-24-04.soWhat: The results show US shoppers are still spending going into the holiday season, but the gains go to retailers with a clear edge in a category, not to stores across the board. Part of the margin boost is one-off: refunds of tariffs the Supreme Court struck down lifted Abercrombie's earnings by about $0.40 a share, and new tariffs being prepared could reverse that next year. The open question is whether demand holds if the Federal Reserve raises rates in December, as markets now expect.

sources.title: Abercrombie & Fitch Q3 fiscal 2026 results (GlobeNewswire via Manila Times)
CNBC: Stocks making the biggest moves Tuesday
CNBC: Stock market live updates, Nov 24

2026-11-24-04.summary: Several US retailers reported better-than-expected third quarters on Tuesday. Dick's Sporting Goods earned $1.94 a share on an adjusted basis against about $1.40 expected, with revenue up 23% to $5.13 billion, and its shares rose more than 16%. Abercrombie & Fitch posted record sales of $1.44 billion, up 11%, and an operating margin of 15.5%, helped by about $20 million of refunded tariffs; it raised its full-year profit forecast and the stock jumped about 22%. Kohl's revenue of $3.5 billion beat the $3.39 billion forecast, and Best Buy's comparable sales rose 6.1%, its best in five years.

2026-11-24-05.headline: Anthropic dips below its $83 IPO price three trading days after the largest listing on record
2026-11-24-05.soWhat: Trading below the IPO price matters because it hurts investors who bought in the offering and makes the next large AI listings harder to price. The split with Monday's chip rally shows investors separating companies that sell AI hardware from model developers that must keep spending heavily on computing before profits arrive. The open question is whether the weaker share price limits how cheaply Anthropic can raise further capital for data centers.

sources.title: CP24 (Reuters): Anthropic breaks below US$83 IPO price as debut rally unravels
CNBC: Stocks making the biggest moves Tuesday

2026-11-24-05.summary: Anthropic shares fell as much as about 6% before the market opened on Tuesday, dropping below their $83 IPO price before recovering to around $83. The company raised $93.5 billion in its listing, the largest IPO on record, ahead of SpaceX's $85.7 billion in June. The stock opened at $111.50 on its November 19 debut, 34% above the offer price, and closed that day at $97.17. It then missed Monday's broad AI rally. Reports tied the slide to a wider tech selloff, worries about stretched AI valuations and rising interest rates that make heavy computing spending more expensive.

2026-11-24-06.headline: HPE's AI server sales jump 69% and guidance tops forecasts, but shares fall 11% on margin worries
2026-11-24-06.soWhat: AI server makers grow fast but keep a thin slice of the value, because most of the price of a system goes to the GPUs and memory they buy in. When memory and chip costs rise faster than server prices, the assembler's margin shrinks even as sales soar, and the profit stays with suppliers such as Nvidia and the memory makers. The open question is whether HPE's networking business, which earns higher margins, can grow fast enough to offset the squeeze.

sources.title: Investing.com: HPE delivers quarterly results beat, raises guidance
CNBC: Stocks making the biggest moves Tuesday

2026-11-24-06.summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise reported fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $14.55 billion and adjusted earnings of $1.43 a share, both above forecasts. Its cloud and AI segment, which includes servers, grew 68.6% to $11.26 billion, and networking grew 12.3% to $3.06 billion. HPE forecast fiscal 2027 revenue of $59.4 billion to $63.1 billion, well above the roughly $55 billion analysts expected, and added $5 billion to its share buyback. Shares still fell about 11% on Tuesday after rising about 17% on Monday, as analysts said the outlook implies lower gross margins because of price pressure and higher component costs.

2026-11-24-07.headline: ABB buys German fan maker Ziehl-Abegg for $2.65 billion to grow in data center cooling
2026-11-24-07.soWhat: Every AI data center needs large amounts of cooling, so fans and motors that move air efficiently have become a growth market rather than a mature one. Buyers like ABB pay a high multiple for low-margin businesses because they expect to raise margins through scale, purchasing and their own drives and service networks. It is the second large fan-maker deal in weeks after EBM-Papst's sale to Madison Air, leaving fewer independent suppliers.

sources.title: Investing.com (Reuters): ABB to acquire Germany's Ziehl-Abegg for $2.65 billion
Handelsblatt: ABB übernimmt Ventilatorenhersteller für 2,65 Milliarden Dollar

2026-11-24-07.summary: ABB agreed to buy Ziehl-Abegg, a German maker of fans, motors and drives, at an enterprise value of $2.65 billion, or an equity value of about $2.2 billion. The price is 1.9 times Ziehl-Abegg's expected 2026 sales of about $1.4 billion and 18.6 times its earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization. Ziehl-Abegg's products cool data centers, clean rooms and industrial processes, and its margin is in the mid-single digits. ABB plans to lift that margin to the level of its own Motion division within three years. The deal is expected to close in the second half of 2027.

2026-11-24-08.headline: Petrobras returns to ethanol with a R$2.8 billion deal for 42% of corn ethanol maker Neomille
2026-11-24-08.soWhat: Brazil blends ethanol into all its gasoline and most of its cars can run on either fuel, so ethanol competes directly with the gasoline Petrobras refines. Owning both the pipeline and a share of production lets Petrobras capture margin along the whole chain instead of only selling fossil fuel. Corn ethanol is the fastest-growing part of the market because farmers in central Brazil grow corn as a cheap second crop after soy. The open question is how much of Petrobras's spending shifts from oil to low-carbon fuels over time.

sources.title: Petrobras filing (SEC Form 6-K): stake in Neomille

2026-11-24-08.summary: Brazil's state oil company Petrobras agreed to buy 42% of Neomille, the country's third-largest corn ethanol producer, for R$2.8 billion. That includes R$1.8 billion of new capital for Neomille and up to R$397 million in payments tied to future performance. Neomille, part of the CerradinhoBio group, has two plants with capacity of about 800 million liters of ethanol a year, expected to reach about 1.5 billion liters by 2028. The deal follows Petrobras's November 12 purchase of Logum, which runs Brazil's main ethanol pipeline network. Petrobras also plans to use the ethanol and corn oil to make sustainable aviation fuel.

2026-11-24-09.headline: Fluence's battery backlog hits a record $8.9 billion as data centers seek faster power, despite a $274 million loss
2026-11-24-09.soWhat: Batteries are one of the quickest ways to add usable power for data centers and grids that cannot wait years for new plants and transmission lines, which is why orders are surging. But the business is a contract manufacturer with thin margins, so factory problems and component costs can turn strong demand into losses. The open question is whether Fluence can turn its backlog into deliveries at a profit as its new US factories ramp up.

sources.title: Startup Fortune: Fluence Energy shares jump after a record $8.9 billion backlog

2026-11-24-09.summary: Fluence Energy, which builds large battery storage systems, reported a record order backlog of about $8.9 billion at September 30, up from $5.3 billion a year earlier. It booked $3.5 billion of orders in the fourth quarter and more than $6.2 billion in the fiscal year. Revenue fell 29% in the quarter to $744 million because factory delays pushed deliveries into next year, and the company lost $273.9 million for the year. Its gross margin in the quarter was negative 5%. Shares rose about 10% on Monday and gained further after hours.

2026-11-24-10.headline: Copper drops 3% and mining shares slide as a firmer dollar and rate-hike bets hit metals
2026-11-24-10.soWhat: Copper has become a bet on AI data centers and power grids, so its price now swings with tech sentiment as well as with Chinese demand. Miners' profits move much more than the metal price because their costs are largely fixed, which is why their shares fall faster than copper. The open question is whether the expected Fed hike and a stronger dollar keep pressure on metals into 2027.

sources.title: Rallies.ai: Copper miners fall as metal prices retreat
CNBC: Stock market live updates, Nov 24

2026-11-24-10.summary: Benchmark copper on the London Metal Exchange fell 3% to $12,117 a metric ton on Tuesday, giving back part of Monday's jump of as much as 5.3% after Nvidia's leadership news lifted AI-linked assets. A firmer dollar weighed on metals, and gold and silver also fell. Mining shares dropped in Europe and the US: BHP fell 3.1%, Rio Tinto 2.3%, Freeport-McMoRan 3.5% and Teck Resources 4.4% in early trading. Money markets now price a quarter-point Federal Reserve rate hike in December, which tends to lift the dollar and weigh on commodities.

2026-11-24-11.headline: Opposition to the $85 billion Union Pacific–Norfolk Southern rail merger grows as 57 more parties object
2026-11-24-11.soWhat: The merger would create the first US railroad running from coast to coast, which the railroads say would speed freight that now changes hands in the middle of the country. Shippers fear higher rates and fewer options, because many plants and farms are served by only one railroad. Under its rules for large rail mergers, the board must find that a deal enhances competition, so the volume of objections makes heavy conditions, or a rejection, more likely. The open question is what conditions the railroads would accept.

sources.title: PR Newswire (Stop The Rail Merger Coalition): Manufacturers, farmers, railroads and unions unite against UP-NS merger

2026-11-24-11.summary: Fifty-seven more shippers, farm groups and others formally opposed Union Pacific's planned $85 billion merger with Norfolk Southern in the latest comment round at the Surface Transportation Board, according to a coalition fighting the deal. New opponents include Marathon Petroleum, Cleveland-Cliffs, J.B. Hunt and the American Farm Bureau Federation, and General Motors raised concerns. Rival railroads CSX, BNSF and CPKC also oppose it, and 28 state attorneys general have now filed objections. The coalition counts 97 parties calling for rejection and 142 asking for conditions if the deal is approved.

2026-11-24-12.headline: Partners Group investors approve splitting a €6.6 billion evergreen fund that had limited withdrawals
numbers: New withdrawal cap: 2.5% of NAV a quarter (from 5%)
2026-11-24-12.soWhat: Evergreen funds let individual investors buy into private assets and promise limited regular withdrawals, but the assets themselves can take years to sell. When too many investors want out at once, managers must either gate the fund or sell assets at a discount, and this split is a test of how that tension gets resolved. The outcome matters for the whole push by private markets firms into wealth management. The open question is how fast the run-off portfolio can return cash without selling assets cheaply.

sources.title: Global Banking & Finance (Reuters): Partners Group shareholders approve split of troubled SICAV fund
Bloomberg: Partners Group investors back €6.6 billion evergreen split

2026-11-24-12.summary: Investors in Partners Group's Global Value SICAV, a 19-year-old private equity fund sold mainly to wealthy individuals, approved splitting it into two portfolios, with 83% of votes in favor against a required two-thirds. One portfolio, about €1.5 billion, will keep investing for long-term growth, while the other, about €5.2 billion, will sell assets and pay out cash. Withdrawal limits for new share classes were halved to 2.5% of net asset value a quarter. Partners Group capped withdrawals in June after requests surged, which hit its share price, and its shares rose about 3% after the vote.

2026-11-24-13.headline: Government contractor Amentum ends the year with a $48 billion backlog and starts its first buyback
2026-11-24-13.soWhat: Government services firms win multi-year contracts and earn a thin margin on the labor and services they supply, so a large backlog gives unusual visibility into future revenue. Profit growth comes mainly from winning higher-margin technology work and cutting debt rather than from fast sales growth. The open question is how US budget pressure and agency workforce changes affect new contract awards in 2027.

sources.title: Amentum fiscal 2026 results (SEC Form 8-K)

2026-11-24-13.summary: Amentum, which provides engineering, technology and support services to the US and allied governments, reported fiscal 2026 revenue of $13.8 billion, down 4%, and fourth-quarter revenue of $3.62 billion, down 8% because the prior year had an extra week. Adjusted earnings per share rose 13% to $0.71 in the quarter, and adjusted EBITDA for the year was $1.13 billion, an 8.2% margin. Its backlog reached $48.3 billion, about 3.5 times annual revenue. The company forecast fiscal 2027 revenue of $13.8 billion to $14.05 billion, approved its first $500 million share buyback, and its shares jumped after hours.

2026-11-24-14.headline: Zoom starts paying a dividend as enterprise sales grow at their fastest pace in 13 quarters
2026-11-24-14.soWhat: Once a fast-growing software company slows to single-digit growth but still generates strong cash, returning cash through dividends and buybacks becomes the main way to reward shareholders. Zoom's mix is shifting toward large customers buying phone, contact-center and AI tools, while the consumer side that boomed in the pandemic shrinks. The open question is whether enterprise growth can speed up enough to lift total growth above about 5%.

sources.title: Zoom Q3 fiscal 2027 results (SEC Form 8-K)

2026-11-24-14.summary: Zoom reported quarterly revenue of $1.29 billion, up 4.9% from a year earlier. Sales to enterprise customers rose 8.6% to $805 million, their fastest growth in 13 quarters, while its online business for individuals and small firms slipped 0.6% to $485 million. Free cash flow was $558 million. Zoom started a quarterly dividend of $0.25 a share, payable December 17, and expects full-year revenue of about $5.1 billion.

2026-11-24-15.headline: Alabama sets new rules for data center power contracts to keep other customers from paying their costs
numbers: Automatic approval: if no vote within 90 days
AEP Ohio comparison: exit fee of 36 months of minimum charges
2026-11-24-15.soWhat: Utilities must build plants and wires years before a data center reaches full demand, and if the customer leaves early, other ratepayers can be left paying for that investment. States are now writing rules on minimum terms, exit fees and collateral; AEP Ohio, for example, charges data centers that leave after five years an exit fee equal to 36 months of minimum bills. These rules shape where data centers are built and how fast utilities can grow their regulated asset base. The open question is whether case-by-case review protects households as well as fixed minimum terms would.

sources.title: Daily Caller: Alabama Power's data center deals face new electricity cost rules

2026-11-24-15.summary: Alabama Power's revised rate schedule for large data centers took effect on Monday after a Public Service Commission order. It covers data centers that reserve at least 150 megawatts at one site, and the commission will review each contract's length, minimum payments, upfront money and collateral. Alabama Power cannot price a contract below the extra cost of serving the site, and contracts are approved automatically if the commission does not vote within 90 days. The utility must publicly name the customer, its location and the maximum capacity reserved. Critics say the order sets no minimum financial terms and keeps contract details confidential.

2026-11-25-01.headline: US inflation climbs to 3.8% and growth hits 4.3%, cementing bets on a December Fed rate hike as stocks slide
numbers: Proposed tariffs: up to 20% on 14 economies
2026-11-25-01.soWhat: Strong growth combined with rising inflation is the mix that pushes a central bank to raise rates rather than cut, which lifts borrowing costs for companies, home buyers and governments. Higher rates hit long-duration assets hardest: fast-growing tech stocks whose profits lie far in the future, real estate and highly indebted firms. New tariffs stacked on existing ones would add to goods prices just as inflation is already climbing. The open question is whether one hike is enough or whether markets start pricing a longer tightening cycle in 2027.

sources.title: Yahoo Finance: Stock market today, Nov 25
TipRanks: Wall Street braces for inflation data

2026-11-25-01.summary: The Fed's preferred inflation gauge, the PCE price index, rose 0.3% in October and 3.8% from a year earlier, the fastest annual pace since 2023. Core PCE, which strips out food and energy, rose 3.3%, above the 3.2% economists expected. Third-quarter GDP was revised up to a 4.3% annual growth rate from a first estimate of 3.4%, and futures markets put the odds of a quarter-point Fed rate hike in December at about 98%. The same morning the administration proposed new tariffs of up to 20% on China, the EU and 12 other trading partners, which could take effect in January at the earliest. US stocks fell sharply in morning trading, with the S&P 500 down about 2.3% and the Nasdaq down about 3.3%.

2026-11-25-02.headline: Dell's revenue doubles to $54.9 billion as AI server orders lift its backlog to $132 billion
2026-11-25-02.soWhat: Dell assembles servers around Nvidia chips and sells them to cloud companies, AI labs and large enterprises, so its backlog is a direct read on how much AI infrastructure is still being ordered. The catch is that AI servers carry thin margins, reported in the mid-single digits, because most of the value goes to the chipmaker, so revenue grows much faster than profit. A $132 billion backlog gives visibility into 2027 even as investors question AI spending. The open question is whether buyers keep converting orders into deliveries if funding for AI projects tightens.

sources.title: CNBC: Dell earnings beat on AI strength
The Next Web: Dell's revenue doubles to $54.9bn

2026-11-25-02.summary: Dell's revenue for the quarter to late October rose 103% to a record $54.9 billion, well above the $49.3 billion analysts expected, and adjusted earnings per share of $9.45 beat forecasts of $6.59. Sales of AI-optimized servers rose 291% to $22 billion, and Dell booked $60.2 billion of new AI orders, leaving a record $132.3 billion backlog. It raised its AI server forecast for the year to $78 billion and its full-year revenue outlook to about $202 billion. The board added $25 billion to its share buyback, though PC sales of $12.9 billion missed estimates.

2026-11-25-03.headline: Analog Devices sinks 17% on a cautious outlook, leading an 8% fall in chip stocks
2026-11-25-03.soWhat: Analog chips that manage power and sensors go into cars, factory equipment and power grids, so they recover later and more slowly than AI chips after customers work down their stockpiles. Analog Devices' inventory rising to 141 days and a big capacity build that will not produce chips until 2028 raise worries about costs before demand fully returns. When a stock trades at about 37 times earnings, a small guidance miss can cause a large drop. The open question is whether industrial and auto demand is truly recovering or just being restocked.

sources.title: Startup Fortune: Analog Devices falls 17% after an earnings beat
Motley Fool: Why Analog Devices stock fell nearly 20%

2026-11-25-03.summary: Analog Devices reported quarterly revenue of $4.37 billion, up 42% from a year earlier, and adjusted earnings of $4.06 a share, both above forecasts. But it guided to first-quarter earnings of $3.82 a share, below the roughly $3.88 analysts expected, and plans to more than double capital spending to $1.6 billion to $1.9 billion next fiscal year. Its shares closed down about 17%, Texas Instruments fell about 7.6% in sympathy, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 7.9%. Nvidia lost about 5.9% as part of its rally on Jensen Huang's return as CEO faded.

2026-11-25-04.headline: Copper plunges 5.3% in a day and nears a bear market as AI spending doubts spread to metals
2026-11-25-04.soWhat: Copper's 2026 rally rested partly on expected demand from data centers and the power grid, so the AI sell-off in stocks is now hitting the metal too. Miners' profits move more than the copper price because their costs are largely fixed, which is why miner shares often fall harder than the metal. Physical buyers are still paying extra for metal available right away, which suggests the drop is driven more by investor sentiment than by a glut of copper. The open question is whether the fall lasts long enough to delay new mine projects, which would tighten supply later.

sources.title: Stock Analysis: Copper nears bear market after a 5% drop
MINING.COM: Copper price erases Nvidia rebound

2026-11-25-04.summary: Three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange fell 5.3% on Tuesday to $11,826 a tonne, its steepest drop in months, and slipped further to about $11,738 on Wednesday. That leaves the metal close to 20% below the record near $15,000 it reached in September, the usual definition of a bear market, and down about 16% in November. Southern Copper fell 4.5% and Freeport-McMoRan 4.0%. Traders cited doubts about AI-related spending, softer Chinese demand, an expected December Fed rate hike and the threat of new US tariffs.

2026-11-25-05.headline: Equinor signs an 18-year gas supply deal with Germany's VNG, its longest contract since 1986
numbers: Volume: up to 15.3 TWh a year (~1.4 bcm)
Pricing: market-linked at Trading Hub Europe
Uniper deal (Aug): 30+ TWh a year to 2041
2026-11-25-05.soWhat: After losing Russian pipeline gas, German buyers relied heavily on short-term and spot purchases, which left them exposed to price spikes like this year's after Gulf supply was disrupted. Long contracts with a nearby pipeline supplier give buyers security of supply and give Equinor a guaranteed outlet for its Norwegian fields for nearly two decades. Because prices follow the market, the deal secures volume, not a fixed price, so buyers still carry price risk. It also signals that German buyers expect to need gas well into the 2040s despite climate targets.

sources.title: Offshore Technology: Equinor agrees 18-year gas supply contract with VNG
Enerdata: Equinor secures gas supply agreement with VNG

2026-11-25-05.summary: Norway's Equinor agreed to supply Germany's VNG with up to 15.3 terawatt-hours of natural gas a year, about 1.4 billion cubic meters, from January 1, 2027 through 2044. The gas will be delivered at Germany's trading hub, Trading Hub Europe, and priced in line with market prices. Equinor called it its longest gas sales agreement since the Troll contracts of 1986. It follows a 15-year deal with Uniper in August covering more than 30 terawatt-hours a year.

2026-11-25-06.headline: StarHub agrees to merge with M1 in an all-share deal, cutting Singapore to three big mobile operators
2026-11-25-06.soWhat: Singapore's telecom market has four network operators serving fewer than 7 million people, and price wars led by cheap digital brands have squeezed profits. Merging two of them removes duplicate networks, shops and staff, which is where most savings in telecom deals come from, and should ease price competition. The losers could be customers if prices rise, which is why the regulator's view matters. Paying in shares lets Keppel exit M1's day-to-day running while keeping a stake in the upside.

sources.title: Investing.com: StarHub to acquire M1 in S$5 billion all-stock deal
Growbeansprout: StarHub and M1 to merge

2026-11-25-06.summary: Singapore's StarHub will combine with M1, the mobile operator controlled by Keppel, by issuing about 651.7 million new shares to M1's owners, or about 27.4% of the enlarged company. The combined group will have an enterprise value of about S$5 billion ($3.87 billion), and StarHub will take on about S$380 million of M1's net debt. Keppel will own about 23% of the merged company and must keep its shares for at least 12 months. The deal needs approval from Singapore's media regulator IMDA and shareholders and is expected to close in the first half of 2027.

2026-11-25-07.headline: Deere's large-farm equipment sales drop 15%, but it forecasts a North American recovery in 2027
2026-11-25-07.soWhat: Big tractors and combines are bought when farm incomes are strong, so two years of low crop prices and high interest rates have cut orders. Deere's forecast of a recovery in large equipment suggests dealers have worked down excess stock and farmers are ready to replace aging fleets. Construction equipment, helped by infrastructure and data center building, has partly offset the farm slump. The open question is whether a December rate hike, which raises the cost of financing machines, slows that recovery.

sources.title: Deere press release (PR Newswire)
MarketBeat: Deere Q4 2026 earnings

2026-11-25-07.summary: Deere earned $1.05 billion, or $3.89 a share, in its fiscal fourth quarter, down slightly from a year earlier, as revenue fell 2% to $12.1 billion. Sales of large farm machinery fell 15% and that unit's operating profit dropped 33%, while small tractors rose 10% and construction equipment rose 12%. Full-year profit fell 3% to $4.86 billion. For fiscal 2027 Deere forecast net income of $4.5 billion to $5.25 billion and expects US and Canadian large-farm equipment demand to rise 5% to 15%.

2026-11-25-08.headline: China's Xiamen Airlines orders 50 Boeing 737 jets worth $7.4 billion at list prices
numbers: China Southern Airbus order: 137 A320neo family
2026-11-25-08.soWhat: Chinese airlines stopped taking Boeing jets during the 2025 trade war, so new orders show how closely aircraft sales track US-China politics. China is expected to be one of the largest sources of new plane demand over the next two decades, and splitting orders between Boeing and Airbus lets Beijing reward or pressure either side. Deliveries starting in 2031 show how full both makers' order books are. For Boeing, the order adds backlog but not near-term cash, which depends on raising 737 output.

sources.title: CNBC: China's Xiamen Airlines to buy 50 Boeing jets
MyNorthwest: Boeing lands 50-jet order in China

2026-11-25-08.summary: Xiamen Airlines, a unit of China Southern Airlines, agreed to buy 50 Boeing 737-8 jets with a combined list price of about $7.4 billion, to be delivered from 2031 to 2034. The actual price will be lower after customary discounts, and the order still needs shareholder and Chinese government approval. It follows China's approval in May of an initial purchase of 200 Boeing planes, its first such commitment since 2017. China Southern also agreed to buy 137 Airbus A320neo-family jets.

2026-11-25-09.headline: Workday, Autodesk and Nutanix all beat forecasts, yet their shares fall as software stays out of favor
2026-11-25-09.soWhat: Investors worry that AI agents will reduce the number of human users that software companies charge for, which threatens the per-seat subscription model behind most business software. That is why results that beat forecasts no longer lift these shares unless future sales and cash flow accelerate. Money has moved from software makers to the hardware that runs AI. Lower valuations are also attracting private equity buyers, who can buy steady subscription businesses cheaply.

sources.title: CNBC: Stocks making the biggest moves Tuesday
Startup Fortune: Autodesk stock slips after earnings

2026-11-25-09.summary: Workday's quarterly revenue rose to $2.71 billion and adjusted earnings of $2.82 a share beat estimates, but free cash flow of $691 million missed the $712 million expected and its subscription guidance was light, sending shares down about 7% after hours. Autodesk beat forecasts with revenue of $2.16 billion and raised its full-year outlook, but its shares still fell more than 3%. Nutanix dropped more than 8% after saying its CEO will step down once a successor is found. Large software stocks such as Salesforce, Adobe and ServiceNow are down roughly 25% to 60% this year, while chip stocks are up.

2026-11-25-10.headline: Japan's JAPEX swaps into Norway's Goliat field as Equinor trims a non-operated stake
2026-11-25-10.soWhat: Big producers like Equinor prefer to own more of the fields they operate, where they control costs and timing, and sell down stakes in fields run by others. Asian buyers such as JAPEX want secure oil and gas supply outside the Middle East, which has become more valuable after this year's Gulf disruptions. Paying part of exploration well costs, known as a carry, is a common way for a newcomer to earn its way into promising acreage. Deals like this move North Sea assets to owners who value them most rather than adding new supply.

sources.title: OE Digital: Equinor, JAPEX agree Goliat-Verdande stake exchange
Equinor press release (Norwegian)

2026-11-25-10.summary: Equinor will transfer an 8% stake in the Goliat oil field in the Barents Sea to Japan Petroleum Exploration (JAPEX), cutting its holding from 35% to 27%. In return Equinor gets JAPEX's 3.5% stake in the Equinor-operated Verdande field, lifting its share to about 62.8%, plus $65 million in cash. JAPEX also takes 20% and 10% stakes in two exploration licenses and will pay part of Equinor's costs for wells planned there. Goliat is operated by Vår Energi, and the deal needs Norwegian government approval.

2026-11-25-11.headline: Clariant confirms talks with private equity firm CD&R to buy US specialty chemicals maker Ashland
2026-11-25-11.soWhat: Specialty chemicals sell small volumes of ingredients that improve a product, such as thickeners in shampoo or coatings on pills, and earn higher, steadier margins than bulk chemicals. Many of these makers have suffered from weak demand and cheap Chinese competition, which has pushed their share prices down and made them takeover targets. Teaming a strategic buyer with private equity lets each take the parts it wants and share the cost. Clariant's falling shares show investors worry about it taking on debt for a deal at a weak point in the cycle.

sources.title: Investing.com (Reuters): Clariant, CD&R in talks to buy Ashland
Personal Care Magazine: Clariant confirms interest in Ashland takeover

2026-11-25-11.summary: Swiss chemicals group Clariant said it is in talks to acquire Ashland together with buyout firm Clayton, Dubilier & Rice, but warned that no deal is certain. Bloomberg reported an all-cash deal valuing Ashland at about $3.4 billion. Ashland, which makes ingredients for personal care, medicines and coatings, has been exploring a sale since August under pressure from activist investors, with interest from several private equity firms. Clariant's shares fell 2.9% to 9.95 Swiss francs after the confirmation.

2026-11-25-12.headline: Volkswagen's first wage talks end without a deal as workers threaten strikes from January
numbers: VW ask: pay freeze for 2027 and 2028
2026-11-25-12.soWhat: Labor is one of the biggest costs for carmakers in Germany, where wages are among the highest in the world, while Chinese rivals, US tariffs and the shift to electric cars are squeezing prices. A pay freeze would protect Volkswagen's thin margins, but strikes would cost output during a weak market. Other German suppliers such as Bosch and Schaeffler face similar disputes, so the outcome sets a pattern for the country's car industry. The open question is whether the union trades pay restraint for job guarantees, as it did in 2024.

sources.title: GV Wire (Reuters): Volkswagen workers threaten strikes after first wage talks
just-auto: Volkswagen seeks pay freeze as IG Metall talks begin

2026-11-25-12.summary: Volkswagen and the IG Metall union ended their first round of German wage talks in Emden without agreement. Volkswagen wants to freeze pay for 2027 and 2028, lengthen working hours at the same pay when needed and cut some bonuses, while the union is asking for a 5% raise over 12 months. About 4,500 workers protested outside, and the union warned of strikes from January if no deal is reached at the next meeting on December 15. Volkswagen expects an operating margin of no more than 1% this year, down from 5.9% in 2024.

2026-11-25-13.headline: HLD plans a €4.60-a-share offer for French care-home operator Clariane, sending its shares up 36%
2026-11-25-13.soWhat: Clariane, formerly Korian, runs nursing homes and clinics and was hit by heavy debt and a scandal at a rival that hurt trust in the French care-home sector. Care homes have high fixed costs for staff and buildings and depend on regulated fees, so investors with long horizons can wait for occupancy and pricing to recover. A controlling group gives the company a stable owner to back a turnaround. Minority shareholders get a premium exit, but those who stay depend on the new owners' plans.

sources.title: Yahoo Finance: Plans to establish a controlling stake in Clariane
MLQ: HLD plans a €4.60-a-share tender offer for Clariane

2026-11-25-13.summary: Investment firm HLD Europe and Crédit Agricole Assurances, which own about 27% and 26% of Clariane, plan to act together as a controlling 53% shareholder group. HLD will then make a mandatory cash offer of €4.60 a share, a 38% premium to the last close of €3.33, valuing the company at about €1.6 billion. The offer is not meant to take Clariane off the stock market, and filing is expected in the first half of 2027. Clariane's shares jumped about 36% to around €4.52.

2026-11-25-14.headline: Smucker raises its profit outlook as Uncrustables pass $1 billion, even as cheaper coffee cuts sales
2026-11-25-14.soWhat: Packaged food companies pass commodity costs through to shoppers, so when coffee beans get cheaper, revenue falls but profit margins can widen. That is why Smucker's earnings jumped while sales slipped. Growth now comes from a few strong brands such as Uncrustables and Café Bustelo, while much of the rest of the portfolio is flat. Investors want proof that sales, not just margins, can grow.

sources.title: SEC: Smucker Q2 FY27 results (8-K)
FoodNavigator: Uncrustables, Café Bustelo hit milestones

2026-11-25-14.summary: J.M. Smucker's quarterly net sales fell 2% to $2.3 billion, while adjusted earnings rose 52% to $3.20 a share, including a 22-cent benefit from tariff refunds. Coffee sales fell 5% because the company passed lower green coffee costs on to shoppers through lower prices. Its Uncrustables frozen sandwiches passed $1 billion in annual sales, and it raised its full-year adjusted earnings forecast to $10.80 to $11.20 a share. The shares fell about 3% before the market opened because the sales outlook was unchanged.

2026-11-25-15.headline: Couche-Tard's fuel margins lift earnings as its Żabka takeover in Poland nears completion
2026-11-25-15.soWhat: Convenience store chains make much of their profit from the margin on each liter of fuel, which tends to widen when wholesale prices fall faster than pump prices. That buffer is helping while shoppers spend cautiously inside the stores. Żabka adds a fast-growing, mostly non-fuel chain in Poland, which reduces Couche-Tard's reliance on gasoline as electric cars spread. The open question is how fast Żabka's growth offsets slow in-store sales in North America.

sources.title: Couche-Tard Q2 FY27 results (Newswire)
Investing.com: Couche-Tard earnings call transcript

2026-11-25-15.summary: Alimentation Couche-Tard, which owns Circle K, said adjusted earnings per share rose 7.7% to $0.84 in the quarter to October 11, beating forecasts of about $0.80. In-store sales rose 1.7% to $4.8 billion and same-store merchandise sales rose 1.5%, while gross profit from road fuel rose 5.6% to $1.79 billion as margins improved in all regions. Its offer for Polish convenience chain Żabka became unconditional after final regulatory approvals, and holders of about 57% of shares have agreed to sell. Reported earnings fell because of currency losses tied to the Żabka deal.

2026-11-25-16.headline: Activist Trian presses Solventum to spin off its health data unit unless a sale tops $7 billion
numbers: Tax leakage on a sale: >$8 a share (Trian)
2026-11-25-16.soWhat: Medtech conglomerates often trade at a discount because investors struggle to value very different businesses together, so splitting them can unlock value. A health data and coding software unit has different growth, margins and buyers from wound care and dental products. Activists push for spin-offs over sales when taxes would eat into the proceeds. The open question is whether a buyer pays enough to beat a tax-free spin.

sources.title: Investing.com (Reuters): Trian presses Solventum to spin off health information unit
The Star: Peltz pushes Solventum to spin off HIS unit

2026-11-25-16.summary: Nelson Peltz's Trian Fund Management, which owns just under 5% of Solventum, urged the 3M spin-off to separate its Health Information Systems unit through a tax-free spin-off. Trian said a sale makes sense only if the price is well above the rumored $5.5 billion to $7 billion range, because a sale could cost more than $8 a share in taxes. Solventum said in August that it plans to separate the unit to focus on medical products. The company said the process is ongoing.

2026-11-26-01.headline: A US-led group agrees to buy Lukoil's foreign oil business, ending a year-long hunt for a buyer after sanctions
numbers: Payment: restricted Russian shares, held 5 years
2026-11-26-01.soWhat: Sanctions forced a sale of a large, integrated oil business, and the share-swap structure solves the core problem: how to pay a sanctioned seller without cash reaching Russia. Financial buyers rather than oil majors end up with the assets, so the first job is operational, restoring full refinery runs and keeping fuel flowing to markets such as Bulgaria, where Burgas is the largest refinery in the Balkans. Governments that host the assets gain certainty after a year in limbo. The open question is whether OFAC approves the terms, since an earlier agreement lapsed in July without Treasury sign-off.

sources.title: World Oil: U.S.-led consortium agrees to acquire Lukoil's international portfolio
The National: US-led group reaches deal to acquire Lukoil's global assets

2026-11-26-01.summary: A consortium led by investment firm Eldridge, with the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC), UAE-based Catena Investment Holding and Xtellus Partners, agreed to buy Lukoil International, the unit that holds the Russian company's assets outside Russia. The business produces about 350,000 barrels of oil equivalent a day in 11 countries, owns three European refineries with about 350,000 barrels a day of capacity (Burgas in Bulgaria, Zeeland in the Netherlands and Petrotel in Romania), the trading arm Litasco and more than 2,000 filling stations in 16 countries. The buyers pay with restricted shares in Lukoil and other Russian companies rather than cash, and the proceeds sit in a locked custodial account for five years or until sanctions are lifted. The DFC takes a stake for the US government at no upfront cost, and the deal still needs approval from the US Treasury's sanctions office (OFAC). ExxonMobil, Chevron, ADNOC and Carlyle had all looked at the assets after the US sanctioned Lukoil in late 2025.

2026-11-26-02.headline: The Dow claws back a 1,100-point drop to close higher as AI stocks recover, and Asian chip shares rebound on Thanksgiving
2026-11-26-02.soWhat: Markets are trying to separate the AI companies that will earn a return on their spending from those that will not, and the result is very large daily swings in a small group of stocks. A rotation into energy, telecom and other defensive shares shows investors still want to own equities, but with less exposure to AI capital spending. The backdrop is tough: inflation at 3.8% and a likely December Fed rate hike raise the bar for highly valued growth stocks. The open question is whether the late-day recovery holds once full trading resumes after the holiday.

sources.title: ABC News/AP: How major US stock indexes fared Wednesday 11/25/2026
Motley Fool: Dow erases 1,100-point loss
TradingKey: Japan, South Korea stocks; Kioxia surges

2026-11-26-02.summary: US stocks swung sharply on Wednesday before the Thanksgiving holiday. The Dow fell more than 1,100 points during the day but closed up 0.33% at 50,183, while the S&P 500 recovered from a 3.2% intraday fall to end down 0.3% at 7,182.78 and the Nasdaq, down as much as 4.6%, closed 0.6% lower at 23,585.80. Energy led the sectors and investors moved into defensive names such as Charter Communications, which rose 8.4%, while the 10-year Treasury yield eased to 4.91%. On Thursday, with US markets shut, Japan's Nikkei rose 0.9% to 57,499 as memory maker Kioxia jumped 12.6% and SoftBank Group gained 7.3% after heavy losses the day before.

2026-11-26-03.headline: Brent jumps 3.5% to $94.61 after the Houthis claim a strike on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery and export terminal
2026-11-26-03.soWhat: Oil is being pulled between two forces: a supply surplus that had pushed Brent to a three-month low, and attacks that threaten the Gulf's export points. An export terminal matters more than a single refinery because it controls how much Saudi crude reaches buyers, so even a short loading halt adds a risk premium. Producers outside the Gulf and tanker owners gain from higher prices and longer voyages, while refiners and airlines in Asia face higher crude costs. The open question is what OPEC+ decides for 2027 output at its November 29 meeting.

sources.title: CNBC: Oil prices and Hormuz, Nov 25 2026
CNN: Smoke seen from space after Houthis claim strike on Saudi refinery
Newsquawk: European market wrap, 25 November 2026

2026-11-26-03.summary: Brent crude rose 3.5% to settle at $94.61 a barrel on Wednesday and US WTI gained 2% to $83.68, a day after Brent touched its lowest level since August. Yemen's Houthis said they attacked Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia's largest refinery at about 550,000 barrels a day and next to one of the world's biggest crude export terminals. The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed four drones, but satellite images showed thick smoke and a shipping source said loadings at the terminal were suspended. Iran also said tankers hit naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, while US crude stocks rose 1.1 million barrels to 418.9 million.

2026-11-26-04.headline: S&P puts Nvidia's AA credit rating on watch for a cut, citing governance gaps after its CEO left and returned
numbers: Likely outcome: at most one notch, to AA-
2026-11-26-04.soWhat: For a company with Nvidia's cash flow, a one-notch cut barely changes borrowing costs, but it is a formal signal that governance has become a measurable risk. Large investors who track ratings and governance scores may hold less of the stock, and the episode shows how much the market value of a key supplier depends on one person. Rivals do not gain directly, but customers building AI data centers care about supplier stability. The open question is whether the board adds independent directors and a succession plan before S&P's review ends.

sources.title: Benzinga: S&P puts Nvidia on credit watch, Moody's leaves it unchanged
Yahoo Finance UK: S&P warns Nvidia's credit rating could be downgraded

2026-11-26-04.summary: S&P Global Ratings placed Nvidia's AA rating on CreditWatch with negative implications, saying the departure and reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang did not answer its questions about how the board oversees senior executives. S&P flagged board independence, oversight of management, handling of geopolitical risk and the lack of a succession plan, and lowered its management and governance assessment from positive to neutral. It said any downgrade would likely be one notch, to AA-, within about 90 days, and it left its view of Nvidia's finances unchanged. Moody's kept its Aa1 rating with a stable outlook, and Nvidia shares fell about 6% on Wednesday.

2026-11-26-05.headline: Dubai Islamic Bank agrees to buy Emirates Islamic in an all-share deal, creating a $159 billion Islamic lender
numbers: Swap ratio: 0.642 DIB shares per EI share
2026-11-26-05.soWhat: Islamic banks follow Sharia rules, earning returns through profit-sharing and lease structures rather than interest, and scale matters because funding and compliance costs are largely fixed. Emirates Islamic brings cheap funding: current and savings accounts make up about 63% of its deposits, against about a third at DIB, which lowers the cost of money the combined bank lends out. Emirates NBD swaps full control of a subsidiary for a stake in a larger rival. The open question is whether Emirates NBD's own shareholders see the share ratio as fair value for a profitable unit.

sources.title: The National: Dubai Islamic Bank to acquire Emirates Islamic
Arab News: DIB acquires Emirates Islamic to make second-largest Islamic banking group

2026-11-26-05.summary: Dubai Islamic Bank (DIB) agreed to acquire all of Emirates Islamic from its parent Emirates NBD, which will receive 0.642 new DIB shares for each Emirates Islamic share and become a significant DIB shareholder. The combined group would have about AED 585 billion ($159 billion) of assets, making it the second-largest listed Islamic banking group after Saudi Arabia's Al Rajhi Bank. No cash changes hands and the deal needs regulatory approval. DIB shares had risen about 11% on November 23 when the banks said their boards would consider the deal.

2026-11-26-06.headline: Britain's energy price cap rises 26% to £2,166 a year from January as wholesale gas costs climb
2026-11-26-06.soWhat: The UK cap passes wholesale costs through to households with a lag, so higher gas prices this autumn now reach bills just as winter demand peaks. Suppliers are protected from selling below cost, but more households fall behind on bills, raising bad-debt risk for retailers that already earn thin margins. A higher cap also adds to inflation that the Bank of England is trying to bring down. The open question is whether gas prices ease enough by the April cap to reverse part of the rise.

sources.title: Uswitch: January 2027 price cap to increase by 26%
EDF: Energy Price Cap to rise by 26% from January to March 2027
Newsquawk: European market wrap, 25 November 2026

2026-11-26-06.summary: Ofgem, the UK energy regulator, raised its price cap for January to March 2027 to £2,166 a year for a typical household that buys gas and electricity by direct debit, up £443 or 26% from £1,723. The figure came in above Cornwall Insight's forecast of £1,999 but below suppliers' average forecast of £2,219. The cap limits the price per unit of energy and the standing charge, not the total bill, so households that use more pay more. Dutch TTF gas, the European benchmark, traded between about €87 and €92 per megawatt hour on Wednesday.

2026-11-26-07.headline: Expedia agrees to buy Czech flight-booking site Kiwi.com, its fourth travel-technology deal in a row
2026-11-26-07.soWhat: Flights are a low-margin product for online travel agencies, but they bring customers who then book higher-margin hotels and car rentals. Kiwi's technology lets Expedia sell cheaper multi-airline routes in Europe and supply them to the travel firms that use its B2B platform. Low-cost airlines and rival agencies face a stronger competitor, while General Atlantic gets an exit. The open question is whether European regulators accept the deal after they blocked Booking Holdings' purchase of flight specialist Etraveli in 2023.

sources.title: Skift: Expedia to buy Kiwi.com
Expedia Group: Agreement to acquire Kiwi.com

2026-11-26-07.summary: Expedia Group agreed to buy Kiwi.com, a Brno-based online travel agency known for virtual interlining, which stitches together flights from airlines that have no agreement with each other into one itinerary. The price was not disclosed and the deal is expected to close in the first half of 2027. Kiwi.com's 2025 revenue was €227 million, about 20% below its 2023 peak of €284 million, and investor General Atlantic held 66.7% of its shares. Kiwi follows Expedia's purchases of Tiqets, CarTrawler and Layla, whose disclosed prices total $676 million, and Expedia's business-to-business revenue grew 23% to $1.71 billion last quarter.

2026-11-26-08.headline: Ambarella plunges about 30% as the memory shortage leads customers to delay orders for its camera chips
2026-11-26-08.soWhat: AI data centers are absorbing so much memory that makers of cameras, cars and other devices cannot get enough at a workable price, so they hold back their builds. That hurts companies like Ambarella that sell the other chips in those devices, even when demand from end users holds up. Memory makers gain pricing power, while device makers and their chip suppliers lose volume. The open question is how long the shortage lasts, since new memory factories take years to build.

sources.title: 24/7 Wall St: The memory shortage has a new victim
CNBC: Stocks making the biggest moves Wednesday

2026-11-26-08.summary: Chip designer Ambarella forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $70 million to $75 million, far below the $112 million analysts expected and about 37% below its third-quarter revenue of $115.2 million. Its CEO said scarce and expensive memory is leading customers in every end market to postpone or delay orders, with consumer products, about half of revenue, hit hardest, and that most of the cut is delays rather than cancellations. The shares fell about 29% to $31.54 on Wednesday after dropping more than 40% in late trading. Memory makers Micron and Sandisk also fell about 9% and 10% in the day's AI sell-off.

2026-11-26-09.headline: HP's revenue rises 9% to $16 billion as higher PC prices offset fewer units, though memory now makes up 40% of PC parts costs
numbers: Memory & storage: ~40% of PC parts cost
2026-11-26-09.soWhat: PC makers are passing the memory shortage on to buyers through higher prices, so revenue can grow even as fewer machines ship. That works for business customers buying premium AI-capable PCs, but consumer demand softened late in the quarter and retailers carried more stock. Memory suppliers capture much of the value, while PC makers' margins depend on how fast they can reprice. The open question is whether buyers keep paying more if memory costs keep rising into 2027.

sources.title: Futurum: HP Q4 FY 2026
HP Inc Form 8-K, Q4 FY2026 results
CNBC: Stocks making the biggest moves Wednesday

2026-11-26-09.summary: HP Inc's fourth-quarter revenue rose 9.3% to $16.0 billion and adjusted earnings of $0.83 a share beat the $0.75 analysts expected, helped by a $0.15 gain from tariff refunds. Personal Systems revenue grew 14% to $11.75 billion, and commercial PC revenue rose 23% even though units fell 28%, as customers bought pricier premium machines. Memory and storage reached nearly 40% of HP's PC component costs, up from 15% to 18% at the start of the year, and gross margin slipped to 17.5%. HP raised its dividend to $0.31 a share and its stock rose 11.5%.

2026-11-26-10.headline: GTA VI is estimated to have sold about 45 million copies in its first three days, a record pace for a video game
2026-11-26-10.soWhat: Big games now earn most of their money in the first weeks, and digital sales through console stores keep more revenue with the publisher than boxed copies did. A launch of this size can fund years of development and supports later income from online play and in-game purchases, which made GTA V one of the most profitable entertainment products ever. Sony also gains, since three-quarters of copies sold on PlayStation. The open question is how much of the launch carries into long-term online spending, which drives Take-Two's earnings after the first year.

sources.title: Investing.com: GTA VI hits 45.5M units sold in first 3 days
TipRanks/The Fly: GTA VI sold 44.9M units by end of weekend, says Alinea

2026-11-26-10.summary: Citi estimates that Grand Theft Auto VI sold about 45.5 million copies in its first three days, based on PlayStation data showing about 34.1 million on PS5 and an assumed 75/25 split with Xbox. Tracking firm Alinea Analytics put sales at 44.9 million by the end of the launch weekend. Citi said the game reached 1.4 times its first-day sales over three days, compared with about 1.25 times for GTA V. Publisher Take-Two has not confirmed the figures; the game launched with a reported 15.9 million pre-orders.

2026-11-26-11.headline: Ukrainian drones hit two Rosneft refineries in Samara, the latest of about 16 Russian refineries struck this month
2026-11-26-11.soWhat: Damaged distillation units cut Russia's output of diesel and gasoline, so more crude gets exported unrefined while domestic fuel supply tightens. That supports refining margins elsewhere, especially for diesel in Europe and Asia, benefiting refiners that are running well. Russian oil companies lose higher-value product sales and face costly repairs under sanctions that limit access to Western parts. The open question is whether talks on energy infrastructure lead to a pause in strikes on both sides.

sources.title: Kyiv Independent: Ukraine strikes 2 Russian oil refineries in Samara
UNITED24 Media: Drones strike two refineries with capacity of nearly 16 million tons
Newsquawk: European market wrap, 25 November 2026

2026-11-26-11.summary: Ukraine's military said drones struck Rosneft's Kuibyshev and Syzran refineries in Russia's Samara region overnight on November 25, damaging crude distillation units, a catalytic reformer and storage tanks. The two plants have a combined capacity of nearly 16 million tonnes a year, roughly 320,000 barrels a day. Ukraine has hit about 16 Russian refineries since the start of November, forcing some to halt and others to cut output. President Putin said Russia would respond and wants talks on protecting energy infrastructure, while Kazakhstan's oil output fell to 1.74 million barrels a day amid loading problems at the CPC export terminal.

2026-11-26-12.headline: Constellation completes the roughly $5 billion sale of 4.4 GW of gas plants to LS Power, a condition of its Calpine deal
numbers: LS Power gas fleet: ~11.5 GW with NRG deal
2026-11-26-12.soWhat: Regulators made Constellation sell plants so the merged company would not control too much generation in PJM, the largest US power market, where prices are set by competing plants. Private owners like LS Power are buying gas plants because data center demand has made dispatchable power more valuable. Constellation keeps the cash and its nuclear-heavy fleet, while the buyer takes on exposure to PJM's power and capacity prices. The open question is whether PJM prices stay high enough to justify the prices now being paid for gas plants.

sources.title: Rigzone: Constellation completes $5B sale of 4.4GW PJM assets
Business Wire: Constellation completes divestiture of legacy Calpine PJM assets

2026-11-26-12.summary: Constellation Energy completed the sale of about 4.4 gigawatts of mostly gas-fired power plants in the PJM grid region to LS Power, including the Bethlehem, York 1 and 2, Hay Road and Edge Moor plants in Pennsylvania and Delaware. Rigzone reported the price at about $5 billion before adjustments. The sale meets divestiture conditions set by the US Justice Department and federal power regulator FERC for Constellation's purchase of Calpine, which closed in January 2026. LS Power also bought the 606-megawatt Brazos Valley plant in Texas in October, and with a proposed NRG deal its gas fleet would reach about 11.5 gigawatts.

2026-11-26-13.headline: Global regulators move BNP Paribas into a higher capital bracket for systemically important banks
2026-11-26-13.soWhat: G-SIB buckets are set by a bank's size, global reach and links to other banks, so growing bigger raises the capital a bank must hold, which lowers its return on equity. Half a percentage point of extra capital on a bank of BNP's size ties up billions of euros that could otherwise be lent or returned to shareholders. Banks near a bucket line have a reason to manage their size, and MUFG gains room to lend or pay out. The open question is how BNP offsets the cost, through pricing, smaller trading books or slower growth.

sources.title: FSB: FSB publishes 2026 G-SIB list
Global Banking & Finance: BNP Paribas moves up global systemic bank list

2026-11-26-13.summary: The Financial Stability Board's 2026 list of global systemically important banks (G-SIBs) keeps the same 29 banks as last year but moves BNP Paribas up from bucket 2 to bucket 3. That raises the extra capital buffer BNP must hold from 1.5% to 2% of risk-weighted assets, starting on January 1, 2028. Japan's MUFG moves down to bucket 1, cutting its surcharge to 1%. Bucket 3 also includes Bank of America, Citigroup, HSBC and ICBC.

2026-11-26-14.headline: Hannover Re targets at least €2.9 billion of profit in 2027 as reinsurance renewals run late with price in focus
2026-11-26-14.soWhat: Reinsurers insure insurance companies, and the January 1 renewals set prices for a large share of the year's business. Late renewals and a focus on price mean buyers are pushing for cuts after several profitable years, so reinsurers are trading some margin for volume. A combined ratio below 85% means Hannover expects to keep about 15 cents of underwriting profit per euro of premium, before investment income. The open question is how far rates fall at January 1 and whether catastrophe losses stay within the bigger budget.

sources.title: Reinsurance News: Hannover Re raises net income target by 7% to €2.9bn
Global Reinsurance: Hannover Re targets €2.9bn net income for 2027

2026-11-26-14.summary: Hannover Re, one of the world's largest reinsurers, set a 2027 net income target of at least €2.9 billion, about 7% above its 2026 goal of at least €2.7 billion. For 2027 to 2029 it aims for a return on equity of at least 18% and average EBIT growth of at least 5% a year, with a property and casualty combined ratio below 85%. It raised its budget for large losses to €2.5 billion from €2.3 billion and kept paying out about 55% of profit as dividends. Its board said January renewals are running later than usual and talks focus mostly on price.

2026-11-26-15.headline: Maersk orders 12 dual-fuel ships of 24,000 containers each, the largest in its fleet, for delivery in 2030-31
2026-11-26-15.soWhat: Maersk had held back from ordering the largest ships while rivals such as MSC grew their fleets, so this order signals it wants to defend its share on the main Asia-Europe routes. Bigger ships lower the cost per container, but they only pay off when they sail full, and a wave of deliveries can push freight rates down for the whole industry. Shipyards in China gain more work, while smaller carriers face tougher cost competition. The open question is whether trade volumes in 2030 are strong enough to fill the new capacity.

sources.title: Splash247: Maersk storms into megamax league
Baird Maritime: Maersk orders 12 dual-fuel 24,000TEU containerships
Riviera: Maersk confirms first batch of 24,000-TEU order

2026-11-26-15.summary: A.P. Moller-Maersk confirmed it has ordered 12 container ships that can each carry 24,000 twenty-foot containers (TEU) and run on either LNG or conventional fuel, with deliveries in 2030 and 2031. Maersk did not disclose the shipyard or price; trade outlet Splash247 estimated the cost at about $2.9 billion, and Riviera reported that China's Hengli Heavy Industries is the likely builder, with options for 12 more ships. The ships will be the biggest Maersk has ordered. Freight forecasters expect transpacific container rates to keep easing and air cargo rates to fall next year.

2026-11-26-16.headline: Polestar's revenue falls 14% and its loss widens to $403 million as it winds down US sales
2026-11-26-16.soWhat: A negative gross margin means Polestar loses money on each car before paying for research, marketing and overhead, so selling more does not close the gap. Losing the US market removes high-priced sales just as competition from Chinese and established brands pushes prices down in Europe. Owner Geely and its lenders carry the funding burden, while rivals pick up customers. The open question is how long Polestar can keep funding losses with about $653 million of cash.

sources.title: Quartz: Polestar posted a wider loss as pricing and U.S. exit weighed
Grafa: Polestar Q3 revenue falls 14.3% to US$642 million

2026-11-26-16.summary: Electric carmaker Polestar reported third-quarter revenue of $642 million, down 14.3% from $749 million a year earlier, even though retail sales rose 1% to 14,371 cars. Its gross margin fell to minus 18.1% from minus 6.1%, and the net loss widened to $403 million from $365 million, as price cuts, a weaker model mix and charges tied to North American resale values weighed. Polestar is winding down most of its US business after being barred from selling new cars there from model year 2027. It ended the quarter with about $653 million of cash and kept its 2026 volume guidance.

2026-11-26-17.headline: Urban Outfitters posts record sales of $1.67 billion but falls 13% as Anthropologie slows
2026-11-26-17.soWhat: Clothing retailers are priced on comparable sales, which strip out new stores and show whether existing customers are buying more. Unsold stock that must be marked down is the main risk to margins, so slow-selling styles at Anthropologie matter more than the record total. Brands that read trends well, here Free People, keep pricing power. The open question is whether the holiday season clears Anthropologie's inventory without heavy discounts.

sources.title: Urban Outfitters Form 8-K, Q3 results
Yahoo Finance: Urban Outfitters stock falls as comparable sales growth slows
CNBC: Stocks making the biggest moves Wednesday

2026-11-26-17.summary: Urban Outfitters' third-quarter revenue rose 8.9% to a record $1.67 billion and earnings rose to $1.54 a share from $1.28, but comparable retail sales grew 4.4%, short of the roughly 5.3% analysts expected. Growth came from Free People's FP Group, up 8.5%, and the Urban Outfitters brand, up 5.8%, while Anthropologie grew just 1.7% as new styles were slow to sell and older stock needed deeper discounts. The company guided to mid-single-digit revenue growth for the holiday quarter with flat Anthropologie sales. The shares fell 13% on Wednesday.

2026-11-26-18.headline: Cogent wins early FDA approval for Ekitna, the first new treatment in years for a rare stomach cancer after first-line therapy
2026-11-26-18.soWhat: A small biotech's first approval turns it from a research company into a seller, and launching on time is what investors watch next. Rare cancers with few options can support high prices and quick uptake through specialist doctors, and orphan drug status gives seven years of US market exclusivity. If the mastocytosis approvals follow, one molecule covers several markets, which spreads the cost of building a sales team. The open question is how fast oncologists switch patients who would otherwise get sunitinib alone.

sources.title: Cogent Biosciences: FDA approval and launch of EKITNA
AJMC: FDA approves bezuclastinib plus sunitinib for GIST

2026-11-26-18.summary: The FDA approved Cogent Biosciences' Ekitna (bezuclastinib), taken with the older drug sunitinib, for adults with advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) that have already been treated with imatinib. The decision came on November 24, ahead of the November 30 target date, under the FDA's real-time oncology review. In the 413-patient PEAK trial, the combination produced median progression-free survival of 16.5 months and a 46% response rate. Cogent has two more decisions ahead for the drug in systemic mastocytosis, including one due on December 30.

2026-11-26-19.headline: Fisher & Paykel Healthcare's profit jumps 37% on hospital demand and it raises its full-year outlook
2026-11-26-19.soWhat: Fisher & Paykel follows a razor-and-blades model: hospitals buy a device once and then keep buying the disposable tubes and masks used with each patient. As more hospitals adopt high-flow therapy outside intensive care, the consumable sales recur and earn high margins, which is why profit grew more than twice as fast as revenue. Competing device makers face a large installed base that is costly for hospitals to switch away from. The open question is whether hospitals keep adopting high-flow therapy at this pace through the second half.

sources.title: RNZ: Hospital growth powers Fisher & Paykel Healthcare profit higher
Capital Brief: Fisher & Paykel Healthcare lifts full-year guidance

2026-11-26-19.summary: New Zealand's Fisher & Paykel Healthcare, which makes breathing-support devices, reported first-half net profit of NZ$291.4 million, up 37%, on revenue up 15% to NZ$1.25 billion. Hospital products, mostly high-flow nasal oxygen systems and the single-use parts that go with them, grew 22% to NZ$841.5 million. The company raised its full-year profit forecast to NZ$565 million to NZ$605 million from NZ$525 million to NZ$565 million. It lifted its interim dividend to 26 cents a share from 19 cents.

2026-11-26-20.headline: Wholesale turkey prices hit a record $1.76 a pound, up 30%, even as production recovers from bird flu
2026-11-26-20.soWhat: Rebuilding flocks after disease takes time, and processing plants need workers, so supply recovers more slowly than demand. Grocers absorb part of the wholesale rise because a cheap holiday turkey brings shoppers who buy higher-margin items. Farmers see little of the higher price, since feed, fuel and labor costs rose too, so processors and grocers hold most of the pricing power. The open question is whether proposed changes to temporary worker visas ease the labor shortage before next year's season.

sources.title: KFGO: Turkey production bounces back but prices still rise
PBS NewsHour: Americans will pay more for Thanksgiving dinners this year

2026-11-26-20.summary: The USDA projects the wholesale price of whole hen turkeys at a record $1.76 a pound this year, up from $1.36 last year and 94 cents in 2024. US turkey production rose for the first time in several years to 5.1 billion pounds, up from 4.8 billion, but remains below the 5.7 billion of 2020 after years of avian disease. Retail prices rose about 10%, less than wholesale, as grocers used turkeys as discounted traffic builders, some as low as 69 cents a pound. Producers blame labor shortages for processing bottlenecks, while diesel near $5.81 a gallon and high fertilizer costs squeeze farm budgets.
